title: Kyle Shanahan feels better, will coach preseason opener
summary: The 49ers' coach is making progress in his recovery from a car accident.
full_text: '' Nearly a month after he was in a serious car accident, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan says he is mostly recovered and will coach the team's preseason opener against the Titans on Thursday. "I'm doing real good. My body feels good. I've just got to get this annoying cast off," Shanahan said, gesturing at his left hand. "My ribs feel good, except when I sneeze. And my head feels so much better. Concussions do linger a little bit, the only things I deal with now are headaches and fatigue. That's why I'm not always on the exact same routine but pretty close." Although Shanahan has delegated some head-coaching duties to assistant head coach Chris Foerster, he said he is watching many hours of tape and feels like he's doing most of the things he would ordinarily be doing at this time of year. "As far as the important stuff, I feel it's about 100 percent," Shanahan said. "I haven't missed anything of film. I watch every single play with the coaches, with the players." Shanahan said that at first the concussion he suffered in the accident was making him sensitive to noise, to the point that the music playing during practice would bother him. But he now says he's fully prepared for all the noise of an NFL game, and fully ready to get back to work.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Drew Brees recalls how he and LaDainian Tomlinson "grew up together" on the Chargers
summary: Brees made a special mention of his former teammate during his Hall of Fame induction speech.
full_text: As he was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame on Saturday, Drew Brees was remembered mostly for his time on the Saints. But in his induction speech, Brees spoke fondly about his time with the Chargers, and particularly about one of his Hall of Fame teammates. LaDainian Tomlinson and Brees first met in high school, spent time together as Heisman Trophy finalists in college and were the Chargers' first- and second-round picks in the 2001 NFL draft. Brees made special mention of how much Tomlinson meant to him. "What made it even sweeter is I was joining the guy they drafted in the first round, Hall of Famer and one of the greatest running backs in history, LaDainian Tomlinson," Brees said of getting drafted. "Not many people know this: LT and I grew up two hours from each other and played on the South Texas All-Star team together in 1997. We found our way back together four years later as Heisman Trophy finalists. At the Heisman presentation we both made the statement: 'Wouldn't it be something if we ended up on the same team?' LT, I always felt a strong kinship with you. We had so much in common. Drafted the same year, married the same year, won the Walter Payton Man of the Year the same year. We grew up together quickly in this league. I credit so many things in my career to the five years I spent with the Chargers." After Brees' fifth season, the Chargers decided to let him leave for New Orleans in free agency. The loud contingent of Saints fans in Canton, Ohio, this weekend are glad it worked out that way, and so is Brees. But Brees is also grateful for his time in San Diego, and for having Tomlinson as a teammate.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Ty Simpson will play in the preseason; no decision has been made about Stetson Bennett playing
summary: As the Rams prepare for the first of their three preseason games, coach Sean McVay has made a decision as to whether one of his top backup quarterbacks will play.
full_text: As the Rams prepare for the first of their three preseason games, coach Sean McVay has made a decision as to whether one of his top backup quarterbacks will play. As to the other, McVay has not. McVay told reporters on Saturday that rookie first-rounder Ty Simpson "definitely" will play. As to veteran Stetson Bennett, McVay said this: “I haven't decided on Stetson yet." If Bennett doesn't play, the 12 quarters of preseason reps will be handled by Simpson and Matthew Caldwell, an undrafted rookie who finished his college career at Texas. Bennett, 28, was a fourth-round pick in the 2023 draft. He has yet to make a regular-season appearance for the Rams. Eventually, McVay will have to decide whether Simpson or Bennett (or, in theory, Caldwell) will serve as the No. 2 quarterback behind 2025 NFL MVP Matthew Stafford. The decision surely will be influenced by Simpson's performance in the preseason. Depending on how things go, the Rams may need to revisit the possibility of persuading Jimmy Garoppolo, who is open to playing in 2026 , to serve as Stafford's understudy for a third straight season. McVay may not know for sure until after the third preseason game.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kyle Shanahan has no concern about Nick Bosa's missed practice time for soreness
summary: 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa, who missed most of last season with a torn ACL, has been absent from practice recently due to soreness.
full_text: '' 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa, who missed most of last season with a torn ACL, has been absent from practice recently due to soreness. In coach Kyle Shanahan's first training-camp press conference, he was asked whether the situation causes any concern. “No," Shanahan said. "He was doing great, and then he got sore just going through some of the individual. You wish that didn't happen, but no, there's no concern to where something's happened that is a big setback or anything. We'll wait until the soreness goes away and evaluate why the soreness has happened, but I still feel pretty good about that.” Saying there hasn't been a "big setback" opens the door for the possibility of a non-big setback. And the evaluation regarding the cause(s) of the soreness could lead to a conclusion that there's something deeper causing it. It's just the latest complication for a 49ers team that has had more than a few injury issues since camp opened. Which has to be a concern, given that the situation likely won't get any better once the games start to be played.
author: Mike Florio

title: Aaron Rodgers says Mike Tomlin helped restore his love for the game
summary: Aaron Rodgers loves football.
full_text: Aaron Rodgers loves football. Before last season, he didn't love it as much as he once did. His experience with Mike Tomlin helped rekindle it. In a Saturday interview with SiriusXM NFL Radio, Pat Kirwan asked how he can walk away from a game he loves. " I do love it, yeah ," Rodgers said. "I'm also 42. I've played 22 years. I played three in college. I've never had a fall to myself. I want to start a family with my wife, you know? I think you just have to know when it's time. "And, you know, there's been times in the last three offseasons where I felt like maybe it is time. But doors open, and I just tried to listen to the signs. I might have been listening to the wrong signs by going to New York, but it was a good learning experience, you know, and I learned a lot during that process, and I am thankful for that time there. "And I'm thankful for last year with Coach Tomlin, because he helped me get that love back, that deep love back for the game. That, you know, tearing my Achilles and going through a year of rehab, and just never feeling like myself, it just kind of beats you up a little bit, and I didn't want that to be my ending in the game that I love so much, and Mike and being around the guys, got me that love back, and I was content in walking away. And then they hired Mike McCarthy, and I was like, 'Okay, maybe we need a full circle here, me and Mike need a full circle here." Whether Rodgers believes it was a good idea will depend largely on how his last season goes. Which will depend on whether McCarthy can match or beat last year's 10-7 season that resulted in an AFC North crown and another one-and-done postseason run.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jamal Adams switches from No. 54 to No. 32
summary: When veteran defender Jamal Adams joined the Vikings, the team assigned him a traditional linebacker number: 54.
full_text: When veteran defender Jamal Adams joined the Vikings, the team assigned him a traditional linebacker number: 54. He recently switched to 32. And while he's still officially listed in the team's online roster as a linebacker, the change means Adams will be playing plenty of safety — his original NFL position. Adams anticipates being deployed at both positions. "I was telling some people inside the training room, just to have somebody believe in me again, and to know I can go back there and play the safety position, it feels great," Adams said, via Lindsey Young of Vikings.com. "I can kind of do it all in the back end. I just want to be versatile and do anything I can to help the team. "The key is winning. So whatever they need me to do, I'm going to do. That's what I'm here for." Adams reiterated prior comments regarding the long road back to full health after tearing a quad tendon in Week 1 of the 2022 season. "When I got hurt in '22, and then . . . those two or three years, I felt like I lost a little bit off my career," Adams said. "So for me, it's like a rebirth. There was a lot of adversity I went through, and I knew eventually I was going to make it out of that hole, but it was going to take time — and it took longer than I expected. But mentally and physically, I had to rebrand myself, be better on and off the field as far as my mentals and how I approached the game. "I have a different perspective. It's a different perspective on not only football but just life. Just being grateful and being happy where I am. Being where my feet are and just embracing the opportunity." Adams's versatility fits perfectly with the Brian Flores defense, which uses chaos and unpredictability to rattle nerves and create mismatches. Adams could end up being a key piece of the Minnesota attack.
author: Mike Florio

title: Laremy Tunsil suffered torn triceps on Saturday
summary: Tunsil is expected to miss significant regular-season time.
full_text: The Commanders are dealing with a significant blow to their offensive line. According to Mike Garafolo and Steve Wyche of NFL Network, left tackle Laremy Tunsil suffered a torn triceps during Saturday’s practice. He is likely to require surgery and is now set to miss at least a significant portion of the regular season. Tunsil, 32, suffered the injury during one-on-one drills. A five-time Pro Bowler, Tunsil has been with the Commanders since last March, when Houston traded him to Washington. In March, Tunsil signed a two-year contract extension to keep him with the club. He started 14 games for the Commanders last year. In all, he’s started 139 career games for Miami, Houston, and Washington since entering the league as a first-round pick in 2016.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Report: Panthers are expected to sign QB Kyle Trask
summary: Panthers quarterback Haynes King injured his hamstring in the Hall of Fame Game this week and they are set to add another quarterback to the roster for the coming practice week.
full_text: Panthers quarterback Haynes King injured his hamstring in the Hall of Fame Game this week and they are set to add another quarterback to the roster for the coming practice week. Mike Kaye of the Charlotte Observer reports that they will sign Kyle Trask. Trask recently worked out for the team. Trask played for the Buccaneers when Panthers head coach Dave Canales was the offensive coordinator in Tampa. He spent four seasons with the Bucs before being released last year and spent some time on Atlanta's practice squad later in the year. Joe Person of TheAthletic.com reports that King is considered week-to-week as a result of the hamstring injury.
author: Josh Alper

title: Broncos put DL Matt Henningsen on IR, release DB Sam Webb
summary: Broncos defensive lineman Matt Henningsen tore his Achilles at practice this week and the team officially brought his season to an end on Saturday.
full_text: Broncos defensive lineman Matt Henningsen tore his Achilles at practice this week and the team officially brought his season to an end on Saturday. Henningsen was placed on injured reserve as part of a flurry of roster moves. They also released defensive back Sam Webb while signing defensive back Ricardo Hallman and wide receiver Kyrese Rowan. It's the second straight year that Henningsen has torn his Achilles in August. He played in 34 games for the Broncos over the 2022 and 2023 seasons, but spent all of 2024 on the practice squad. Hallman started his final 38 games at Wisconsin before going undrafted this year. Rowan spent time on Denver's practice squad last season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bears sign defensive backs Brandon Hill and William Wright
summary: The Bears continued to shuffle their defensive backfield on Saturday.
full_text: The Bears continued to shuffle their defensive backfield on Saturday. They announced the signing of defensive backs Brandon Hill and William Wright. They also signed Xavier Woods on Friday. Hill played in two games for the Texans after being drafted in the seventh round in 2023 and returned to Houston's practice squad last season. He also spent time with the Raiders in 2025. Wright was undrafted out of Tennessee this year and he spent time with the Broncos earlier in the offseason. The Bears waived defensive backs K.C. Eziomume and Gervarrius Owens in corresponding moves. Both players were cut with injury designations and will revert to injured reserve if they go unclaimed.
author: Josh Alper

title: Texans sign RB Owen Wright
summary: The Texans brought a new player into their backfield mix on Saturday.
full_text: The Texans brought a new player into their backfield mix on Saturday. The team announced the signing of running back Owen Wright to their 90-man roster. Punter Jack Stonehouse was waived in a corresponding move. Wright signed with the Ravens after going undrafted in 2023 and played in one game for Baltimore during his rookie season. He spent 2024 on injured reserve and played in three games for the Bucs last season. Wright ran three times for six yards while with Tampa and also returned three kickoffs. He was waived in May. Stonehouse went undrafted in April and signed with the Texans in May. His departure leaves Kai Kroeger as the only punter on the roster in Houston.
author: Josh Alper

title: Seahawks sign RB Justin Jones
summary: The Seahawks announced a pair of roster moves on Saturday.
full_text: '' The Seahawks announced a pair of roster moves on Saturday. They signed running back Justin Jones to the active roster. Linebacker Power Echols was waived in a corresponding move. Echols signed with the team on Friday, so it was a very brief stint in Seattle for him. Jones took part in the Seahawks' rookie minicamp earlier this offseason. He did not get the ball much while at Auburn, but was a regular on special teams and blocked a punt against Arkansas last season. The Seahawks also signed running back T.J. Harden this week. Rookie Jardarian Price is atop the depth chart with Zach Charbonnet still working his way back from a torn ACL.
author: Josh Alper

title: Kyle Shanahan says his Tesla was on autopilot before accident
summary: Shanahan said he doesn't know whether it malfunctioned or he accidentally turned it off.
full_text: Four weeks to the day after being involved in a car accident, 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan had a formal press conference for the first time during 2026 training camp. Previously, he'd met with reporters in his office and clarified that the accident, which happened while he was operating his Tesla, was his fault. On Saturday, speaking for nearly 20 minutes, Shanahan was asked if he's mad at himself for causing the accident. "I mean, anytime you cause an accident that could be avoided, you’d feel pretty stupid ," Shanahan said. "I mean, especially when you have a chance to hurt someone else. And so, like, I think you'd get mad when you get a ticket, at yourself. So it was kind of the same. You know, things that, you know, I think everyone's done to a degree what I've done. But, you know, dropping a phone and falling all the way to my back seat where I have to fully take my eyes off the road. You know, it's something that I normally wouldn't do. "I've had autopilot for nine years, so I'm pretty comfortable with it and, you know, who knows what happened when I turned around? Whether it malfunctioned or whether I knocked it off? That's something I don't know yet. But regardless, that's — it is always your fault, whether you're on autopilot or not. You can't take your eyes off the road. It's a partnership driving, you don't just turn it over to a computer, and it's a good lesson, no matter how comfortable I am with that, that I believe someday could save my life or someone else's, or it's really helped me have perspective on that stuff." He also was asked whether he spoke to his players about the lessons he learned. "I mean, I didn't, like, sit there and feel like I had to — I didn't have, like, a ton of guilt over it or anything," Shanahan said. Like, I think, you know, the word's an 'accident,' and it truly was that way. But you realize how quick and close that stuff can happen. And, you know, when, you know, when you're going at 20 miles an hour, you're not really — and you're on autopilot — I obviously have zero worries. I have so much trust in that stuff. And that was a good lesson that you can't ever have zero worries. But I think it definitely could be example for a lot of people." Shanahan also said that he's feeling good, and that his head " feels so much better ." He added that he's still dealing with "headaches and fatigue." He also said he'll coach the team in the preseason opener against the Titans. The biggest new detail from the press conference, as it relates to the accident, is that the car was driving itself when the accident happened. The next question to be answered is whether, as Shanahan said, it malfunctioned or he accidentally disengaged it when he turned to retrieve his phone after it fell from his lap.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cardinals put S Joey Blount, TE Kenny Yeboah on injured reserve
summary: The Cardinals placed a couple of players on injured reserve on Saturday.
full_text: ''' The Cardinals placed a couple of players on injured reserve on Saturday. Safety Joey Blount and tight end Kenny Yeboah both landed on the list. Neither player will be eligible to be activated during the regular season, although they could play this year if they are released with an injury settlement at some point in the future. Blount was injured during practice this week. He suffered a season-ending neck injury in Week 1 of the 2025 season, so it's back-to-back bad breaks for Blount. Yeboah's hamstring injury occurred in the Hall of Fame Game on Thursday night. He signed with the Cardinals in June and last saw regular season action with the Jets in 2024.
author: Josh Alper

title: Browns change plans Saturday, give Deshaun Watson unexpected first-team reps
summary: The Browns have been rotating quarterbacks Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders with the first team from day to day at training camp, so any deviation from that schedule is sure to grab attention.
full_text: The Browns have been rotating quarterbacks Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders with the first team from day to day at training camp, so any deviation from that schedule is sure to grab attention. Such a deviation came on Saturday. Head coach Todd Monken said before practice that it would be Sanders working with the first team, but multiple reporters shared that Watson received all of the work with the first team. Monken did not speak to the media after practice. A team spokesman said, via multiple reporters, that Monken changed the plans because he wanted to see Watson with certain personnel groups. Earlier this week, Monken clarified a report that both quarterbacks will get a start in the preseason by saying that "if it’s still a competition at that time, why wouldn’t you start one and start the other" without targeting any date for the competition to end. The Browns play their first preseason game next Saturday, so the identity of the first guy up as the starter should come early in the week.
author: Josh Alper

title: Luther Burden limped to locker room during Bears practice
summary: Bears wide receiver Luther Burden had to make an early exit from Saturday's practice at training camp.
full_text: Bears wide receiver Luther Burden had to make an early exit from Saturday's practice at training camp. Per multiple reports, Burden limped to the locker room after trying to catch a pass over cornerback Tyrique Stevenson during a drill. Stevenson also stayed down for a time, but was able to return to practice. The team has not shared any update on his condition at this point. Reports indicating that Burden appeared to hurt his left leg. The 2025 second-round pick is expected to take on a larger role in the offense this season, so the Bears will be hoping that any missed time for Burden is brief.
author: Josh Alper

title: Aaron Glenn: David Bailey "fine" after hurting ankle Saturday
summary: Linebacker David Bailey gave the Jets a scare at Sautrday's practice, but it was only a momentary one.
full_text: Linebacker David Bailey gave the Jets a scare at Sautrday's practice, but it was only a momentary one. The first-round pick limped off after hurting his ankle during drills and remained on the sideline for the rest of the session. Head coach Aaron Glenn said at a press conference that Bailey's injury is a minor one. “He got up after the ankle,” Glenn said. “He’ll be fine.” The Jets have joint practices with the Buccaneers on Tuesday and Wednesday. Glenn did not say whether Bailey will take part in those sessions during the press conference and left his status as day-to-day. Safety VJ Payne won't be on the field for that work. Glenn said the seventh-round pick will miss three or four weeks with a bone bruise.
author: Josh Alper

title: Patrick Mahomes says his left knee "feels great"
summary: Two weeks into 2026 training camp, Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes is moving closer to being ready to go five weeks from Monday night.
full_text: ''' Two weeks into 2026 training camp, Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes is moving closer to being ready to go five weeks from Monday night. He continues to recover from a December 14 tear of the ACL and LCL in his left knee. " It feels great ," Mahomes said Friday, via Nate Taylor of ESPN. "When you're tired sometimes, you don't even think about [the knee]. I'm trying to protect it, but at the same time trying to push it and get myself ready to go for the season." He's balancing getting himself ready with keeping his knee healthy. "I try to be smart, but there's just sometimes where, in camp, you're trying to compete and practices are long," Mahomes said. "I mean, you want to win the rep. There's times where I do forget about it and just play football." That happened on Friday, during a fourth down in 11-on-11 drills. He scrambled toward the right sideline before cutting back and throwing an underhand lateral that became a fumble recovered by the defense. "I'm trying to hold myself back because I'm just a competitor," Mahomes said. "I like competing. All of a sudden, I'm running and cutting back and trying to pitch the ball. But when it's fourth down, you want to try to make a play happen. "I'm not going to lose who I am, but I'm going to try to keep myself smart and keep myself in position to be out there for my teammates." The biggest question when Week 1 rolls around is whether Mahomes will be able to play like he always has. Far from a classic pocket quarterback, Mahomes runs left and right and left and right and buys time before firing a pass to an open receiver. Those movements and cuts will put stress on the knee. Having running back Kenneth Walker III on the team may result in more running plays for the Chiefs' offense. Still, when it's time to pass, Mahomes will apparently forget about the knee and focus on the sticks.
author: Mike Florio

title: Drew Brees' Hall of Fame speech focused on Sean Payton, city of New Orleans
summary: Brees signed with the Saints in 2006 as New Orleans was healing from Hurricane Katrina.
full_text: '' The day he retired, Drew Brees had to know he would be on this stage, on this day in Canton. He finished his 20-year career with 80,358 passing yards and 571 passing touchdowns, both second all time. He went to 13 Pro Bowls and won two NFL Offensive Player of the Year awards. He won Super Bowl XLIV and earned Super Bowl MVP honors. Brees, 47, was a no-brainer, first-ballot Hall of Famer, so as expected, he was the last of five inductees to make his speech Saturday. Brees made his 10 minutes last, turning his speech time limit into 25 minutes. "I don’t take for granted that I got to play the most coveted position in all of sports," Brees said. "From as far back as I can remember, I wanted to play quarterback. I never saw the position as one of pressure, but rather one of great responsibility. . . . The quarterback is the distributor of hope and confidence. A master of probability. The ultimate problem solver. I’ve always seen the game of football and the quarterback position as a true art form like a song or a dance." He spent the bulk of his speech on thanking the city of New Orleans and coach Sean Payton. Brees began his career as a second-round pick of the Chargers in 2001, but he became Drew Brees in his 15 seasons with the Saints. Brees' severe shoulder injury in 2005 cast doubt on his career and sent him into free agency as damaged goods, with the Dolphins failing him on his physical. Payton wanted Brees, embraced Brees, welcomed Brees and turned Brees into a Hall of Fame quarterback. "Coach, you were brilliant," Brees said. "I saw myself as an extension of you on that field. I always had something to prove to you, and I always wanted to make you right. And I know you trusted me, and that allowed us both to be great." Brees helped New Orleans heal from Hurricane Katrina, and the city of New Orleans and the Saints helped Brees heal his career. "It doesn’t take you long to realize what makes New Orleans so special," Brees said. "New Orleans has been through a lot to the point where in some cases the feeling was we may have lost everything. It may never come back the same. Storms teach us that our greatest treasures aren’t the things we own. They’re the people we love, and the way we show up for one another. It reminds us to hold our loved ones a little closer, to love a little harder, to laugh a little louder, and to never take a single day for granted. Sometimes it takes losing what can be replaced to truly appreciate the things that can’t. "New Orleans, you accepted me; you embraced me; you believed in me but more importantly, you trusted me with the soul of the city and I would have died to protect that calling," Brees said. "The greatest teams in the history of sports are the ones who accept the responsibility of being a true representation of their city/country/community. I speak for all my Saints teammates when I say that's what we were inspired to be every day for you. If you love New Orleans, it will love you back. There is no truer statement. "The Who Dat Nation, there are a few events in your life where you remember exactly where you were when it occurred. For Saints fans, it is the Steve Gleason blocked punt on Monday Night Football, reopening of the Dome September 25, 2006, and when the Saints won Super Bowl XLIV. It was your spirit that allowed us to be special, smell greatness and finish strong."
author: Charean Williams

title: Roger Craig reveals dementia diagnosis in his Hall of Fame speech: This diagnosis doesn't define me
summary: The 66-year-old former 49ers running back said in his 10-minute speech he hopes telling his story can help someone else.
full_text: Roger Craig earned his place in Canton on Saturday. He doubted it would ever come, having waited 28 years since he became eligible. "You spend your whole life trying to prove you belong, and then one day, you're told you're one of the all-time greats," Craig said. "Man, it's overwhelming. I think about that kid from Davenport who loved football. I think about the journey more than anything — the early mornings, the doubts, the sacrifices. It all led here." The 49ers selected Craig in the second round in 1983, and he became an integral part of their dynasty of the 1980s, winning three Super Bowl rings. Craig was the first player ever to have 1,000 yards rushing and 1,000 yards receiving in the same season, which came in 1985, and he led the NFL with 2,036 yards from scrimmage in 1988. "[49ers coach Bill Walsh] didn't just want a running back. He wanted a complete football player," Craig said. "He trusted me to do whatever the team needed. That's why the 1,000 yards rushing, 1,000 yards receiving season means to much to me. We weren't chasing numbers. We were chasing W's — wins. I didn't realize I was making history. It just felt like we were doing something special as a team. Looking back, I appreciate how difficult it is, and how few players have done it since." Craig, 66, taped his 10-minute speech, revealing at the end that he has been diagnosed with vascular dementia. "My doctors believe may be related, at least in part, to the concussions I experienced during my career," Craig said. "The changes were gradual. At first, they were easy to dismiss as normal aging. Over time, my family noticed it too and ultimately led us to seek answers from my doctor. Two things can be true: Football gave me opportunities beyond anything I could imagine. It helped shape the man I became. At the same time, we know more today about brain health than when I played, and I hope sharing my story encourages people to pay attention to their health and seek help when something doesn't feel right. I want people to know this diagnosis doesn't define me. I am still Roger Craig. I am still a father, a husband, a teammate, a friend and someone who loves this game and the people who brought it to my life. If sharing my story helps even one family or one former player, then it's worth it. Football gave me everything."
author: Charean Williams

title: Adam Vinatieri pokes fun at Bill Belichick in Hall of Fame speech
summary: Former Patriots and Colts kicker Adam Vinatieri entered the Hall of Fame on the same day that former Patriots and Browns coach Bill Belichick should have been getting his own bronze bust.
full_text: Former Patriots and Colts kicker Adam Vinatieri entered the Hall of Fame on the same day that former Patriots and Browns coach Bill Belichick should have been getting his own bronze bust. Belichick wasn't present for Saturday's enshrinement ceremony. But Vinatieri mentioned the coach in his speech. "I thought it was because training camp had already started," Vinatieri said regarding Belichick's absence, "but in truth it's because he is judging his girlfriend's cheerleading competition." Vinatieri followed the jab with a bouquet: "All jokes aside, in my opinion Bill is the greatest coach of all time." It's the second straight Hall of Fame weekend that included an honoree taking a shot at Belichick's May/next-December romance. In 2025, Bill Nunn award recipient Mary Kay Cabot, in reflecting on his skirmishes with Belichick when he coached the Browns, said this: “Now I totally understand why Bill gave me such a hard time,” Cabot said. “I was 28 at the time and he just couldn’t relate to a woman that old .” Next year, Belichick should get his chance to take a few shots when he finally gets his opportunity to give an acceptance speech.
author: Mike Florio

title: Protect College Sports Act fails to pass Senate before recess
summary: The Protect College Sports Act has lost the latest game of beat the clock.
full_text: '' The Protect College Sports Act has lost the latest game of beat the clock. Via Ross Dellenger of Yahoo Sports, the Senate adjourned for a five-week recess on Saturday morning without voting on the bill that would reshape college sports. At a time when the proposed legislation had been building momentum, the hiatus could be fatal to the effort to turn the bill into law before the midterm elections. The question becomes whether the NCAA and the power conferences will wait to see what happens, or whether they will move on to another potential solution. One possibility includes individual conferences leaving the NCAA. If/when the Protect College Sports Act passes the Senate, it would go to the House. And it's not an automatic that it would pass the House as drafted. A compromise bill could be required, with the first Tuesday in November serving as the practical drop-dead date for getting something done. Through it all, those who created the current chaos through decades of antitrust violations will look for a way to restore partial order. While college football continues to generate significant ratings and earn plenty of money. The fundamental problem continues to be that the players, in the opinion of the schools, are now getting too much of the revenue. And that's money that used to go only to the schools. This is what's driving the exhausting insistence that the sky is falling. The absence of a federal law that allows the schools to pick the pockets of the players implicitly represents the reality that more than enough legislators can see through the grift. Consider this comment from the Congressional Black Caucus, which issued a statement opposing the bill on Thursday: “Black athletes have transformed college athletics into one of the most successful enterprises in America. Yet the people most affected by this legislation have not been meaningfully included in shaping it." Indeed they haven't. The effort is being crafted by those who long for the days when the players didn't get paid anything. While it will be impossible to put the toothpaste back in the tube completely, the folks who run college sports hope to gather as much of it as they can.
author: Mike Florio

title: Luke Kuechly: There's no way to measure what the game of football has given me
summary: Luke Kuechly, at 35, became the second-youngest Pro Football Hall of Fame inductee ever on Saturday.
full_text: Luke Kuechly, at 35, became the second-youngest Pro Football Hall of Fame inductee ever on Saturday. Only Gale Sayers, who was enshrined in 1977 at 34, was younger. Kuechly earned a bust in Canton in his second year of eligibility after playing only eight seasons. His 14-minute speech remembered those who helped get him to Canton and the life lessons football taught him. "This game teaches you a lot if you're willing to observe and listen," Kuechly said. "It's taught me resilience, consistency, toughness, the value of communication, how to find common ground, and most importantly, how to enjoy it along the way, because often times the best moments are the ones you are in. Ron Rivera used to beat that into our head and say, 'Be where your feet are.' Well, he didn't just mean be where your feet are when you're at the Super Bowl, playing with and against incredible players. He meant, be where your feet are all the time , and that's been great advice. "The joy football gave me didn't come from any particular win. It came from competing, from studying, from practicing and from preparing, and joy came from the people I was with. I think about the bus rides, the plane flights, being with each other at Wofford College during training camp. You’ve never seen guys so happy to have a night off and eat pizza with their buddies. "The relationships formed through football are unique. You see each other at your best and at your worst. You spend long days together in meeting rooms. You learn how different people communicate, lead and overcome challenges. And over time, teammates become friends, and friends become family. That's why, when people ask me what I miss most about football, it's not one specific game or one specific play. It's the locker room. It's conversations that have nothing to do with sports. It's celebrating together after wins, and hurting together after losses. "There's no way to measure what the game of football has given to me, the joy it's provided, and, more than anything, the people that I have been so blessed to be around as a result of this game." Kuechly became the third Panthers legend in five years to be inducted into the Hall, joining Sam Mills and Julius Peppers. Despite his short career, Kuechly made 1,092 tackles, more than 100 tackles in all eight seasons. He was the league's Defensive Rookie of the Year in 2012, a Defensive Player of the Year in 2013 and part of the All-Decade Team of the 2010s. "I've been incredibly fortunate to have been touched by the game of football," Kuechly said in wrapping up his speech. "Football has given me so much more than I could have ever imagined. The people I've met, the experiences we've shared and the joy I've found through this game will stay with me for the rest of my life. Your love and support have meant more than you'll ever know. So thank you to everyone who has been part of this journey. Thank you for sharing today with me. And Keep Pounding."
author: Charean Williams

title: Zay Flowers day-to-day with a quad contusion
summary: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter gave an update on wide receiver Zay Flowers after Flowers left Saturday's practice early.
full_text: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter gave an update on wide receiver Zay Flowers after Flowers left Saturday's practice early. Minter said, via multiple reporters, that Flowers suffered a quad contusion when he collided with defensive back Jaylinn Hawkins during the workout. Minter called Flowers day-to-day and said that he does not expect the wideout to miss a significant amount of time. The injury added to an eventful week for Flowers. He signed a four-year, $140 million extension with the team on Wednesday. The Ravens will have another padded practice on Sunday and they will host the Eagles in their first preseason game next Saturday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Laremy Tunsil to be evaluated after leaving Saturday's practice
summary: The Commanders are waiting for word on left tackle Laremy Tunsil's condition after he picked up an injury on Saturday.
full_text: The Commanders are waiting for word on left tackle Laremy Tunsil's condition after he picked up an injury on Saturday. Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports that Tunsil will be evaluated and tested after leaving the training camp practice early. Garafolo adds that the team does not appear to be overly concerned, but that it would not be surprising if Tunsil missed some time. There's been no specific word on his injury, but, per the report, that it appeared to be in the area of his shoulder and neck. The injury occurred during a 1-on-1 drill with linebacker Odafe Oweh. Reporters at the practice also noted cornerback Trey Amos departed early. Amos was activated from the physically unable to perform list on Friday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Adam Vinatieri: I can officially say my biggest dream has come true
summary: Despite his success, Adam Vinatieri was uncertain whether it was enough to get him in the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
full_text: Despite his success, Adam Vinatieri was uncertain whether it was enough to get him in the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Kickers don't always get their due, and if they do, it's usually a long wait. In his second year of eligibility, though, Vinatieri earned his day in the sun. He was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame on Saturday, joining Jan Stenerud and Morten Andersen as the only pure kickers with busts in Canton. "So here I stand at the top of the mountain. The pinnacle of greatness. The highest achievement in my professional career. I can officially say my biggest dream has come true," Vinatieri said. "As I look out into this crowd, I don't just see Hall of Famers, teammates, coaches, friends, and family. I see every person who believed in me, challenged me, sacrificed for me, and played a role in turning my childhood dream into this unforgettable moment. "This honor is one that I accept with tremendous gratitude and humility, because I know no one reaches this stage alone. Today is not just about me. Today is about family. It’s about teammates. It’s about coaches. It’s about organizations that believed in me. And it’s about every person who played a role in this incredible journey." Vinatieri, 53, played 24 seasons, 10 with the Patriots (1996-2005) and 14 with the Colts (2006-19). He became the NFL's all-time leading scorer with 2,673 points and has the most regular-season field goals with 599. He connected on an NFL-record 44 consecutive field goals between the 2015 and 2016 seasons with the Colts, and no player had more seasons with 100 or more points scored than Vinatieri (21). He earned his reputation as the NFL's greatest clutch kicker in the postseason, which included connecting on last-second game-winning field goals to clinch Super Bowl XXXVI and Super Bowl XXXVIII. in the 2006 playoffs, Vinatieri made 14 field goals as the Colts earned their first Indianapolis-era Lombardi Trophy. Vinatieri had a long list of those he thanked in a humorous speech that included jokes aimed at Bill Belichick, Tom Brady, Pat McAfee, Peyton Manning and Andersen. Vinatieri's speech, though, centered around "a kid from South Dakota who never gave up on his dreams," and he ended his almost 19-minute speech with a love letter to football. "Football, it would have been so easy to forget to tell you just how much you mean to me. If you were sitting here in this crowd today, this is what I would say," Vinatieri said. "I loved you with everything I had. There was a time when I thought I wanted you more than air, but I was wrong. You were the air. You gave me purpose. You gave me direction. You gave me a life I could have never imagined. "The beautiful thing about our relationship was that the more I gave to you, the more you gave back to me. The more I devoted myself to you, the more you rewarded me. The more I committed to you, the more you committed to me. I tried to honor you every single day because I knew you deserved nothing less than my very best. "I gave you 38 years of my life, and in return, you gave me a lifetime of memories. I gave you points; you gave me friendships. I gave you countless hours of work; you gave me the opportunity to travel the world, experience different cultures and meet extraordinary people. Every sacrifice became an investment, and somehow football, you always gave me back more than I put in. "Looking back, I realize I was never just playing football. We were building a life together. You challenged me, humbled me, disciplined me and ultimately shaped the man I became. Now, it feels like a parent letting go of a grown child. You raised me, prepared me and believed in me, and now you're telling me it's time for the next chapter. "For so many years, football, you were the mountain I chose to climb. Today, standing at the summit, I finally understand what the climb was really about. It was never just reaching the top. It was the view you gave me along the way — the people I love, the family I cherish, the friendships I've made, and a life richer than I ever dreamed possible. "So thank you, football. I gave you everything I had, and somehow, you gave me even more in return. Thank you for the life you gave me. I hope I honored you as much as you honored me."
author: Charean Williams

title: Raiders hold Kirk Cousins, Maxx Crosby out of Saturday's practice due to Friday's fight
summary: Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins and defensive end Maxx Crosby got into a scuffle during practice on Friday and they received some extra time to cool off on Saturday.
full_text: '' Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins and defensive end Maxx Crosby got into a scuffle during practice on Friday and they received some extra time to cool off on Saturday. Head coach Klint Kubiak told reporters that both players were held out of practice on Saturday because their fight violated team rules. Both players are expected to be back on the field on Monday. “We have very clear expectations on how we want to practice and how we want to go about our business, and we violated that yesterday," Kubiak said, via Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com. With Cousins out of practice, first overall pick Fernando Mendoza got an extended run with the first team offense during team drills.
author: Josh Alper

title: Larry Fitzgerald: It's not just about the excellence; it's about the people who help get you there
summary: After a 17-year career with the Cardinals, Fitzgerald entered the Hall of Fame on Saturday as a first-ballot inductee.
full_text: Larry Fitzgerald had a 17-season career in becoming one of the NFL's all-time best wide receivers, but his time in the NFL began long before that. Vikings coach Dennis Green, who was friends with Fitzgerald's father, Larry Fitzgerald Sr., hired Fitzgerald as a boy ball at 14 years old. "I grew up watching legends being built right in front of me," Fitzgerald said in a 14-minute speech. "Hall of Fame players like John Randle, Chris Doleman, Randall McDaniel and Warren Moon, who taught me what it means to demand more of yourself than anyone else ever would. Plus, they saw me. At 8 in the morning, before training camp practice, it was: 'What's up, Fitzy! Hey Little Fitz, can you grab me two wrist bands real quick.' "I was being acknowledged by the greats, and if I wanted to ask a question — at the right time — about a play, they would always answer. Without that experience, I'm not here." Here is the Pro Football Hall of Fame, where Fitzgerald became a first-ballot gold jacket player on Saturday. He got a bust in Canton after 17,492 career receiving yards, the second-most in NFL history behind Jerry Rice. His 1,432 career catches are also second all time while his 121 receiving touchdowns rank sixth. He was an 11-time Pro Bowl selection and made All-Pro in 2008. He did it with a team that didn't always have star quarterbacks, as 22 of them threw at least one pass to Fitzgerald. Cardinals owner Michael Bidwill's favorite stat to sum up Fitzgerald's career is that Fitzgerald had more career tackles (41) than dropped passes (29). Fitzgerald, like the more than 300 Hall of Famers before him, had a long list of those to thank. Cris Carter, Kurt Warner, Emmitt Smith and Randy Moss were among the former players he called by name. "If you were paying attention, you heard some fundamental themes in this speech," Fitzgerald said. "One, it's not hard to find people who will tell you what you want to hear. Make a conscious effort to surround yourself with people who will tell you what you need to hear. The hard things. The uncomfortable things. Believe me, the people in that second group care about you far more than those in the first. "Two, life is short. Time is precious. And not one of us knows how much we have. So many of the people I mentioned today are no longer with us. Some gone much too soon. Make your time count. Fill every 24 hours with the passions and pursuits that mean the most to you. "And lastly, there's not much traffic on the extra mile in life, so be sure to bring others along with you. I've talked about the people who supported, taught and inspired me. Copy their examples and remember: Don't just pursue excellence for yourself. Help other people pursue it, too. That's the part of this story that matters the most. Not the likes. Not the fame. But the people you travel with. The values you uphold. In the end, it's not just about the excellence. It's about the people who help get you there." Fitzgerald's father was instrumental in his success, and Fitzgerald honored him late in his speech. Fitzgerald Sr., who was widely known in the Twin Cities after 50 years as a sports reporter, died June 1 at the age of 71. "My dad, who I lost recently, is also here in spirit," Fitzgerald said. He was the solid foundation of our family, and the standard I measure myself against. Dad, looking back, I know there were times you must have felt like you were carrying the weight of the world. But you always showed up, and your love, your willingness to sacrifice, and your consistency have been the blueprint I use to raise your grandsons."
author: Charean Williams

title: Commanders sign offensive linemen Daniel Brunskill and Nicholas Petit-Frere
summary: The Commanders tripled down on veteran offensive line additions Saturday.
full_text: The Commanders tripled down on veteran offensive line additions Saturday. In addition to their previously reported signing of Max Scharping, the Commanders announced that they have signed Daniel Brunskill and Nicholas Petit-Frere. Brunskill has seen time at all three spots on the line while appearing in 117 games for the 49ers, Titans and Dolphins. He played in 16 games for the Dolphins last season and made five starts. Petit-Frere played tackle while with the Titans from 2022-2024. He started 28 of the 34 games he played for Tennessee and was Brunskill's teammate for his final two seasons with the team. The Commanders announced that they have placed defensive tackle D.J. Davidson on the reserve/retired list. They also waived wide receiver Chris Hilton Jr. and guard Timothy McKay in corresponding moves.
author: Josh Alper

title: Lane Johnson: This is probably my last year
summary: Johnson is heading into his 14th season with the Eagles.
full_text: ''' Eagles right tackle Lane Johnson returned to the team on Friday after several days away to deal with a personal matter and it won't be long before Johnson is out of the picture in Philadelphia entirely. Johnson said at a Saturday press conference that his mother has been dealing with some health issues and that he appreciates that the Eagles gave him time to deal with off-field matters during camp. Johnson said those off-field issues have gotten larger in recent years, which led him to consider retirement after the 2025 season and has him feeling like 2026 will be his last hurrah. "As you get older, things change in your life," Johnson said. "Priorities, your children get older, parents get older. It just puts things into perspective. I’m looking like it’s probably going to be my last year. Just cause I’m getting to that point —those priorities away from football are starting to merge. Not that I don’t enjoy — I love everything about this game and preparing for it. That’s kinda where I’m at in my career. Just looking forward to this year, playing the best I can and stay healthy. That’s about it." Johnson said that he plans on having "a really good last year" and the Eagles will try to send him out as a winner come the end of the season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Commanders' Laremy Tunsil diagnosed with torn triceps, reportedly will miss most of the 2026 season
summary: Tunsil suffered the injury during practice on Saturday
full_text:
The Washington Commanders were dealt a tough blow during Saturday's practice, as star left tackle Laremy Tunsil suffered a torn triceps, which will require surgery and force him to miss most, if not all, of the 2026 season, per ESPN .
Tunsil suffered the injury while attempting to stifle a bull rush from free-agent addition Odafe Oweh during one-on-one drills. Just five months ago, Washington made Tunsil the first $30 million-per-year offensive lineman , signing a two-year, $60.2 million extension that reset the left-tackle market. It marked the second time in his career that Tunsil became the highest-paid player at his position.
Tunsil was acquired by the Commanders from the Houston Texans via trade last offseason and started 14 games for Washington in 2025. A video of Tunsil's injury circulated around social media. It doesn't offer the clearest look at what happened, but you can see Tunsil grab at his arm while kneeling down after the rep:
Here’s the video of the Tunsil injury pic.twitter.com/cVus3xYMnU
Tunsil just turned 32 years old last Sunday and has long been viewed as one of the best left tackles in the NFL . The former No. 13 overall pick of the Miami Dolphins has made five Pro Bowls over 10 seasons and is viewed as the cornerstone of Jayden Daniels ' protection. PFF ranked Tunsil as the sixth-best offensive tackle in 2025 after he allowed 15 total pressures and two sacks.
This is a troubling development for the Commanders, who had their 2025 season derailed by injury. After going 12-5 in 2024 with an NFC Championship appearance, Washington went 5-12 when several key players were sidelined. On the offensive side alone, Daniels missed 10 games with multiple issues, including a dislocated elbow, star wideout Terry McLaurin had the worst season of his career after being forced to miss seven games due to a quad injury, and running back Austin Ekeler tore his Achilles in Week 2.
The Commanders will likely look in-house for their Tunsil replacement, and they do have a couple of options.
One is Brandon Coleman , the former third-round pick out of TCU in 2024, who began his NFL career at left tackle for Washington. The Commanders did make the NFC Championship with him blocking on the blind side, but Coleman was moved to left guard last year when Tunsil was acquired. Coleman ended up being benched for Chris Paul in Week 3, but did re-enter the starting lineup at left tackle when Tunsil was injured at the end of last season. In this training camp, Coleman was battling Paul for the starting left guard spot.
Another option is Andrew Wylie , who ESPN's Adam Schefter says is "likely" to be Washington's new left tackle. Wylie is entering his fourth season with the Commanders after spending 2017-22 with the Kansas City Chiefs . He started games at left guard, right guard and right tackle for Patrick Mahomes and won two Super Bowls.
While experienced, Wylie has never started at left tackle. He was Washington's starting right tackle in 2023 and 2024, but was replaced by No. 29 overall pick Josh Conerly Jr . in 2025. Wylie then moved inside to right guard and played 16 games with five starts.
The young Coleman and the veteran Wylie are likely Washington's top two options, but there are a couple of notable names still out there on the open market. Taylor Decker and Cam Robinson headline the slim pickings.
Decker requested his release from the Detroit Lions this offseason after the two sides could not "find common ground." The one-time Pro Bowler has 140 career starts to his name, but it's curious as to why he's still available. Would he play for a franchise other than the Lions, has he been actively searching for a new landing spot and what kind of shape is he in? It's worth mentioning that new Commanders offensive coordinator David Blough spent several seasons with the Lions as a backup quarterback. The two have some kind of a relationship.
As for Robinson, he began last season with the Texans before being traded to the Cleveland Browns four weeks into the season. Robinson started in 12 of 13 games played for the Browns, and has 114 career starts for four different franchises. He was a former No. 34 overall pick of the Jacksonville Jaguars back in 2017.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: 49ers' Kyle Shanahan says his car was on autopilot at the time of his recent accident
summary: Shanahan publicly addressed the accident for the first time on Saturday
full_text:
On Saturday, Kyle Shanahan took questions regarding his recent car accident for the first time since the San Francisco 49ers started training camp. The 49ers' coach said he is roughly at full strength and plans to coach in Thursday's preseason opener against the Tennessee Titans .
Shanahan suffered a multitude of injuries from the accident, which occurred on July 14. Among the injuries Shanahan sustained were a concussion, three broken ribs and a broken left hand. Shanahan has cut back on some aspects of his typical coaching duties as he tries to return to full strength.
"I try not to come in here every single day because I feel like, if I did, I wouldn't be able to pull off my normal routine, which is watching hours and hours of tape and getting to walk through the night being able to watch stuff after that," Shanahan said, via ESPN . "Eventually I will get there."
Late last month, Shanahan met privately with several reporters to clarify the circumstances of the crash. During that meeting, he stated that he crossed into oncoming traffic, not the 21-year-old driver of the other car.
On Saturday, Shanahan said he was using the autopilot feature in his Tesla Model S at the time of the accident and that it occurred after he dropped his phone and took his eyes off the road. Shanahan, who said he has been using autopilot in some form for 9 years and is "pretty comfortable" with the function, wasn't sure whether the accident was the result of a malfunction or whether he had inadvertently turned autopilot off while trying to retrieve his phone.
"Anytime you cause an accident that can be avoided, you feel pretty stupid, especially when you have a chance to hurt someone else," Shanahan said. "Who knows what happened when I turned around, whether [autopilot] malfunctioned or whether I knocked it off I don't know yet. But regardless, it's always your fault. Whether you're on autopilot or not, you can't take your eyes off the road. It's a partnership, driving, you don't just turn it over to a computer."
Shanahan, 46, is entering his 10th season as the 49ers' coach. Under his watch, the 49ers have compiled an 82-67 regular season record and a 9-5 record in the postseason. The 49ers won NFC titles in 2019 and in 2024. Both of those seasons ended with Super Bowl losses to the Kansas City Chiefs .
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Eagles RT Lane Johnson says 2026 will likely be his last in NFL
summary: The six-time Pro Bowler and two-time Super Bowl champion said he feels the pull of off-field responsibilities as he prepares for what could be his final NFL season
full_text:
One of the best offensive tackles in recent NFL history is likely to hang up his spikes after the 2026 season. Philadelphia Eagles right tackle Lane Johnson told reporters Saturday that the upcoming season will likely be his last in the NFL. Johnson missed a few practices in recent days for personal reasons and told reporters that he feels the pull of off-field responsibilities. Johnson also said he felt it was important to go public with his retirement plan, "to put [his] mind at ease," per the Philadelphia Inquirer .
"Looking like this is probably, potentially going to be, probably my last year, just because I had gotten to that point of those priorities away from football are starting to merge," Johnson said, according to The Athletic . "Not that I don't enjoy (it) — I love everything about this game and preparing for it — but that's where I'm at in my career. Looking forward to this year, playing the best I can, stay healthy, and that's about it."
Johnson is a 13-year veteran who has made six Pro Bowls, two All-Pro First Teams and three All-Pro Second Teams. He's also a two-time Super Bowl champion, having won with the Eagles in both 2017 and 2024.
He's still widely considered one of the small handful of best offensive linemen in the NFL, even at age 36. He checked in ninth in the recent CBS Sports poll , which ranked the top 10 players at every position, and he ranked even higher (third) in ESPN's annual poll of league executives and coaches.
His impact on Philadelphia's offense is dramatic, as the Eagles have experienced a huge drop-off in efficiency with Johnson off the field both in recent seasons and throughout his decorated career. The Eagles have averaged 0.04 EPA per play with Johnson on the field since 2013, and -0.05 EPA per play with him on the sidelines, according to TruMedia. That's equivalent to the difference between the third-best offense in the NFL during that time and the 27th-best.
Given his resume, Johnson is a potential future Hall-of-Famer. Our Bryan DeArdo recently named him the most likely Eagle to be inducted into the Hall of Fame, for example. If Johnson can put together one last season at an extremely high level, as we should expect given his recent track record, it would only improve his chances.
The Eagles, meanwhile, were seemingly prepared for this to be Johnson's last NFL season, having drafted a potential successor in the third round in former Miami Hurricanes tackle Markel Bell . The monster-sized Bell (6-foot-9, 345 pounds) would give Philadelphia one of the largest tackle duos in the NFL, though he obviously will have big shoes to fill in the event that Johnson decides to step away after the 2026 campaign.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Who's next for Canton? Ranking the biggest names eligible for the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2027
summary: Rob Gronkowski, Adrian Peterson and Ben Roethlisberger headline a star-studded group of first-time eligible players for the 2027 Pro Football Hall of Fame class
full_text:
In addition to 2026 snubs Bill Belichick, Robert Kraft and Eli Manning, a slew of other big names will be eligible for induction into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2027.
The list of first-time eligible players for 2027 includes two former league MVPs, a two-time Super Bowl champion quarterback, a former All-Pro defensive back and arguably the greatest tight end in NFL history. To get ready for 2027, we analyze first-time eligible stars in addition to some predictions along the way.
While former Patriots haven't had much luck in recent years, it's hard to imagine that stopping Gronkowski, who wasn't affiliated with Spygate and remains in seemingly good standing with football media.
Injuries may have slowed him down, but it hasn't stopped Gronkowski from being in the conversation among the greatest tight ends in NFL history. Along with being a constant mismatch in the passing game, Gronkowski was a devastating blocker, which strengthens his case as the most complete tight end of all time. His unique talent helped him win four Super Bowls.
Peterson is also widely regarded as one of the best ever at his position. The fifth leading rusher in NFL history, Peterson is the last non-quarterback to win league MVP. That season (2012), Peterson ran for 2,097 yards, the second-highest single-season total in league history. He won his third rushing title at age 30 and was still putting up 1,000-yard seasons at age 33.
The only thing that could hurt Peterson's chances next year is some recent legal issues , including an arrest in October of 2025. Peterson also ended his career with two forgettable seasons, but that alone would likely not be enough to prevent him from being voted in next year.
Roethlisberger is undoubtedly a future Hall of Famer; the question is whether or not enough voters feel that he is first-ballot worthy.
Roethlisberger's career milestones suggest that he is. He's seventh all-time in passing yards (64,088), ninth in touchdown passes (418), a two-time Super Bowl champion and is the youngest starting quarterback to win a Super Bowl. He twice led the NFL in passing yards and has the most 500-yard passing games (four) in NFL history. Roehtlisberger is also the only quarterback to throw six touchdowns in back-to-back games, doing so in 2014. He also holds the unofficial title of one of the hardest quarterbacks to take down.
Roethlisberger's magnum opus was at the end of Super Bowl XLIII, when he capped off the Steelers ' game-winning drive with a touchdown pass to Santonio Holmes that has gone down as one of the greatest plays in Super Bowl history.
Sherman should receive a gold jacket at some point. A member of the 2000s All-Decade Team, Sherman was a three-time All-Pro cornerback and the leader of the Seahawks ' "Legion of Boom" defense, which led Seattle to its first Super Bowl title.
A fellow 2000s All-Decade Team member, Mack delivered impressive longevity for an offensive lineman. He earned his first Pro Bowl nod at 25 and his last one at age 36. In between, he was named to five additional Pro Bowls and was a model of consistency.
Weddle -- another member of the 2000s All-Decade Team -- was a complete safety who excelled in both pass coverage and run support. He led the NFL in interceptions once and had over 100 tackles in a season on four occasions. At age 36, Weddle returned from retirement and helped the Rams win the Super Bowl.
Sherman's condensed prime (he made one Pro Bowl after his age-28 season) could prevent him from being a first-ballot inductee. Mack's lack of All-Pros will likely hurt his case, as offensive linemen are underrepresented in the Hall of Fame. Weddle also played a position that is underrepresented in Canton.
Taking next year off the table, it'll be interesting to see if these players ever get inducted.
McCoy was an excellent defensive tackle who was named to six straight Pro Bowls while manning the Buccaneers ' defensive line. But like Mack and Weddle, McCoy played a position that is often overlooked by voters unless you were the undisputed best at that position for a sustained period of time. For McCoy, that player is Aaron Donald , who will likely be inducted as soon as he is eligible.
Whitworth could potentially receive induction one day based on the fact that he was a two-time All-Pro who, at age 40, helped the Rams defeat his former team (the Bengals ) in the Super Bowl. More Pro Bowl selections would have strengthened his case, though. He was ultimately named to four Pro Bowls, including three straight from 2015-17.
Meteoric highs and lows largely embody Newton's career. In 2015, for example, he won the league MVP while leading the Panthers to a 15-1 regular-season record and an NFC title. He had a forgettable Super Bowl, however, marked by his lack of urgency in recovering his second fumble of the game, which ultimately set up the Broncos ' game-clinching score. Newton also had a short prime that was likely the byproduct of being one of the greatest running quarterbacks in NFL history. It came at a price: exposing himself to major hits.
From a talent and production standpoint, Brown did put together a Hall of Fame career. A former sixth-round pick, Brown built arguably the greatest six-year run in NFL history for a receiver. From 2013-18, he averaged 114 receptions for 1,525 yards and 11 touchdowns per season. He led the NFL in receptions and receiving yards twice and led the league in touchdown receptions once over that span.
Brown won a Super Bowl with the Buccaneers later in his career, but that was after an ugly breakup in Pittsburgh that was followed by even uglier breakups in Oakland and New England. Brown's time in Tampa -- and in the NFL, for that matter -- also ended on a sour note after he ran off the field -- shirtless -- during the middle of a game. It's safe to say that those moments, in addition to some off-field incidents, have put his Hall of Fame future in serious jeopardy.
Haden, Kerrigan, Jenkins, Brooks and Hightower enjoyed long, successful careers that included 15 combined Pro Bowl selections. Each one, however, will likely face an uphill climb for future induction, given that they were never tabbed as an All-Pro. Jenkins, Brooks and Hightower's cases are likely strengthened by the fact that they were key members on Super Bowl-winning teams.
A versatile running back, Bell was on his way to a potential Hall of Fame career after earning three Pro Bowls and two All-Pro nods during his first five seasons while playing alongside fellow "Killer B" teammates Roethlisberger and Brown. A season-long holdout, however, negatively changed the course of Bell's career and all but ended his Hall of Fame chances.
Gore, the NFL's third all-time leading rusher, should be a lock this year after he did not receive enough votes during his first year of eligibility. Suggs, the 2011 NFL Defensive Player of the Year and the owner of the most tackles for loss in NFL history, is surely hoping that a third time is a charm after he did not receive enough votes for induction during his first two years of eligibility.
Like Gore, Witten also didn't receive enough votes last year, his first year of eligibility. If recent history repeats itself, Jason Witten will have better luck this time around. Last year, Antonio Gates, another prolific tight end, was inducted in his second year of eligibility.
Regarding Roethlisberger, it's very possible that voters treat him similarly to Gates, Gore and Witten by not voting him in on his first year of eligibility. Conversely, it's safe to assume that Belichick will get enough votes after he was surprisingly omitted from this year's induction class.
Other players that will undoubtedly receive votes are Manning, Witten (who, like Gore, did not receive enough votes in his first year of eligibility), offensive linemen Willie Anderson, Jahri Evans, Marshal Yanda, receivers Tory Holt, Hines Ward and Reggie Wayne, safety Darren Woodson, quarterback Ken Anderson and defensive lineman…

title: 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame ceremony: Where to watch, TV, live stream
summary: Five players are set to join pro football's most exclusive fraternity
full_text:
Five former NFL players are about to formally join the most exclusive fraternity in professional football. Drew Brees, Larry Fitzgerald, Roger Craig, Adam Vinatieri, and Luke Kuechly will become the newest members of the Pro Football Hall of Fame during Saturday's induction ceremony.
Located in Canton, Ohio, the Pro Football Hall of Fame was built in 1963. Since then, 387 former NFL players, coaches and executives have received gold jackets, bronze busts, a ring and a permanent place in pro football lore.
This year's class will include one of the most prolific passers in football history, an equally prolific receiver, one of the most versatile running backs in NFL history, the NFL's all-time leading scorer and the second-youngest player to receive Hall of Fame induction.
Here's how you can watch the ceremony, in addition to summaries of each member of this year's induction class.
Date: Saturday, Aug. 8 | Time: 12 p.m. ET Location: Tom Benson Hall of Fame Stadium (Canton, Ohio) TV: ESPN/NFL Network; Stream: Fubo
Brees retired as the NFL's career leader in both passing yards (80,353) and touchdown passes (571) and is currently second in both categories behind Tom Brady . Brees never won league MVP, but he did capture Super Bowl MVP honors after leading the Saints to their first championship at the end of the 2009 season.
One of the most efficient and prolific quarterbacks of all-time, Brees led the NFL in passing seven times, completion percentage six times and touchdown passes on four occasions.
Fitzgerald is second only to Jerry Rice in career catches (1,432) and career receiving yards (17,492). During the 2008 playoffs, Fitzgerald caught 30 passes for 546 yards and seven touchdowns while helping the Cardinals reach the franchise's first Super Bowl. He caught seven passes for 127 yards and two scores in Arizona's Super Bowl loss to Pittsburgh.
At 35, Kuechly is the second-youngest person to earn a Hall of Fame induction. The youngest was Gale Sayers, who was 34 when he was inducted back in 1977.
Kuechly was one of the NFL's premier defensive players before injuries cut his career short after eight seasons. After winning Defensive Rookie of the Year, Kuechly won Defensive Player of the Year the following season and was named to seven straight Pro Bowls and was a five-time All-Pro. He helped spearhead a successful period in Panthers history that included three straight division titles and an NFC title in 2015.
The NFL's all-time leading scorer, Vinatieri, ended two Super Bowls with winning field goals. In addition to his four Super Bowl wins, Vinatieri is also notorious for his two critical kicks in blizzard-like conditions against the Raiders during the Patriots' first championship run.
One of the most versatile running backs in NFL history, Craig became the first player in history to post 1,000-yard rushing and receiving campaigns in the same season in 1985. His versatility was on full display in the prior year's Super Bowl, when he scored a Super Bowl record three touchdowns in the 49ers ' win over the Dolphins .
Three years later, Craig amassed over 2,000 all-purpose yards during the regular season before becoming the first running back to have over 100 receiving yards in a Super Bowl. Craig won his third Super Bowl a year later while helping the 49ers win back-to-back Super Bowl titles.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Kirk Cousins, Maxx Crosby held out of practice after altercation during Raiders' Friday practice
summary: Cousins and Crosby didn't practice after violating team rules
full_text:
Maxx Crosby and Kirk Cousins engaged in an altercation during the Las Vegas Raiders ' training camp practice on Friday. Both players were held out of practice on Saturday for violating team rules. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak, who informed reporters of his decision to sideline Crosby and Cousins, said that both players will take part in Monday's practice.
"We have very clear expectations on how we want to practice and how we want to go about our business, and we violated that yesterday," Kubiak said, via ESPN.
Friday's altercation began when Cousins took exception to Crosby hitting him on the arm twice during the team period. After the second hit, Cousins confronted Crosby and grabbed his jersey. The two players then exchanged words before being separated.
Crosby said prior to training camp that he had been warned by the team's new coaching staff about touching the quarterback during practice. He acknowledged at the time that his aggressiveness once led to his removal from practice while he was at Eastern Michigan.
"When you get out there and bullets are flying, I'm not thinking about not finishing the play," Crosby said prior to the start of camp, via ESPN . "That's just not in my nature. That's something I've been dealing with my whole career. It's not easy."
Kubiak addressed the incident following Friday's practice.
"Those are two leaders on our team going at it," he said. "Obviously, fighting in a game [or] you throw a punch in a game, you are out of the game. So we got to be smart."
While Crosby's aggressive nature is well-documented, Cousins' actions on Friday were an insight into his competitive spirit. It may also serve as a rallying cry for a Raiders offense that was pushed around far too often in 2025.
"You want him to defend your team," tight end Michael Mayer said of Cousins. "He's always had [that edge] since the first day I met him when he came in here."
The Crosby-Cousins scuffle was one of two altercations that took place during Friday's practice. And while fighting during practice isn't always a good thing, it might be for a once proud franchise that is looking to turn things around.
"It's energy, man," Mayer said. "We don't want to be throwing punches, but I think on any padded day of camp there's going to be some [scuffles]."
