title: What the media is saying about Cardinals QB Carson Beck now
summary: When Arizona Cardinals GM Monti Ossenfort selected University of Miami quarterback Carson Beck in the third round of April’s NFL draft, a lot of eyebrows went up. What? Who? How is a guy taken in Round 3 going to make a difference on this roster? Aren’t the Cardinals wanting to tank the 2026 season, then […]
full_text: Aug 6, 2026; Canton, Ohio, USA; Arizona Cardinals quarterback Carson Beck (19) throws the ball against Carolina Panthers cornerback Corey Thornton (31) at Tom Benson Hall of Fame Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect When Arizona Cardinals GM Monti Ossenfort selected University of Miami quarterback Carson Beck in the third round of April’s NFL draft, a lot of eyebrows went up. What? Who? How is a guy taken in Round 3 going to make a difference on this roster? Aren’t the Cardinals wanting to tank the 2026 season, then have their choice of several great college signalcallers? Why waste a third-round pick on a guy who isn’t going to help this team this year whatsoever? And then, what does the team do with Beck next year after they take their future franchise QB in the first round? RELATED: BECK GETS RAVE REVIEWS IN PRESEASON DEBUT All great questions. The selection of Beck was the very first pick in Round 3. Taken right after Beck was DT Tyler Onyedim of Texas A&M, DE Keyron Crawford from Auburn, and OT Markel Bell, Beck’s teammate at Miami. All three were positions of need that could make a dent on this year’s roster. Every completion from @carsonbeck01 's preseason debut 👀 pic.twitter.com/0WI9ofkRYw — NFL (@NFL) August 7, 2026 Despite being chosen in the third round, Beck was only the third quarterback taken. Fernando Mendoza from Indiana was the first overall pick by the Las Vegas Raiders, followed by the surprise selection of Alabama’s Ty Simpson at #13 by the Los Angeles Rams. No signalcallers were chosen in the second round. A glance at the 2026 preseason college football QB rankings shows Arch Manning of Texas, Oregon’s Dante Moore, Trinidad Chambliss of Ole Miss, and Miami’s Darian Mensah. All are already on the Heisman watch list. Why didn’t Ossenfort just wait another year to grab a young buck to sit and wait in the quarterback room? A waste of time and effort to get a quarterback in the third round, right? Well, Joe Montana was a third-round pick. So was Russell Wilson. Bart Starr was selected in Round 17. Brian Sipe in Round 13. Mark Brunell Round 5. Mark Rypien a round later. Washington legend Joe Theismann got picked in Round 4. Johnny Unitas in Round 9. What round was Roger Staubach taken? Round 10? How many quarterbacks were taken before Tom Brady heard his name called in Round 6? So, yes. Great quarterbacks don’t always have to be taken in the first round of the draft. There are probably more first-round busts than first-round success stories at the QB position: Johnny Football, Ryan Leaf, Marcus Mariota, Justin Fields, Zach Wilson, Jim Drunkenmiller, and the Cardinals’ Josh Rosen. Hell, Dan Marino was taken in the first round after five other quarterbacks had already come off the board. All this circles back to Beck. He has the size NFL coaches savor, being 6’-5” and a beefy 235 pounds. He was voted “Florida Mr. Football” as a high school senior and the USA Today Offensive Player of the Year. Beck won a high school state championship. He won two National Championships while at Georgia and almost won another one while at Miami. Winning and being a champion is nothing new for Beck. He played over the top in the Hall of Fame Game. Keep in mind, he was surrounded by second-team players on his own team and played against the Carolina Panthers’ second-team defense. So, keep that in perspective. But every guy on the Panthers’ second-team defense should make the final roster. Most will have plenty of snaps this year. Some will eventually start. And that second-tier defense had more talent than almost any college defense Beck ever faced. LINK: GET TO KNOW ROOKIE QB CARSON BECK But Beck played extremely well. His numbers: 15 completions on 19 attempts, 188 yards, 1 touchdown pass, 0 interceptions, 1 sack, 2 rushes for 3 yards, QB rating of 125.4, and 0 turnovers. Third-down efficiency of 58.3%. Fourth-down plays: 0-1. Drives: 6. Results: punt, TD, TD, FG, downs (one kneel-down to end half), downs (incompletion on fourth-down play). Longest play: 49 yards to WR Jalen Brooks in Quarter 2. Cardinals’ head coach Mike LaFleur had Beck’s snap counts all laid out. He would play the entire first half and then the first drive of the second half so that it would feel like an actual game coming out of the halftime locker room. So, what is the media saying about Ossenfort’s choice for a young quarterback? Arizona Sports: Tyler Drake “Just about everyone in the football world got a good, hard look at rookie quarterback Carson Beck running the show. Looking calm, cool, collected and confident throughout his more than two quarters of work, the rookie executed just about everything that was asked of him. He put the ball in places where only the receiver had a chance at snagging it. He showed off his ability to go through his reads, hang in the pocket, and deliver. It’s the preseason , but Beck looked like he had been there before.” Cardinals rookie Carson Beck on the midgame adjustment he made with WR Jalen Brooks before connecting on the deep ball (that JB somehow hung onto despite the hit) ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/yovIB5c3jc — Tyler Drake (@Tdrake4sports) August 7, 2026 ESPN First Take: Stephen A. Smith “Arizona’s got nowhere to go but up. In (Beck’s) situation, that’s somebody that you should consider throwing up in there if he’s got that kind of moxie with him. We know what we saw. Intermediate throws, deep throws, especially the trajectory on those throws, particularly the corner touchdown that he threw. It was very, very impressive – no doubt about that. He had a lot of accuracy. He was poised. He dipped and dunked when necessary. He took what the defense gave him. All of those things are incredibly important that you’re looking for from a relatively young quarterback.“ Yahoo! Sports: Ian Casselberry “Carson Beck, the Cardinals’ third-round draft pick (No. 65 overall), looked impressive in his NFL preseason debut. Beck showed touch on his TD throw to Simi Fehoko on a 5-yard face route for the score. It was quite the preseason debut for the rookie third-round pick out of Miami.” Have you guys heard about this Carson Beck kid? (via @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/gpsGcCXv9z — B/R Gridiron (@brgridiron) August 7, 2026 Arizona Daily Sun: Jaydn Wilgus “Carson Beck has spent long days at the team facility learning a new offense, building chemistry with teammates and picking the brains of coaches. He is not focused on the starting role. He is concentrating on learning the offense and adjusting to a new system. He added that leadership has developed through experience as much as preparation. His approach remains focused on daily improvement rather than outcomes.” Bleacher Report: Timothy Rapp “Carson Beck made quite the preseason debut on Thursday night. The Arizona Cardinals rookie quarterback led his team to three scoring drives in the first half of Thursday’s Hall of Fame Game, making a strong first impression. Beck didn’t just have good numbers—he also made some fantastic throws. Suffice to say, NFL fans and pundits were impressed with Beck’s showing.” Revenge of the Birds: Seth Cox “The questions about Carson Beck will continue to mount. Not whether he is good, but when the Arizona Cardinals should pull the trigger and start him this season. And it had the interwebs hyped. What is fun is that the Cardinals spent the better part of the week getting crapped on for a training camp slideshow that was a cut of the lowlights. That is what the internet is for, though, to give you an opportunity to shut it up for at least one night. Several other good throws too. pic.twitter.com/wvVD10HqJV — rich madrid (@richjmadrid_) August 7, 2026 NFL.com: Kevin Patra “It should come as no…

title: The Falcoholic Reacts: How productive will Zachariah Branch be?
summary: Zachariah Branch continues to be the standout player at training camp. The Falcoholic’s own Kevin Knight recently highlighted the impression he is making on the team. From creating separation to making difficult contested catches, the rookie wide receiver is doing it all to prove he is ready to play significant snaps at the start of […]
full_text: FLOWERY BRANCH, GEORGIA - MAY 27: Zachariah Branch #17 of the Atlanta Falcons runs through drills during OTA's at IBM Performance Field on May 27, 2026 in Flowery Branch, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Zachariah Branch continues to be the standout player at training camp. The Falcoholic’s own Kevin Knight recently highlighted the impression he is making on the team. From creating separation to making difficult contested catches, the rookie wide receiver is doing it all to prove he is ready to play significant snaps at the start of the season. After there was internal belief that the coaching staff needed to take it slow with him, Branch is looking ready to see the field in 11 and possibly even some 12-personnel sets. His emergence this summer has led to raised expectations. It’s reasonable to believe he can produce a certain amount of yards in his rookie season. While there is uncertainty at quarterback, Branch will have big play opportunities given the star power around him. His ability to win one-on-one matchups while Kevin Stefanski schemes up plays to get him the ball in space will be crucial to turn his eye-opening summer into a productive fall and winter. Many fans believe he can do that by gaining over 500 receiving yards. With his sheer explosiveness and elusiveness, Branch may not need as many receptions as most wide receivers would need to gain over 500 yards. How he creates extra yards after the catch could accumulate into more production, particularly on third downs. Although there will be games where he isn’t much of a factor, the former Bulldog looks capable of making a sizable impact on a team that will likely be forced to score more following Jalon Walker’s devastating season-ending injury. title: Ravens WR Zay Flowers ‘day-to-day’ with quad injury
summary: The Baltimore Ravens had a minor scare at Saturday’s training camp practice when star wide receiver Zay Flowers – who just signed a four-year, $140 million contract extension – went down in a collision with safety Jaylinn Hawkins. Flowers got up initially then went back down to the ground to stretch out his left leg […]
full_text: OWINGS MILLS, MARYLAND - JULY 29: Zay Flowers #4 of the Baltimore Ravens practices on the first day of training camp at Under Armour Performance Center Baltimore Ravens on July 29, 2026 in Owings Mills, Maryland. (Photo by Jamie Sabau/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens had a minor scare at Saturday’s training camp practice when star wide receiver Zay Flowers – who just signed a four-year, $140 million contract extension – went down in a collision with safety Jaylinn Hawkins. Flowers got up initially then went back down to the ground to stretch out his left leg before limping off the field and eventually inside the facility, per Baltimore Beatdown’s Kevin McNelis. Head coach Jesse Minter said after practice that Flowers is “day-to-day” with a quad contusion and will likely miss some practice time. Looking forward to giving you guys a more thorough breakdown and some photos later today with @BmoreBeatdown ! pic.twitter.com/gGyI8vh1Vf — Kevin McNelis (@KMackSports) August 8, 2026 Flowers, 25, became the NFL’s fourth-highest-paid wide receiver this week with a $35MM APY deal that will keep him in Baltimore through the 2031 season. He has been the focal point of the Ravens’ passing game over the last two seasons, averaging 6.9 targets, 4.7 receptions, and 66.8 yards per game in back-to-back Pro Bowl campaigns. His absence will lead to an uptick in opportunities for the rest of the team’s receiving corps, particularly 2024 fourth-round pick Devontez Walker and rookies Ja’Kobi Lane and Elijah Sarratt, who are looking to carve out roles in offensive coordinator Declan Doyle’s new scheme. Lane had another highlight-filled practice on Saturday, beating Nate Wiggins on a go route in 1-on-1 work and reeling in a back shoulder pass from Lamar Jackson in 7-on-7’s with one hand despite tight coverage from Keyon Martin. “It’s a great opportunity for other guys to step into those roles, different guys to run some of the routes that Zay’s great at,” Minter added. “But I don’t expect it to be too long.” Doyle is also expected to expand Rashod Bateman’s role after primarily serving as a deep threat thus far in his career. With Flowers sidelined, the veteran wideout could step into the Ravens’ WR1 spot with a much more varied deployment in terms of alignments, motion, and route concepts. Bateman said this week that he feels re-energized by Doyle’s system and his place in it, which includes much more work out of the slot. F it we're talking about it. There have been 180 WRs to run 500+ routes since 2021, when Rashod Bateman entered the league. He has lined up in the slot on just 10.3% of his snaps, the third-lowest (178/180) mark in that span. He has consistently taken 80% or more of his snaps… https://t.co/RqDoyMU9cl — Matt Harmon (@MattHarmon_BYB) August 6, 2026 “I’m moving around all over the place,” Bateman told reporters on Thursday. “I feel like in the past I’ve been kind of a one-dimensional receiver.” But Doyle, he believes, recognizes his talent and is giving him more opportunities to show it on the field, which he called a “blessing.” The Ravens will certainly monitor Flowers very closely over the next week. Under John Harbaugh, starters like him rarely played in the preseason. While Minter has yet to announce any preseason start/sit decisions, Flowers is extremely unlikely to play in next weekend’s matchup against the Eagles.

title: Buffalo Bills 2026 scouting report: wide receiver Skyler Bell
summary: The Buffalo Bills entered the 2026 offseason period in need of receiving help. Last year, they had a receiving corps that could kindly be described as poor, and it was one that was clearly not a threat for multiple top-flight defenses. When you can send any number of blitzers against a quarterback as good as […]
full_text: ROCHESTER, NEW YORK - JULY 29: Skyler Bell #13 of the Buffalo Bills participates in drills during training camp at St. John Fisher University on July 29, 2026 in Rochester, New York. (Photo by Joe Hrycych/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills entered the 2026 offseason period in need of receiving help. Last year, they had a receiving corps that could kindly be described as poor, and it was one that was clearly not a threat for multiple top-flight defenses. When you can send any number of blitzers against a quarterback as good as Josh Allen, yet still have supreme confidence that his wideouts have next to no chance at uncovering, you know there’s a problem with the group as a whole. So, general manager Brandon Beane fixed the mess that, well, he made the offseason prior. He traded for a stud veteran wideout, and the early returns on that deal seem positive. He also drafted a speedster in the fourth round, gambling that the slightly undersized pass-catcher’s talent would outweight that smaller stature. In today’s edition of “91 players in 91 days,” we discuss that rookie wideout. _____________________________________________________________________________ Name: Skyler Bell Number: 13 Position: WR Height/Weight: 5’11” 192 lbs. Age: 24 (25 on 7/5/2027) Experience/Draft: R; selected by Buffalo in the fourth round (No. 125 overall) of the 2026 NFL Draft College: UConn Acquired: Fourth-round draft choice Financial situation (per Spotrac): Bell’s four-year rookie deal is worth a total of $5,471,764. For the 2026 season, his cap hit is $1,157,941 if he makes the 53-man roster. If he’s released, Buffalo will carry a dead cap charge equal to the total guarantees on the deal, or $1,091,764. 2025 Recap: In his fifth year of eligibility, Bell had his best season, building on the solid start he had at Connecticut in 2024 and playing even better in 2025. He caught 101 passes for 1,278 yards and 13 touchdowns. All of those totals led Division I Independent schools (Notre Dame, Oregon State, and Washington State were the other Independent schools). Bell was a consensus All-American pick, and he was also named a finalist for the Biletnikoff Award as the nation’s top wide receiver. At the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine, Bell displayed excellent speed and burst. He ran the forty-yard dash in 4.4 seconds, and he leapt 41” in the vertical jump and 11’1” in the broad jump. Positional outlook: Bell is one of 14 wideouts in camp for the Bills. Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman, DJ Moore, Joshua Palmer, Mecole Hardman Jr., Tyrell Shavers, Quentin Skinner, Dante Pettis, Mac Dalena, Max Tomczak, Stephen Gosnell, Trent Sherfield, and Ja’Mori Maclin are the others. 2026 Offseason: Bell is healthy and he’s been solid at training camp so far, albeit with some hiccups. The Bills have used him in a variety of roles, and he’s shown great burst and route running ability to give himself space. He’s had some issues with drops, however. 2026 Season outlook: When he was drafted, I envisioned Bell coming in and making an immediate impact as the third or fourth receiver. However, I think now that assessment might have been a little premature. Bell is going to make the team, and I still think he’s going to be active on game days and available for specific packages. However, with veteran Joshua Palmer having a good camp and third-year man Keon Coleman doing some good things, it’s going to be tough for Bell to find time on the field, especially if he has trouble securing catches after beating corners off the line of scrimmage. Bell has a speed element that most of Buffalo’s other wideouts just don’t have, but unless he offers the ability to return kickoffs or punts, he’s going to have a bit of an uphill climb to playing time early in his career. Could he beat out Coleman and Palmer for time? Absolutely. Palmer showed little in his time before suffering an injury last season, and Coleman has been a disappointment for two seasons running. Coleman, for what it’s worth, has had his own issues with drops this summer, so Bell could make a move as August rolls onward. Buffalo’s top five receivers aren’t necessarily set in stone, but I feel fairly confident in calling Shakir, Moore, Palmer, Coleman, and Bell the five guys that will definitely be on the roster come September. Can Bell find some utility on punt return to make himself a lock for a game jersey on Sundays? OR will that role go to a veteran like Mecole Hardman Jr.? Will the Bills see enough potential in Bell that he leapfrogs Coleman or Palmer for reps on offense? Those questions are all as-yet unanswered. For now, we know that the Bills seem to have found a good mid-round player in Skyler Bell. He’s someone I’m very excited to see in preseason action, and even more excited to see once the games matter in September and beyond.

title: 2026 Season Opener Countdown: 36 Days Remaining
summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, N.C. - AUGUST 19: Brentson Buckner #99 of the Carolina Panthers jumps out from the fog pouring out of the mouth of an inflated panther as he is introduced before the game against the New York Giants on August 19, 2004 at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, North Carolina. The Panthers won 27-20. (Photo By Grant Halverson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #36. Brentson Buckner The Carolina Panthers had one of the most dominant defensive lines of the early 2000s. Spoiler: all four of the starters from that group are going to show up on this list, and we’ve made it to the first one. Brentson Buckner was the fourth of the four horseman, and he thrived in that role. Buckner came into the NFL from nearby Clemson University via a second round pick by the Pittsburgh Steelers. He was a near immediate impact player there. For reasons I can’t quite figure out, he was traded from the Steelers to the Chiefs but then somehow ended up on the Bengals before the season started. His effectiveness was drastically diminished from his time with the Steelers, and he departed after one season to join the 49ers. There, he started to recapture his old form before signing with the Panthers. Buckner joined the Panthers at 30 years old and spent the final six years of his career in Carolina. He tallied 14.5 sacks and 25 tackles for loss in those six seasons, forming a dominant front four with Kris Jenkins, Mike Rucker, and Julius Peppers. He was exactly the kind of player you want at defensive tackle alongside superstars like Kris Jenkins and Julius Peppers. He was ever reliable and brought enough juice as both a run stopper and pass rusher to keep pressure off the bigger names around him. He was an integral part of a dominant Panthers defensive front that helped carry the team to the Super Bowl in 2003, and he contributed 1.5 sacks in the NFC Championship game to help send the Panthers to that Super Bowl. He was released in 2006, and that ended up marking the end of his playing career. He stayed in Charlotte coaching high school football and cohosting a radio show before getting into coaching at the NFL level. His contributions to what was a sort of golden era of Panthers football lands him at number 36 on the list of top 100 Panthers of all time.

Offense We’ll start with the notable injury news of the day, as 2nd year WR Luther Burden limped off the practice field roughly halfway through practice and did not return. The injury occurred during a 1-on-1 route with Tyrique Stevenson right in front of us, but there was no obvious moment when the injury occurred. It looked like Burden had some sort of leg injury from how he was limping. Hopefully it’s nothing serious. Looking at the LT competition, Braxton Jones remained out after he got injured a few days ago. Jedrick Wills Jr. got all the 1st team reps I saw. The rest of the OL starters were the usual combination (LG Thuney, C Bradbury, RG Jackson, RT Wright). The 2nd string OL, from L to R, was Kiran Amegadjie, Luke Newman, Logan Jones, Jordan McFadden, and Theo Benedet. I did not see anybody else take a 1st or 2nd team rep on the OL, though several of the 2nd string OL also played some snaps on the 3rd string at times. The Bears did a lot red zone work today, from walk-throughs to 7-on-7s and full team drills. One notable play that popped up a few times was a QB keeper. They lined up in shotgun, had the RB motion one way, and then had the QB keep and run off tackle to the other direction. They ran that with all 3 strings in walk throughs, and then brought it back 2 different times in full team drills later. I couldn’t see any of the 7-on-7s, so while I heard Caleb and Loveland had a big day there , I can’t personally verify that. Defense There were a ton of defensive guys out today, so some of the 1st/2nd/3rd string lineups were a bit wonky. DE Montez Sweat was out after getting hurt a couple days ago, and DE Shemar Turner has yet to practice while he works back from injury, so DE was definitely shorthanded. With that said, I did find it notable that DT James Lynch got a lot of work at DE with the 2nd string. Given the DE injuries, I also found it notable that Dayo Odeyingbo still got a lot of reps at DT, and even did some positional drills with the DTs instead of the DE. That meant DE Daniel Hardy got a decent number of snaps with the starting defense, which is something we hopefully won’t see during the season. DT is the only defensive position not currently decimated by injuries, so it seems particularly notable that rookie 6th round pick Jordan van den Berg continued to get some snaps with the 1s. He was easily the quickest and fastest DT in all the positional drills, and he showcased his strength with some nice bull rushes, too. He seems to be at least DT4 at this point. I didn’t see Neville Gallimore take any 1st team reps, but he could have mixed in at some point. Undrafted rookie DT Jayden Loving also earned some reps with the 2s. LB was also extremely shorthanded, as TJ Edwards only did individual drills today and D’Marco Jackson didn’t practice. I’m not sure why Jackson was out, as he practiced Thursday before the Bears’ day off yesterday. Jack Sanborn was the next man up, as he and Devin Bush were the only LB I saw take any snaps with the starters. That probably doesn’t speak well for 2025 4th round pick Ruben Hyppolite’s chances of making the roster, as he is seemingly behind Edwards, Jackson, Devin Bush, Sanborn, and likely 5th round pick Keyshaun Elliot when he returns from the PUP. CB is also extremely shorthanded right now, as Kyler Gordon remains on PUP and Jaylon Jones, who had been the starting nickel back in Gordon’s place, is also out. Tyrique Stevenson added to these woes when he got banged up in the same 1-on-1 rep that injured Luther Burden. He landed hard on his tailbone and immediately grabbed at it. He consulted with trainers for a few minutes, and returned to practice while still moving gingerly. He seemed to be back to normal by the end of practice. Rookie 4th round pick Malik Muhammad took advantage of all the injuries, as he was the starting nickel back for the day. When Stevenson was out, Muhammad slid outside and Josh Blackwell filled in as the starting nickel. Stop me if you’ve heard this before, but S is also extremely banged up. Coby Bryant is out with an injury, and Elijah Hicks is still on the PUP list. Cam Lewis took Bryants’ available reps with the 1s today, but he got hurt right at the end of practice and was carted off. It looked like he came up grabbing at his ankle. Undrafted rookie Skyler Thomas stepped in with the starters after Lewis left, so he seems to be pushing for a roster (or at least practice squad) spot. Newly signed safeties Xavier Woods and William Wright were out there today. Woods worked exclusively with the 2s, but I would imagine the injury to Lewis helps him slide into the starting lineup sooner rather than later. Rookie Dillon Thieneman made some splash plays in 11-on-11s late in practice. He stuffed Kyle Monangai on a goal-line running play, and then undercut a Caleb Williams Hail Mary (on 4th down) for an interception a few minutes later. Special Teams The Bears didn’t do a ton of special teams work today, but they did have a punt drill. A few observations from that, mostly who was playing: I spotted RB Kyle Monangai with the 1st team punt protection unit, which really surprised me. He didn’t play a single special teams snap last year. The Bears had 3 players working on catching punts: WR Kalif Raymond, WR Zavion Thomas, and WR JP Richardson. Thomas ended up fumbling one of his catch attempts. Hang out with Lester & JB at 2:00 p.m. CT in the embed right here, or you can head over to our YouTube channel to join in on our live Bear & Balanced to discuss the day and how the Bears are looking this far.

title: Cash, Stash, or Slash: Austin Booker
summary: We have talked about how the Chicago Bears have a lot of work to do for their defensive line for 2027 and moving forward. There are players with large contracts that are underperforming and almost certainly won’t return (Dayo Odeyingbo, Grady Jarrett); there are players like Gervon Dexter that has his contract expiring. But there […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - JANUARY 10: Austin Booker #94 of the Chicago Bears reacts after a sacj during an NFL wild card playoff game against the Green Bay Packers at Soldier Field on January 10, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images We have talked about how the Chicago Bears have a lot of work to do for their defensive line for 2027 and moving forward. There are players with large contracts that are underperforming and almost certainly won’t return (Dayo Odeyingbo, Grady Jarrett); there are players like Gervon Dexter that has his contract expiring. But there is Austin Booker, who is developing, but just how good can he be and what does that mean for an extension? The question about how good Booker can be is a serious question that the Bears don’t have the answer to yet. They need to be confident in that answer before they can even flirt with a contract extension for him. This year is going to be a huge one for Booker to determine what kind of earnings he might be headed towards for his second NFL contract. Austin Booker: Stash At this point, you almost need to sit on Austin Booker, not just for 2026, but probably for 2027 as well. Booker has 6 career sacks after two seasons in Chicago. If Booker doesn’t improve much more from his 2025 season, he’s going to settle in as a DE3, and he will be paid like a rotational player in Chicago or somewhere else. But what if Booker leaps this year? What if Booker jumps to 8 to 10 sacks? What if he presents consistent pressure from the edge, and what if he improves in run defense enough to where he is just an average defender? If that happens in 2026, and it is certainly in the realm of possible outcomes, suddenly Booker is going to be looking for starting Edge money, and that’s certainly a significant raise from a rotational player. Then the question becomes, what do the Bears think? Do the Bears think he’s going to continue on an upward trajectory, will they be concerned that 2026 was a peak for him and that’s the player moving forward, or perhaps do they think it’s an anomaly and he will regress moving forward? There are simply too many variables at play right now to determine if Booker is going to be a part of this defensive line moving forward, and exactly what his role is going to be within that unit. I think the Bears need to see how this season plays out. If Booker performs similarly to what he did in 2025, that’s a rotational player that doesn’t need an early extension. But if he does take a step forward this season, I think the Bears still should wait and see what Booker looks like in 2027 as well, and if he’s looking sharp and as good or improving again from 2026, I could see Booker as a November extension candidate, as they did with Andrew Billings a few years ago. Booker has such a wide range of outcomes at this point after two seasons, so the Bears should just place him in the “Stash” category and see what direction his career heads.

title: Tanner Hudson continues to show his worth in Bengals offense
summary: In recent years, the tight end position has been a revolving door for the Cincinnati Bengals. Once CJ Uzomah left after the 2021 season, several tight ends tried to fill the void. The revolving door didn’t close until Mike Gesicki landed in Cincinnati and signed an extension in March of 2025 to stay for multiple years. […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - DECEMBER 28: Cincinnati Bengals tight end Tanner Hudson (87) walks off the field at halftime during the game against the Arizona Cardinals and the Cincinnati Bengals on December 28, 2025, at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images In recent years, the tight end position has been a revolving door for the Cincinnati Bengals . Once CJ Uzomah left after the 2021 season, several tight ends tried to fill the void. The revolving door didn’t close until Mike Gesicki landed in Cincinnati and signed an extension in March of 2025 to stay for multiple years. There’s been another tight end, though, who has been in the background. He hasn’t been at the top of the depth chart, but that hasn’t stopped him from contributing heavily and earning the trust of Joe Burrow. Tanner Hudson Height: 6-5 Weight: 241 lbs. Age: 31 College: Southern Arkansas Hometown: Paris, Tennessee Experience: 7 years Cap Status Hudson signed a one-year contract worth $1.35 million, which included $50,000 guaranteed. His salary counts for less than one percent of the team’s total salary cap. This is the third one-year deal he’s signed with the Bengals. Background Hudson started his collegiate career as a quarterback and punter at Memphis before transferring to Southern Arkansas, where he transitioned to tight end. The position change turned out to be the right move, as Hudson became one of Division II’s most productive tight ends. He finished his college career with 143 catches for 2,152 yards and 25 touchdowns, earning first-team All-GAC honors and second-team All-American recognition his senior year. Hudson went undrafted in 2018 and signed as a free agent with the Buccaneers. He spent three seasons bouncing back and forth between the active roster and practice squad, and earned a Super Bowl LV ring. He had brief stops with the 49ers and Giants before the Bengals signed him to their practice squad late in the 2022 season. Hudson emerged as a reliable receiving option for the Bengals in 2023, posting career highs with 39 receptions for 352 yards and his first NFL touchdown. He developed strong chemistry with backup quarterback Jake Browning and has remained a dependable depth piece at the position ever since, catching 19 passes in both the 2024 and 2025 seasons. Outlook for 202 6 The top tight end on the depth chart is Mike Gesicki, but he’s a tight end in name only. He’s more of a slot receiver than a tight end. Drew Sample is going to be above Hudson on the depth chart as well, but he plays as an H-Back as much or more than he does at tight end. Hudson has carved out a nice little space for himself on the Bengals’ roster. He’s not as good of a blocker as Sample, and he’s not the receiver Gesicki is, but he can do both when he’s asked to, and he can do both well. The biggest threat to Hudson in 2026 is Erick All. A local kid, All hasn’t taken a snap since 2024 and has been dealing with a knee injury that started back in college. All is reportedly healthy, and if he can stay that way, he’ll cut into Hudson’s playing time. If All is unable to stay healthy, though, the Bengals could do a lot worse than Hudson as their TE3.

title: Anthony Munoz ranked among the 100 best NFL players of all time
summary: There are dozens of not only great players, but phenomenal players in the history of the NFL. Bryan DeArdo of CBS Sports recently published his list of the top 100 players in NFL history. Cincinnati Bengals great Anthony Munoz landed at No. 19, being proclaimed as the best left tackle in NFL history. To understand how […]
full_text: There are dozens of not only great players, but phenomenal players in the history of the NFL. Bryan DeArdo of CBS Sports recently published his list of the top 100 players in NFL history . Cincinnati Bengals great Anthony Munoz landed at No. 19, being proclaimed as the best left tackle in NFL history. To understand how big of a feat that is, let’s take a look at some of the previous Bengals before and after Munoz, as well as other players Munoz landed in front of on the list. On the Bengals side, you’re looking at players like Ken Anderson, Ken Riley, Boomer Esiason, Chad Johnson, A.J. Green, Corey Dillon, James Brooks and Tim Krumrie, with a dozen more to list. Now, league-wide, Munoz landed in front of Marcus Allen, Steve Van Buren, Troy Aikman, Bart Starr, Forrest Gregg and Mike Ditka, to name a few. Munoz, a Hall of Famer and Bengals Ring of Honor member, is considered one of the best linemen in NFL history. He was the third overall pick by the Bengals in the 1980 NFL Draft, though it was considered a risky move at the time with his injury history. He became a starter during his rookie campaign and stayed in that spot for the next 13 seasons with the Bengals; he was a 9x All-Pro and 11x Pro Bowler. Fewer than 50 players have been selected to more than 10 Pro Bowls. At the time of his retirement, he was tied with Tom Mack for most Pro Bowls for an offensive lineman in history. Munoz was a pivotal member of both Super Bowl teams led by Ken Anderson and Boomer Esiason, also helping both players eventually win league MVPs. Not too many know, but he was a versatile player. Not only was he a phenomenal pass blocker, but he tallied seven receptions and four touchdowns. He was Offensive Lineman of the Year in 1981 and 1988 (both Super Bowl years for the Bengals), along with NFLPA Offensive Lineman of the Year in ‘81, ‘85, ‘88, and ‘89, and NFL Alumni Association Offensive Lineman of the Year in ‘87, ‘89, ‘90, and ‘91. Offensive linemen create and sustain their legacy by protecting the quarterback, especially the left tackle. Munoz went his entire 13-year career with just 14 holding penalties and 16 false starts. In 1994, he was named to the NFL 75th Anniversary All-Time Team and ranked 17th on the greatest players list in 1999. He was inducted into the NFL Hall of Fame in 1998 and the Cincinnati Bengals Ring of Honor in 2021. An all-time great, indeed.

title: At least for one day: Browns Shedeur Sanders is QB2, Deshaun Watson takes QB1 lead
summary: With the Cleveland Browns, you never really know what to expect. That statement has been true across coaching staffs, front offices, and ownership, no matter who was in those roles. Throughout the offseason, including in training camp, the Browns quarterback competition had seen Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders alternating time with the first team. Whether […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 03: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns talks with Shedeur Sanders #2 during the Cleveland Browns OTA Offseason Workouts at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 03, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images With the Cleveland Browns, you never really know what to expect. That statement has been true across coaching staffs, front offices, and ownership, no matter who was in those roles. Throughout the offseason, including in training camp, the Browns quarterback competition had seen Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders alternating time with the first team. Whether there was a “signal” that Watson had taken the lead or the veteran came into camp with a “leg up,” Cleveland HC Todd Monken was consistent with his messaging and, generally, how the reps were distributed. Both of those things changed on Saturday. First, Monken informed the media before practice that the plan was to continue with the alternating at quarterback, with Sanders next up to take reps with the first team: Todd Monken before practice: “(Deshaun) might end up with a 7-on-7 (rep with the 1s) … but Shedeur will take the majority of the 1 reps today.” The Browns are off Sunday, and Monken isn’t scheduled to speak to reporters again until Monday. https://t.co/61crf3LiQ7 pic.twitter.com/8cIWe56250 — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) August 8, 2026 When practice started, Monken’s words were not followed up with action as Watson took all of the first-team reps, with Sanders splitting time with the second team, along with Dillon Gabriel . As seen in the infamous QB tracker , Watson attempted 34 passes on Saturday, with Sanders throwing 20 and Gabriel throwing 12. A majority of the time, Watson was followed by Gabriel, not Sanders, in each drill. Following practice, when asked about the change in reps from what the media was told prior to practice and what actually happened on the field, we were told that “There were personnel groupings (Monken) wanted to see Deshaun with.” Prior to practice, Monken noted that the team was starting to whittle things down to what would be considered game preparation in advance of the Chicago Bears. The team is off on Sunday before returning to the field on Monday. There is a lot of speculation as to what led to today’s changes. Whether Monken is close to naming Watson the starter, something happened in the few minutes between the media session and practice, the coach is trying to motivate Sanders, or any other suggestion that you can come up with, for one day Watson was clearly the Browns starter, and Sanders was demoted. title: Browns closing in on QB decision for preseason opener
summary: Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken has spent the first 10 days of training camp putting the offense through its paces as he ponders what to do with an uninspiring quarterback room. Monken has the unenviable task of choosing between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders to start the August 15 preseason game against the Chicago […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 11: Deshaun Watson #4 and Shedeur Sanders #2 of the Cleveland Browns run a drill during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 11, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken has spent the first 10 days of training camp putting the offense through its paces as he ponders what to do with an uninspiring quarterback room. Monken has the unenviable task of choosing between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders to start the August 15 preseason game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field. It is not a make-or-break decision by any means; Monken has said that he expects to give both Watson and Sanders a start in the preseason. And depending on which day of the week it is, and which quarterback fans are predisposed to prefer, either Watson has flexed his veteran presence to firmly grasp the QB1 role, or Sanders has shown enough improvement and grasp of the offense to be the obvious choice. Thankfully, at least as it pertains to the game against the Bears, we all may know soon enough which quarterback will be in the huddle for the first offensive series of the preseason, as Monken and the staff will spend the next few days reviewing the candidates and then make the decision public ( quotes via The Beacon Journal ): “That’s something we’ll talk about tomorrow. I think tonight, tomorrow, and then Monday, we’ll start to really focus in on who’s going to start, how we’re going to play our guys, and where we’re at a quarterback’s a piece of that. “We’re now done with installs (and have had) a chance to assess. We already talked about it last night and then tomorrow. And now we’re into game week. Closest thing we’ll have to a game is the Bears. And so I will start to put the pieces where we think, again, at that time after another week, we’ll reassess come Monday. But you’ll see that on Monday.” Monken previously stated that he would give both Watson and Sanders one start in the preseason before making the final call about which quarterback will start the opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars. But that plan is subject to change depending on how things go next week in practice and then in the game against the Bears, according to Monken ( quote via Browns Zone ): “That’s still in mind. We’re still on that track of liking to have one start one game and then the other. But everything we do is subject to change. I mean, with every position we have on the field. We’ll see how it goes today. We’ll see how it goes Monday. We’ll see how it goes Tuesday. And then we’ll put our best foot forward next Saturday.” The good news is that by Monday everyone should know the plan for the preseason game against the Bears. The bad news is that it really doesn’t matter which quarterback Monken picks, as neither has shown enough to instill confidence that they can be the answer. And the debate over which quarterback is the right choice – Watson or Sanders – will continue long into the upcoming season.
author: Thomas Moore

title: Browns: Will team come to regret this contract extension?
summary: The Cleveland Browns traded defensive end Myles Garrett on June 1, which almost immediately kicked off a wave of speculation about what would come next. The prevailing thought was that the decision to part with the game’s best defensive player surely meant that the Browns were punting on the 2026 season (and maybe a few […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JULY 29: Denzel Ward #21 of the Cleveland Browns intercepts a pass intended for Tylan Wallace #16 during Cleveland Browns Training Camp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on July 29, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns traded defensive end Myles Garrett on June 1, which almost immediately kicked off a wave of speculation about what would come next. The prevailing thought was that the decision to part with the game’s best defensive player surely meant that the Browns were punting on the 2026 season (and maybe a few additional ones) and that general manager Andrew Berry was about to start some form of a fire sale. Speculation quickly centered on cornerback Denzel Ward as the most likely trade target – unless someone was dumb enough to covet one of the quarterbacks – as the eight-year veteran would bring back the biggest return in a trade. Berry had other plans, of course, as he signed Ward to a contract extension that should keep one of the game’s best cornerbacks on the Browns through the 2029 season . The deal pays Ward $52.3 million in guaranteed money, and the overall value of the contract makes Ward the highest-paid cornerback in the league, at least for the moment. While the deal was met with favorable reviews from fans, not everyone is as enamored with it, a group that includes ESPN’s Seth Walder. In his latest column, Walder looks at some of the recent contract extensions across the league, and he does not take a favorable view of what the Browns did with Ward : The Browns handed Ward, one of their defensive pillars, a two-year extension worth $31.1 million per year to keep him in Cleveland through 2029. But it’s not a deal I would have made. Ward is 29 years old and, critically, had two years left on his contract (at a reasonable $20.25 million per year). I would not have been in a rush to add more money to secure his rights in his age-31 and age-32 seasons. Ward is still well-respected and ranked seventh among cornerbacks in Fowler’s survey of coaches and executives on the best players at each position. But Ward’s Next Gen Stats coverage numbers took a nosedive in 2024, as he allowed 1.8 yards per coverage snap (last among outside corners with at least 300 coverage snaps that season) along with a higher-than-average 17.8% target rate. His yards per coverage snap returned to better than average in 2025 (1.0), though. But even if 2024 was a blip, Ward’s age and the team’s contractual control make this deal an unforced error. Making Ward the game’s highest-paid player at his position could also be problematic if the latest rankings from Pro Football Focus turn out to be accurate, as Dalton Wasserman has Ward listed at No. 20 : Ward’s production saw a bit of a dropoff in 2025 after he led the NFL with 17 pass breakups in 2024. He collected just one interception and four pass breakups last season, but Ward has an excellent track record that could foreshadow a bounce-back. He has long been up to the task of covering the NFL’s top wide receivers. So did the Browns overpay for Ward? It’s possible that they may come to regret the final year of the deal if Ward does slow down in 2029. But he is still one of the game’s top cornerbacks, which even Waserman highlighted in pointing out that Ward can still lock down the game’s best wide receivers. ( Just ask Ja’Marr Chase of the Cincinnati Bengals , who has had plenty of long afternoons when lining up against Ward.) #Browns CB Denzel Ward gets an interception during today's training camp practice. pic.twitter.com/J8y0IgcwI7 — Camryn Justice (@camijustice) August 7, 2026 The Browns also need leaders on the team, especially on the defensive side of the ball as they transition from defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz to Mike Rutenberg. Having Ward in the secondary to keep everyone on the same page should help that transition go a bit more smoothly. And while public perception does not factor into contract decisions, after trading Garrett, the Browns needed to give the fans something to hold on to, which is a bonus to keeping a popular player like Ward on the team. The bottom line is the Browns are better with Ward than without him, so even if the final year of the deal turns out to be a disappointing one, they should get plenty out of Ward over the next three seasons. What do you think? Did the Browns make a mistake by extending Ward, or was this the right move at the right time? Get the discussion going in the comments!

title: Browns’ new pass rusher Jared Verse ready to do his job, lead, and win
summary: The Cleveland Browns are rolling along with training camp, with plenty of new players and coaches from last year’s roster. Most notable of the missing is All-World pass rusher Myles Garrett. In his stead is the young Jared Verse, who was part of the trade for Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams. RELATED: TAKEAWAYS FROM […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns are rolling along with training camp, with plenty of new players and coaches from last year’s roster. Most notable of the missing is All-World pass rusher Myles Garrett. In his stead is the young Jared Verse, who was part of the trade for Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams. RELATED: TAKEAWAYS FROM VERSE PRESS CONFERENCE Verse has come out repeatedly and stated that he is not on the Browns roster to become Myles Garrett 2.0. He realizes that you can’t copy greatness. Instead, he wants the Cleveland fanbase to understand that he is a player with talent on his own accord. Not a copy of the original, but another original of a different breed. He has his own credentials and accolades. Verse is five years younger. He has some things that Garrett doesn’t, like the fact that Verse was named to the Pro Bowl in his first two years in the league. Garrett got his first Pro Bowl nod at the conclusion of his second year. Verse was crowned “NFL Rookie Defensive Player of the Year,” whereas Garrett was not. In their first two-year comparisons, Verse had more tackles and more drive-ending tackles. But again, Verse does not want to be compared to Garrett. Who would? Verse recently had a long conversation with Yahoo! Sports regarding him relocating from the Rams to the Browns, and talked with Jori Epstein. For starters, the trade rattled him a bit. “Getting that news, in a way, it kind of broke me and made me really sad. It sucked. It was a terrible feeling. But right after they told me, I locked back in.” Browns DE Jared Verse called trade from Rams upsetting but said he’s happy to be here and grateful Browns believe in him. pic.twitter.com/7mqP0yUvhF — Scott Petrak ct (@ScottPetrak) June 3, 2026 The Rams went all the way to the NFC Championship Game last season, losing to the eventual Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. Suddenly, he was on a plane to a club that had only won eight games in the past two seasons and had fired its head coach. Trading beaches, year-round sun, and Hollywood for Lake Erie, snow, and the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. But Verse knew that life goes on, and the NFL is a business. “There are a few moments in your life that genuinely sculpt you into who you are as a person. And I genuinely don’t want to overemphasize it. I mean, obviously I’m still alive today [and] it’s not the end of the world.” Verse came from a defensive unit that was ranked #17 overall to a club that has lived with its defensive progress ranked #4. Of course, this was the effort of former DC Jim Schwartz. In his place is Mike Rutenberg , who is not a Schwartz disciple. New head coach Todd Monken stated early that the defense would continue to flow along the Schwartz train, but so far, there have been quite a few changes in personnel. Including the addition of Verse. He believes he can make a difference in Cleveland while at the same time keeping the continuity of the defense’s ranking. “My job is to be the best me. I’ve told a thousand people, I’m not here to replace Myles. That’s not my job. It’s not my description. When I signed any contract, that’s not part of anything I signed.” Several months later, post-trade, OTAs and minicamps aside, Verse has spent quite a bit of time in the weight room and brought back one of his college trademarks: trash talking. As a rookie with the Rams, head coach Sean McVay jumped all over Verse about the habit, so he stopped the practice. But he hasn’t heard a note from Monken or DC Rutenberg or D-Line coach Jacques Cesaire for that matter. “If I beat you, you’re going to know about it. And then you’re going to receive advice.” But just because he beats a guy, or shows him up, does not mean he is doing his own salsa dance after getting to the quarterback in a black jersey. Recently, he beat rookie OT Spencer Fano and basically embarrassed the newbie. However, Verse remained after practice and summoned Fano. The two worked together so that Verse could explain what happened and guided the young tackle on how to use more inside leverage and athleticism against speedy rushers. The NFL is another level with much faster outside pass rushers. Including Verse. He not only used the time to show Fano several flaws in his pass protection, but he also gave him some advice and words of confidence. “I’m like, ‘Hey, man, you’re a very athletic tackle. When you go up against regular ends, you can do that move. But you got to face Trey Hendrickson this year. You got to face T.J. Watt and Josh Hines-Allen in your first game. These dudes are going to make you pay for it.” Verse has made a transition to the Browns’ way of attacking an offensive backfield. With the Rams, they were more about decisive pursuits, whereas Cleveland preaches an attack-style front that does not require a traditional read-and-react scheme. Coming to Cleveland, the Browns will use him as a pass rusher who has upper-body strength but brings 4.58 speed. It worked well with Garrett, and the coaching staff s ees Verse getting high sack and pressure numbers this year because the system boosts Verse’s sack objectives. LINK: GET TO KNOW JARED VERSE Cesaire spent 11 years in the NFL as a defensive end. He played in 125 games with 220 total tackles, 12.5 sacks, and 19 QB hits. He was one of Schwartz’s coaches who has remained on Monken’s staff. So, a lot of Schwartz’s techniques are being transferred through Cesaire. He has already been working on Verse’s moves and counter shifts. And the defensive line as a whole has been in a flux of improvement over the past few years that has now come to fruition: DT Mason Graham, DT Maliek Collins, DE Alex Wright, and now Verse. The backups have quality as well: Adin Huntington, Isaiah McGuire, Kalia Davis , Julian Okwara, and the jury is still out on former second-round pick Mike Hall. Verse stated: “I’m here now. Mason [Graham]’s a better player. We got (LB) Quincy Williams. We got all these dogs across the board. We got our DBs in the secondary getting paid. This is some dog work. I ain’t going to lie. I’m excited to see what happens.” The Browns actually can have a good win-loss record this year. They have the last-place schedule , so a lot of their games are against the lower half of the league. While they kick off the year with two playoff clubs from last year, Jacksonville and Tampa Bay, they play the New York Jets, Las Vegas Raiders, Tennessee Titans, New Orleans Saints, Atlanta Falcons, and the New York Football Giants. All bad teams from last year. Plus, the AFC North Division is no longer the toughest division in the NFL. Every team in the division is a coin flip and could become a split for the Browns, which would add three more wins to their final tally. Remember, last season the Cincinnati Bengals only won one more game than Cleveland, and the Baltimore Ravens went 8-9-0. No. 35 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @Browns DE Jared Verse! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/YyBgnxW2Hh — NFL (@NFL) August 5, 2026 “We’re not here to rebuild and tank for the No. 1 pick of whoever’s going to be up for quarterback or running back or wide receiver. We’re not tanking for any of that. It’s not like a rebuild year where we’re trying to go out there and get three wins, four wins, nothing like that. We’re here to win. I know a lot of people are like, ‘Oh, it’s the Browns. They got this, they got that. They lost Myles, who’s a great player.’ ” Vegas has the Browns’ win total projected at 5.5 games. Yes, the quarterback situation remains in flux , and that is a huge thing that will keep the win totals down. But Verse sees the talent. He sees an improved offense. He sees that the defense will carry on Schwartz’s direction. And he hopes that this year will become a special year for his teammates and the Browns fanbase. Every NFL season, four new clubs, on average, become new playoff teams from the year before. title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 36
summary: It is Day 36 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: (Original Caption) DALLAS, TEXAS-01/01/67-: Don Meredith (17) of the Dallas Cowboys, looks downfield for a pass receiver during NFL Pro title game against the Green Bay Packers. It is Day 36 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. We’re giving you an interesting one for Day 36 on our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit the first great heartbreak in Cowboys history. The Packers came to the Cotton Bowl to face Dallas in the 1966 NFL Championship Game, which was held on New Year’s Day 1967. The winner would represent the NFL in the first AFL-NFL World Championship Game, now known as Super Bowl I. Sunday, January 1, 1967 — 4:05 p.m. ET Cotton Bowl, Dallas, Texas Final Score: Green Bay Packers 34, Dallas Cowboys 27 Dallas, a seven-season expansion franchise, had never achieved a winning record or postseason appearance. However, under the guidance of Tom Landry, their young team went 10-3-1, clinched the Eastern Conference title, and earned the privilege of hosting Vince Lombardi’s defending champions, the Green Bay Packers. Green Bay arrived at 12-2, boasting a roster brimming with championship experience. While Dallas possessed talent, speed, and ambition, this was their first encounter with the immense pressure of contending for a league title. The difference in experience was immediately apparent. Green Bay opened with a touchdown drive, capped off by Bart Starr’s 17-yard pass to Elijah Pitts. On the ensuing kickoff, Packers rookie Jim Grabowski returned a fumble 18 yards for another touchdown, leaving Dallas trailing 14-0 despite not having run a single offensive play. The Cowboys’ resilience would eventually define the franchise, even though it could have overwhelmed a team making its first playoff appearance. After a 13-play possession directed by Don Meredith, Dan Reeves completed a three-yard touchdown run to tie the game at 14 before the first quarter ended. Dallas then attacked again, with Don Perkins breaking through for a 23-yard touchdown, erasing the entire deficit. The comeback showed Dallas belonged on the same field, but Starr kept finding ways to restore Green Bay’s advantage. Early in the second quarter, he struck Carroll Dale for a 51-yard touchdown. Meredith responded by moving Dallas deep into Packers territory, helped by a 40-yard completion to Reeves, but the drive stopped near the goal line. Danny Villanueva’s short field goal made it 21-17 rather than producing another tie. Dallas moved even closer in the third quarter. Warren Livingston recovered a fumble, and Meredith led another long possession before Villanueva hit another field goal from 32 yards. The Cowboys were now one point behind at 21-20, and the Cotton Bowl could sense the established champions beginning to feel real pressure from the league’s newest contender. Green Bay’s response was immediate. Starr completed a 40-yard pass to Dale and then found Boyd Dowler for a 16-yard touchdown, restoring an eight-point margin. In the fourth quarter, the Packers quarterback survived a fierce Dallas pass rush and converted a third-and-long with a 28-yard touchdown throw to Max McGee. Bob Lilly blocked the extra point, leaving the score at 34-20 and keeping Dallas within two touchdowns. The blocked kick mattered almost immediately. Facing third-and-20 on the next possession, Meredith went deep to Frank Clarke, who broke free for a 68-yard touchdown. Villanueva’s extra point cut the deficit to 34-27. A game that appeared to be slipping away had suddenly become another one-score fight. Dallas’ defense then gave the offense one final opportunity. Green Bay tried to run down the clock, but Dave Edwards sacked Starr, Willie Townes disrupted a screen and the Cowboys stopped Jim Taylor behind the line. A hurried Packers punt traveled only 17 yards, allowing Dallas to take possession at the Green Bay 47 with 2:12 remaining. Meredith found Clarke for 21 yards, Perkins added four more and a pass-interference penalty placed the ball at the Packers’ two-yard line. Dallas had four chances to score the touchdown that could have forced overtime. Instead, the opportunity slowly came apart. Reeves gained one yard, a false start pushed Dallas backward and another pass fell incomplete. A third-down completion moved the ball back to the two, leaving the season on one final snap. Green Bay linebacker Dave Robinson recognized the fourth-down rollout and attacked Meredith from behind. Robinson jammed Bob Hayes at the line, broke into the backfield and wrapped up the quarterback before he could properly deliver the ball. Meredith somehow released a desperate pass, but safety Tom Brown intercepted it in the end zone with 28 seconds remaining. Dallas had reached the doorstep of football history and finished two yards short. This game belongs on the countdown because it established both the promise and the pain that became intertwined with early Cowboys history. Dallas had gone from expansion irrelevance to within one play of defeating Lombardi’s Packers and reaching the first Super Bowl. The Cowboys proved they could compete with the NFL’s defining dynasty, but they also began building a reputation as a talented team that could reach the biggest stage without finishing the job. #Cowboys vs #Packers 1966 NFL Championship Game Cowboys first postseason game Final Score: Green Bay Packers 34, Dallas Cowboys 27 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/4sjsbWUUtq — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 8, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game This was the first postseason game in Dallas Cowboys history. The franchise had entered the NFL in 1960 and did not record its first winning season until going 10-3-1 in 1966. 1 00 , 99 , 98 , 97 , 96 , 95 , 94 , 93 , 92 , 91 , 90 , 89 , 88 , 87 , 86 , 85 , 84 , 83 , 82 , 81 , 80 , 79 , 78 , 77 , 76 , 75 , 74 , 73 , 72 , 71 , 70 , 69 , 68 , 67 , 66 , 65 , 64 , 63 , 62 , 61 , 60 , 59 , 58, 57, 56, 55 , 54 , 53 , 52, 51 , 50 , 49 , 48 , 47 , 46 , 45 , 44 , 43 , 42 , 41 , 40 , 39 , 38 , 37

summary: Is it possible we’re hyping Caleb Downs up too much? It is a legitimate question considering how absolutely giddy Dallas Cowboys fans have been about getting Downs in the draft. It felt mostly like a pipe dream before the draft, but now we are living in the reality. Downs has been called the best defensive […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - JULY 30: Caleb Downs #13 of the Dallas Cowboys during training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields on July 30, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images Is it possible we’re hyping Caleb Downs up too much? It is a legitimate question considering how absolutely giddy Dallas Cowboys fans have been about getting Downs in the draft. It felt mostly like a pipe dream before the draft, but now we are living in the reality. Downs has been called the best defensive player in the draft, one of the highest football IQ rookies in a long time, and various other accolades, even the lofty ‘generational player’. That’s a lot to heap upon a rookie. But we’re going to heap some more. We asked you where Downs would end up in the Defensive Rookie of the Year vote at the end of 2026. A majority of Cowboys fans (53%) think he will outright win it! Another 25% thought he would finish somewhere between third and fifth. Our partner, FanDuel, currently has the odds for Downs as DROY at +700. That places him third behind Rueben Bain Jr. (+450) and David Bailey (+500). Bonus question: Will Downs be the MVP of the Dallas defense? Or will someone else rise to the top? Let us know who you think the defensive MVP for Dallas will be. summary: The Dallas Cowboys held their annual Blue and White Scrimmage on Saturday. At one point during the scrimmage/broadcast team EVP Stephen Jones was being interviewed. He was discussing the state of the […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 09: Chief Operating Officer and Co-Owner Stephen Jones of the Dallas Cowboys before a NFL Preseason 2025 game between the Dallas Cowboys and Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on August 09, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys held their annual Blue and White Scrimmage on Saturday. If you are unaware this is just another training camp practice where the mothership has a broadcast that shows things happening throughout it. At one point during the scrimmage/broadcast team EVP Stephen Jones was being interviewed. He was discussing the state of the team’s roster and noted that they have done some small things over the course of camp, but he specifically said that he believed the 90-man roster would look different in the coming weeks. He went as far as saying that he would say this if he were a betting man. Jones kept it coy in terms of what kind of move could be on the way. He noted that the Cowboys are actively talking to other NFL teams as well as veteran free agents which could suggest a trade or free agent signing. Right after this point Stephen discussed the areas on the roster where he has seen the most intense roster battles. This answer was somewhat revealing relative to the previous one as he said that cornerback and linebacker are the two areas where they don’t necessarily have an incumbent. This is hardly breaking news to anybody who has been paying attention, but it does suggest more legitimately that this could be where the Cowboys look to make a move. Las Vegas Raiders pass rusher Maxx Crosby has been connected to a lot of rumors, but he doesn’t play either of those positions. Simply put, that isn’t where Dallas is most in need. Could the Cowboys look to trade for or sign a veteran at corner or linebacker? That certainly seems inevitable. Who would you want it to be?

The NFL is a what have you done for me lately league […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - JULY 30: Dak Prescott #4 of the Dallas Cowboys throws during training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields on July 30, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images Dak Prescott is coming off one of the best seasons of his career as his 4,552 yards in 2025 were his second-highest, and it was the third consecutive full season he’s played having 10 or fewer interceptions and 30 or more touchdown passes. The NFL is a what have you done for me lately league though, and every year a player’s résumé has to be updated. The Dallas Cowboys were able to keep George Pickens on the roster to be a duo with CeeDee Lamb, and Ryan Flournoy is poised to take a big leap in his third season. Practice makes perfect, and that’s what camp is about, fine-tuning things before the regular season. However, Prescott already looks like he’s in mid-season form going into his 11th campaign. Whether it’s been the deep ball, slants, crossing routes, out routes, or any other route you can think of, Prescott is throwing with accuracy and is placing the ball beautifully. He’s been on point with his top three targets, plus he and tight end Jake Ferguson look to be completely on the same page. Also, he and KaVontae Turpin have connected on some plays as well. CeeDee Lamb pic.twitter.com/2JKTV6Jbbv — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 6, 2026 George Pickens hauls in a difficult grab with Shavon Revel Jr. in coverage pic.twitter.com/00AxHLiUOB — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 6, 2026 iron sharpens iron. Ryan Flournoy just narrowly muscles this away from DaRon Bland on a frozen rope from Dak Prescott for the TD. #Cowboys pic.twitter.com/jwSX1832vT — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) August 3, 2026 Dak to Jake Ferguson TD pic.twitter.com/UK6OsN3MC4 — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) August 3, 2026 The Cowboys should be a lot better defensively under Christian Parker in 2026, especially with the talent they’ve added during the offseason via signings and the NFL draft. However, there’s still a lot of unknown, and that’s not that case with Prescott and the offense. He has years of continuity with his targets (and one full season with Pickens), and it’s showing out in Oxnard. Make no mistake about it, until further notice, the offense in Dallas is the driving force. Prescott has missed 25 games since the 2020 season. When healthy, he’s simply one of the best signal-callers in the game, and that won’t change if he’s upright in 2026. Prescott is at the point in his career where he’s totally comfortable and confident in his game, and when he’s on the field, the Cowboys are a playoff contender, every season. As camp rolls along, expect Prescott to continue looking sharp as the Cowboys’ offense looks to put together another year of high-powered production.

title: Why Cowboys training camp feels different in 2026

(Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 Dallas Cowboys team is just a week away from the start of their 2026 preseason schedule. As we near that date and the midway point of training camp, a couple of things seem to stand out as standards as the Cowboys go through camp. High intensity is here to stay Dallas started camp with a level of intensity that fans just haven’t seen in Oxnard in a while; even the practices without pads had some oomph. For an offense that still features plenty of players who played under former head coach Mike McCarthy, that physicality is particularly noticeable. McCarthy’s teams weren’t necessarily known for bringing that type of edge to training camp, making the change under the Cowboys’ current coaching staff a welcome development. Of course, intensity in training camp doesn’t automatically translate to success once the regular season begins, but for a team that has spent the offseason emphasizing toughness and accountability, seeing that mentality show up consistently on the practice field is encouraging. For Cowboys fans who have spent the past few seasons asking for a more physical identity, the early returns in Oxnard are certainly worth watching. Dak Prescott On The Defense's Intensity: "It Pisses Us Off a Little" pic.twitter.com/BfveaXS3YG — DLLS Cowboys (@DLLS_Cowboys) August 8, 2026 Hmm ok https://t.co/fINmJXNvsa — BGJ( The fatigued Cowboys CC) (@YaitesJames) August 5, 2026 Attention to detail is helping the defense The second noticeable theme has been the defense’s attention to detail. Rather than relying solely on individual talent to make plays, the Cowboys coaches have emphasized getting everyone to execute their assignments and communicate within the scheme. That is particularly important for a defense that underwent significant changes during the offseason. With new faces throughout the defense and a new defensive coordinator, building cohesion is just as important as generating splash plays everybody misses since Dan Quinn and Micah Parsons left. Training camp is where details are supposed to be cleaned up. When the pieces on defense and offense are executed correctly, the Cowboys can play faster because players aren’t thinking about where they’re supposed to be. title: Amongst an exciting rookie class, don’t forget about Malachi Lawrence
summary: On Thursday, we received our first dose of real football as the Hall of Fame game had a fantastic finish. What stood out was how impressive the rookies were during the contest. Carson Beck and Haynes King stole the show in their debuts for their teams. In just over a week, it’ll be Dallas’ turn […]
full_text: May 1, 2026; Frisco, TX, USA; Dallas Cowboys linebacker Malachi Lawrence (57) goes through a drill during practice at the Ford Center at the Star Training Facility in Frisco, Texas. Mandatory Credit: Chris Jones-Imagn Images | Chris Jones-Imagn Images On Thursday, we received our first dose of real football as the Hall of Fame game had a fantastic finish. What stood out was how impressive the rookies were during the contest. Carson Beck and Haynes King stole the show in their debuts for their teams. In just over a week, it’ll be Dallas’ turn to unveil their 2026 club against the defending champion Seattle Seahawks. While yes, the position battles will take center stage as one of the main storylines, we all want to see our rookies, right? We hope Dallas had a great draft class so it’s only right that the fans are anxious to see if that is true. It’s very plausible that their first pick, Caleb Downs, doesn’t play in that first game; as for the other rookies, if available, they likely will play. Aside from Downs, Dallas’ other first-round pick is flashing in training camp as well, and it’s only right that we praise how his training camp has unfolded. Malachi Lawrence my goodness pic.twitter.com/A1gN6XHJIm — FergSZN (@FergSZN) August 1, 2026 Malachia Lawrence is making strides Lawrence is a hyper-athletic pass rush prospect. He’s got a long frame, with elite closing speed once he gets to the edge. He’s also a polished player for his experience with a very good move set to rush the passer. Although the pass rush has been somewhat quiet to begin training camp, Lawrence has started to put together quality reps. He has been a little overshadowed by his other rookies on the roster such as Caleb Downs and Jaishawn Barham, but that doesn’t mean he doesnt command some attention. His head coach talked about his positive outlook on Lawrence before training camp: “I’ve been most pleasantly surprised by the instincts when he drops in coverage,” Schottenheimer said of Lawrence. “They didn’t drop him much at UCF, for the right reasons.” Despite not having much experience doing so, Lawrence actually has the ideal level of athleticism to be effective in coverage. The UCF product scored a near-perfect Relative Athletic Score , with Lawrence notching a 9.95 out of 10. Schotty has been encouraged by Lawrence’s work overall during his first offseason in the NFL and is a believer in the rookie, Jon Machota of The Athletic reports. “But I like the way he’s tackled this offseason. I think he’s another guy that the talent is real. I don’t remember him making a lot of mistakes, and that’s a good thing,” Schottenheimer added. Malachi Lawrence showing some bend coming around the corner pic.twitter.com/PF4R6blUKb — Mike Leslie (@MikeLeslieWFAA) August 7, 2026 Lawrence is starting to come on, and that shouldn’t really comes as a surprise. His traits are an ideal fit for the Cowboys defense as a stand-up edge rusher. Armed with his explosive first step, Lawrence has the potential to have a very good rookie season. Yet, for now, we’ll settle for Lawrence doing something exciting in Dallas first preseason game. With the Cowboys having to exhibit more from the pass rush, look for Lawrence to see a fair chunk of snaps against Seattle. Lawrence, Downs, and Barham spearhead what could be a very productive draft class for the Cowboys, with Lawrence having gone under the radar thus far behind Barham and Downs. Which other rookies are you most looking forward to seeing over the next few weeks and in the preseason?
