title: Cowboys rookies: How public assessments shifted as pads came on in Oxnard
summary: Evaluating NFL talent during the early days of training camp can be deceptive. Before the pads come on, assessments are often based on draft pedigree, athletic projections, positional versatility, and speculation about how a prospect might fit into the Cowboys’ plans. That changes when players finally have to play football in pads. Contact provides new […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 4: Anthony Smith #83 of the Dallas Cowboys catches the ball during training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields on August 4, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images Evaluating NFL talent during the early days of training camp can be deceptive. Before the pads come on, assessments are often based on draft pedigree, athletic projections, positional versatility, and speculation about how a prospect might fit into the Cowboys’ plans. That changes when players finally have to play football in pads. Contact provides new information: Can a linebacker diagnose and fill a gap against a real blocker? Can an edge rusher turn his athleticism into actual pressure? Can a receiver create separation against NFL defensive backs? Can a tight end contribute when blocking becomes part of the equation? Pads don’t necessarily tell us who can play. But they do give us an early indication of which traits survive the transition from theory to physical NFL football. For the Cowboys this year, the most interesting shifts include a major rise for Jaishawn Barham, a physical confirmation of Caleb Downs’ first-round billing, and a changing equation in the tight end room. Other rookies, meanwhile, have simply confirmed what we thought we knew before camp. Key takeaways from the first padded practices The first-rounders are mostly confirming the scouting reports. Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence have both provided evidence that their first-round billing wasn’t simply the product of draft speculation. Downs has shown the instincts and physicality to make an immediate impact in the secondary, while Lawrence’s explosiveness and ability to threaten the edge have continued to stand out once contact was introduced. In both cases, the padded practices have been more confirmation than revelation. The Barham surge. Jaishawn Barham is arguably the biggest positive storyline among the Cowboys’ rookies. The third-round linebacker entered camp competing for a role, but his instincts, speed and physicality have quickly translated into first-team opportunities. What looked like intriguing athletic upside before camp is beginning to look like a legitimate chance to contribute early. The tight end equation is getting more complicated. Michael Trigg entered camp as an intriguing receiving option in an unsettled TE3 competition. But once blocking became a bigger part of the evaluation, Brevyn Spann-Ford began attracting attention of his own, combining physicality as a blocker with the ability to make plays in the passing game. That doesn’t eliminate Trigg’s path to the roster, but it makes the competition more interesting. Anthony Smith is getting an opportunity. The Cowboys’ seventh-round receiver entered camp with an intriguing combination of size and athletic ability. His early flashes have given him an opportunity to compete for a place at the bottom of a crowded receiver room. The question now is whether those traits consistently translate against NFL competition. But not every assessment has changed. That’s also an important part of the story. Some rookies have provided exactly the kind of evidence we hoped to see; others have simply confirmed the pre-camp scouting report. And for many undrafted rookies, there simply isn’t enough public evidence yet to make a meaningful judgment. title: Cowboys news: Christian Parker’s communication is making a difference
summary: During the offseason, some of the biggest buzz surrounding the Dallas Cowboys has been the addition of defensive coordinator Christian Parker, and he’s already bringing a new aspect that’s making a difference. Going into his third season, Tyler Guyton hasn’t reached his potential yet, but Terence Steele says he’s on the right track. Dallas added […]
full_text: During the offseason, some of the biggest buzz surrounding the Dallas Cowboys has been the addition of defensive coordinator Christian Parker, and he’s already bringing a new aspect that’s making a difference. Going into his third season, Tyler Guyton hasn’t reached his potential yet, but Terence Steele says he’s on the right track. Dallas added a new running back to their roster on Friday, and a early roster projection came out after the first week of padded practices at training camp. Cowboys’ defense making progress, but they ‘haven’t been in the fire yet’ – Jon Machota, The Athletic Christian Parker is entering his first season calling plays as a defensive coordinator. However, the communication aspect of his philosophy is shining through already. “It’s loud in a good way,” Schottenheimer said. “There’s a lot of communication. I love what he says and how he refers to it as it’s two parts, giving and receiving. You just can’t be blurting out a bunch of stuff that doesn’t matter and confusing people. You got to give it, you got to receive it. Terence Steele speaks on Cowboys’ physicality, Tyler Guyton’s progress – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com Terence Steele talks about how being physical is what the Cowboys want to hang their hat on. Plus, he praised the progress of Guyton going into his third year. “[He’s handled it] like a true pro,” Steele said of Guyton’s demeanor and work ethic. “He could’ve gone a different way about it, but he did it the right way. I was with him a lot this offseason, and he put a lot of great work in. The dude works his butt off, so he came into this camp confident and he’s on his way.”I’m very proud of him. I’m very, very proud of him.” Cowboys roster projection 2.0: Training camp standouts, wild cards and more – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News The Cowboys had their first week of padded practices at training camp in Oxnard, California. Here’s a look at an early roster projection based on what’s been seen. Quarterback (2) Dak Prescott, Joe Milton III Notable cuts: Sam Howell Briefly: The Cowboys were hoping Joe Milton could take another step after an up-and-down first season in Dallas. It looks like he’s done it. Milton has had some good moments in camp. He’s also shown improvement with his touch on passes — he earned the nickname Bazooka Joe for a reason — and his time spent in the pocket. He’ll still escape a little early at times, but he’s looking to throw more than he did last season. Dallas Cowboys are hoping they hit lightning in a bottle with their latest roster move early in training camp – Mauricio Rodriguez, AtoZ Sports Dallas is still trying to figure out their depth at the running back position. On Friday, they signed Jashaun Corbin from the UFL. Corbin adds another body to Dallas RB room Corbin played at major college football programs between Texas A&M and Florida State. His best season came in 2021 at Florida State when he rushed for 887 yards and seven touchdowns, more than doubling his previous high of 401 rushing yards the season prior. Cowboys’ Prescott lands No. 31 on NFL’s Top 100, outside Top 5 QBs – Angel Torres, Cowboys Wire Dak Prescott had an amazing 2025 season despite the Cowboys not having team success. It landed him with a high ranking on the NFL’s top 100 list. Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott has landed inside the NFL’s annual Top 100 list, coming in at No. 31. This is the sixth-time the 11-year veteran has made the list and is his third-highest placement of his career. He was voted No. 14 his rookie season and No. 16 in 2024 after his NFL MVP runner-up season. What I know, what I think and what I don’t know at Dallas Cowboys training camp – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram The Cowboys have been out West for over a week for their 2026 training camp. Here’s a look at a few things that have come to light. The starting offensive line is set . Yes, there is an ongoing competition for the starting left tackle job, but head coach Brian Schottenheimer has said that Tyler Guyton has pulled away in that battle with Nate Thomas to calm any concerns the staff maybe had that Guyton wasn’t the right man for the job. In camp, Guyton has shown improvement with his hand placement and has married his lower body movement with his striking ability to guard the more athletic pass rushers on the other side of the ball. Daily discussion question: What are you most looking forward to from the Rams scrimmage?

title: Pat Bryant continues to make his case at Broncos training camp
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! Pat Bryant is having himself a training camp. The second-year Denver Broncos receiver is mentioned as one of the standout players from the media covering the practices on a daily basis. In fact, Bryant made the play of the day on Saturday. To have Bryant consistently showing up and showing out […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 26: Pat Bryant #13 of the Denver Broncos catches a pass for a second quarter touchdown under coverage by Trikweze Bridges #25 of the Dallas Cowboys at Empower Field at Mile High on October 26, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Pat Bryant is having himself a training camp. The second-year Denver Broncos receiver is mentioned as one of the standout players from the media covering the practices on a daily basis. In fact, Bryant made the play of the day on Saturday. To have Bryant consistently showing up and showing out at this stage is huge for him, the offense, and the Broncos. “I feel like that’s how you are successful in this league, focusing on that consistency,” Bryant said to the media on Friday after practice. “Honestly coming out here every day, working on my craft. As a receiver, you have to catch the ball, so I do that as much as I can.” Vance Joseph with HUGE praise for Pat Bryant. Said he’s the complete package. pic.twitter.com/S5rP7vIrjo — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 8, 2026 We all know the top two receivers in Denver are Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton. But there was question as to who would step into the No. 3 spot. Whether it was Bryant, Mavin Mims or Troy Franklin, those were the three guys vying to take that role. At this point, it’s Bryant. As defensive coordinator Vance Joseph said on Saturday after practice, Bryant is the “complete package.” But this will also drive rest of the receivers in that competition to up their game to keep pace with Bryant. “It’s healthy competition is what we like to call it,” he said to the media. “At the end of the day, everybody’s job is on the line, but to come out here and compete, push each other, make sure everybody’s doing their job, helping each other out when it’s needed. At the end of the day, we all have the same goal: let’s go out there and win.” Even Broncos head coach Sean Payton has noticed Bryant’s consistent and strong play. “(I’m) really pleased with how he’s doing,” Payton said to the media earleir this week. “He’s just one of those congested ball catchers. His feet stay on the ground. So when receivers catch the ball with their feet on the ground, they’re usually pretty good run after the catch. You don’t see him skipping in the air or jumping. That means he has a lot of confidence in catching this thing the right way. “I think in college in that final year (at Illinois), I think he had three walk-off touchdowns. Like literally last play of the game in-cuts where he caught it and didn’t … He was full stride when he caught it. If you’re breaking stride for a catch, there’s that tick of a second everyone gets a little bit of leverage on you. He’s extremely smart. He’s doing really well.” There is still a long ways to go for Bryant and the offense. But the fact the young receiver is making the strides he is at this point in his second year is a positive sign. To have a strong No. 3 wide out in this offense for Bo Nix will only make that unit better and harder to defend. “Just going into Year 2 in the offense, I feel like I kind of understand things a little bit differently,” Bryant said to the media. “Then just my ability last year, I played just about every position, so it kind of helped me going into this year. Whenever a guy’s tired during camp, I’ll go out there and take a rep because at the end of the day, I know my job being Year 2 in this offense.” Horse Tracks

In today’s camp report, we have Pat Bryant really establishing himself as the Broncos WR and a trusted […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL, CO - AUGUST 7: Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph of the Denver Broncos walks the field before practice on Friday, August. 7, 2026, at Broncos Park in Centennial, Colo.(Photo by Timothy Hurst/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) | Denver Post via Getty Images Scrimmage Day! Pat Bryant’s time is now One constant throughout the first week or so of Broncos Camp has been the play of second-year wide receiver Pat Bryant. He showed flashes of his talent late last season before injuries derailed his rookie year, but he has carried that momentum into the early portions of training camp. Today, with Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims sidelined, Bryant stepped up and was the Broncos’ top playmaker and Bo Nix’s most trusted target throughout practice, including what some are calling the best play of camp thus far. During a team drill, Bo Nix was under heavy pressure and threw an absolute dime to Pat Bryant, who was in double coverage for a touchdown. When Nix needed a play today, Bryant was his go-to guy, much like how Courtland Sutton has been in the past. He had 5 or 6 catches in practice today according to reports, so he was heavily involved. Play of the day: Bo Nix under heavy pressure, tosses up a ball into the back of the end zone (from the right red zone) and drops it right into an impossible bucket to Pat Bryant in double coverage who catches it. Arguably the play of camp. — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 8, 2026 After practice, defensive coordinator Vance Joseph was asked about Pat Bryant, and he told reporters that Bryant is the “Complete package” . He added that Bryant “blocks and catches the ball in traffic,” goes up and gets the ball vertically, is great in the red zone, has great size, and has just been playing well all camp. He noted it has been a challenge for him and the defense to cover Bryant, but this is good for the team as a whole. From the start, Bryant was my favorite to win the WR3 role, and so far, he has not disappointed. Every practice, he is making plays, and as Joseph noted, he is the complete package. One of the more reliable pass catchers on the team, a great blocker, he gets open, and while he doesn’t have Jaylen Waddle or Mims-like speed, he plays faster than his 40-time. If he can stay healthy, I believe he is going to have an excellent season for the Broncos and potentially even push veteran Courtland Sutton for snaps as the season progresses. I am high on Bryant, and I am excited to see what he can do moving forward. Remember the name, Pat Bryant. Jonah Coleman continues to turn heads Jonah Coleman will be a playmaker for the Broncos this year. The Broncos rookie back had an excellent practice today and showcased why the team drafted him early in the 4th round. Outside of veteran JK Dobbins, Coleman has become the Broncos’ best between-the-tackles runner on the team during camp, and could see himself having a large role in this offense this upcoming season. Jonah Coleman is having a great practice. A number of good runs between the tackles, highlighted by a high-effort touchdown run in the tight red zone. — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 8, 2026 As DNVR’s Zac Stevens notes, Coleman had several good runs between the tackles, including a high-effort touchdown during a tight red zone period. This is where Coleman thrived in college, and where he will likely thrive again in the NFL. Add in his ability to catch the ball out of the backfield and pass block, and you can see a larger-than-expected role for Coleman this season. He thrives in areas that second-year back RJ Harvey struggled last season (between the tackles) and could push for the RB2 role. Now, this isn’t a knock on Harvey, who has thrived as a pass catcher, but the two have different strengths and weaknesses. All three backs will contribute this season, but it will be interesting to see how they make it work. I wouldn’t be surprised if Dobbins and Coleman rotate a bit as ball carriers, while Harvey is your 3rd-down/pass-catching back who fills in as a change-of-pace guy. That’s just my guess right now on August 8th, but certainly something to watch moving forward. Coleman is going to push his way into this backfield conversation one way or another. Uwazurike impressing One of the more surprising and exciting bright spots of camp has been the play of large defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike. He turned himself into an important rotational run defender last season, but after working on his body some this offseason, he has become “a pass rusher” according to defensive coordinator Vance Joseph. Enyi Uwazurike has been outstanding the past two days, according to Vance Joseph. — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 8, 2026 Joseph told reporters that Uwazurike has “changed his body” and “leaned out” and mentioned how he plays all over the defensive line. He added Enyi has “fixed his body” and that has changed the player. He said Uwazurike has always been a run stopper, but now he is a pass rusher. He added Uwazurike has been “dominant the past two days” and has been fun to watch. Later in the presser, he noted Enyi, including Tyler Onyedim and Sai’vion Jones, will factor in replacing John Franklin-Myers, but it sure sounds like Uwazurike might be that guy right now. He has the excellent size and length you look for, plus elite strength. If he can add some pass-rush to that, which it sounds like he has, he could have a Chris Jones-like impact on this defense. That’s a high mark, but at 6-6 and 320 pounds with athleticism and pass rush potential, good luck blocking that. On top of that, he will likely be getting a lot of one-on-one blocks with Zach Allen, Malcolm Roach, Nik Bonitto, Jonathon Cooper, Jonah Ellis, Que Robinson, and others playing alongside him. I am excited about the potential and can’t wait to see how Enyi looks this upcoming season. title: Broncos sign WRs Kyre Duplessis and Kyrese Rowan
summary: The Broncos are a little bit banged up at the wide receiver position. Star receiver Jaylen Waddle suffered some sort of strain, according to head coach Sean Payton, and is expected to be back in about “4 to 5 days”. Not the end of the world, but likely sidelines him into next week and for […]
full_text: August 9, 2025; Santa Clara, California, USA; Denver Broncos wide receiver Kyrese Rowan (39) before the game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kyle Terada-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Broncos are a little bit banged up at the wide receiver position. Star receiver Jaylen Waddle suffered some sort of strain, according to head coach Sean Payton, and is expected to be back in about “4 to 5 days”. Not the end of the world, but likely sidelines him into next week and for the Broncos preseason opener on Friday Night. Then, at the end of Friday’s practice, Marvin Mims Jr. suffered some sort of lower body injury. He pulled up from a route and immediately went off to the field with a trainer before going back to the locker room. No word on the extent of the injury, but he’s likely sidelined for a little bit at least. So, with the wide receiver room looking a little thin, the team added some depth. They announced that they have signed undrafted rookie wide receiver Kyre Duplessis. The Denver Post’s Luca Evans is reporting that the team is also signing Kyrese Rowan , who spent time with the team last season. We've signed WR Kyre Duplessis. 📰 » https://t.co/LX6ORgJcys pic.twitter.com/dsjuCK4v4t — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) August 7, 2026 Both players were brought in for tryouts during Friday’s practice, and Duplessis looked the best and was signed by the Broncos. However, after Mims went down with the injury, the team called Kyrese Rowan, who had already flown back home, to come back to Denver because they wanted to sign him too . He is expected to have his physical this morning and then officially sign with the team soon after. Rowan was invited to the Broncos’ rookie minicamp last season after he went undrafted and then unsigned during the UDFA signing period. He impressed the Broncos coaches enough that they decided to sign him to their 90-man roster. However, he was among their final cuts, and they decided not to sign him to their practice squad at that time. His story does not end there because in October, Rowan was signed to the Broncos’ practice squad, where he stayed until December, when he was released to make room for Elijah Moore. A week later, Rowan was back on the Broncos’ practice squad. He did not receive a futures deal from the team and remained unsigned throughout the offseason. Now, with the Broncos needing some depth at the wide receiver position, Rowan is back with the team. As for Duplessis, he is an undrafted rookie out of Coastal Carolina and Delaware who has spent time with the Detroit Lions and Seattle Seahawks this offseason. The 5-11, 193-pound receiver brings 4.6 speed and some return experience to the Broncos while also adding some backend depth to their wide receiver room. Realistically, both players are camp bodies needed to get through the remaining training camp practices and their three preseason games. It looks unlikely that Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims will play in the opener, and beyond that is up in the air right now. It also seems unlikely that veteran Courtland Sutton will play much at all this preseason as well. So, the Broncos need to add some depth to their receiver room for the second half of these preseason games. Both players will have an opportunity to impress the Broncos coaches and push for a spot on their practice squad, but even that seems like a long shot currently.

title: Ja’Quan McMillian relishes opportunity to make big plays as Broncos’ nickelback
summary: The Denver Broncos sport of the best secondaries in the National Football League. The starting outside duo of Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss get most of the press clippings. However, nickelback Ja’Quan McMillian has been instrumental to the revitalization of the franchise’s defense the past several seasons. Undrafted out of East Carolina, the Broncos […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - JANUARY 17: Ja'Quan McMillian #29 of the Denver Broncos celebrates during an NFL divisional playoff football game against the Buffalo Bills at Empower Field At Mile High on January 17, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos sport of the best secondaries in the National Football League. The starting outside duo of Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss get most of the press clippings. However, nickelback Ja’Quan McMillian has been instrumental to the revitalization of the franchise’s defense the past several seasons. Undrafted out of East Carolina, the Broncos signed McMillian after the conclusion of the 2022 NFL Draft. He impressed in training camp as a rookie but failed to make the final 53-man roster. After a long wait on the team’s practice squad, the feisty corner played in Denver’s final game of the season against the Los Angeles Chargers. It wasn’t just spot duty; McMillian played every single snap. Since then, the fifth-year pro has been a mainstay for the Broncos’ defense and performed at a high level. His ability to create turnovers has been a standout quality, something Head Coach Sean Payton made note of recently. “I see someone who’s really good at taking the ball away, I see football I.Q. Then someone who’s playing with good leverage. It’s easy to say, ‘Take it away,’ but sometimes if you’re not in a position, you’re just catching up, trying to make a tackle. He’s a great study,” emphasized Payton who believes other players can learn alot by studying McMillian’s playstyle and penchant for turnovers. Over the past three seasons, McMillian boasts six interceptions during the regular season. Two of them have been returned the distance for touchdowns. Additionally, he has forced five fumbles and recovered two of them. Whenever the Broncos have needed a game-changing play, more often than not, it has been McMillian who has answered the call. Just take a look back at his impressive interception versus Josh Allen in the AFC Divisional Playoff victory over the Buffalo Bills as a prime example. It doesn’t get more clutch than that. The Broncos likely don’t win the game without that happening. Yesterday after practice, McMillian talked about why he is seemingly a magnet for the football on the gridiron. “I think it’s both. The more you work on it, taking the ball away, we do turnover drills, that helps. I think a lot of it is something that’s just in the player. I’ve been doing it my whole career at every level. The ball just finds me, and I just do my job. I just happen to be in the right spot,” stated McMillian who acknowledged instincts and learned skills help with his ability to create turnovers. Life as a quarterback in the NFL is tough, but McMillian has held up tremendously. He may not be the most targeted player in Denver’s secondary—but when the ball does come his way—the opposition isn’t having much luck. Since the 2023 season, he touts a staunch 52-percent completion percentage. That’s one of the best in the league. “Communication wise, just being that leader on the field, or getting everybody in position, getting the calls to the to the back end of defense, the linebackers, I think it’s a fun thing,” mentioned McMillian on what he enjoys about playing the nickel spot in Vance Joseph’s defense. “There are a lot of plays you can make in there, blitzing the quarterback, making tackles in the run game, covering, making plays on the balls in every which way. Just being a leader to the guys and being a controller of the back end.” Earlier in the week, defensive lineman Zach Allen praised McMillian as the player that gets the Broncos’ defense going. That’s quite the statement considering how many incredible players the team has on that side of the ball. Going from an undrafted free agent to one of the league’s most underrated defenders has been quite the journey for McMillian, who is playing this year on a second-round RFA tender. While McMillian’s future beyond the 2026 season with the Broncos remains uncertain, the high-profile nickelback hasn’t been shy about his desires. He wants to play for Denver for his entire career. He credits Joseph for helping forge him into one of the league’s top defensive playmakers and hopes their relationship can continue for years to come. “He’s meant a lot to me. I obviously had a different defensive coordinator the first year I was on practice squad. When he came in, I end up making the team. The way he goes about his day, the team, the aggression, he liked to play with the aggressive style. That’s how I like to play, aggressive and physicality. I love ‘VJ’, and our relationship has grown over the years and hope it still continues to grow.”
author: Christopher Hart

title: The Super Bowl 50 trophies nobody talks about
summary: As fans gear up for what everyone in Broncos Country hopes will be another historic Super Bowl run, I got to thinking about the additional hardware that the Broncos picked up following their Super Bowl 50 run. What I am talking about are the gold 5 and 0 that accompany the Lombardi trophy from that […]
full_text: SAN FRANCISCO, CA - FEBRUARY 08: The Super Bowl trophy and the Super Bowl 50 MVP trophy was on display during the presentation for the MVP at the Moscone Center West on February 8, 2016 in San Francisco, California. Von Miller #58 of the Broncos was the games MVP. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images As fans gear up for what everyone in Broncos Country hopes will be another historic Super Bowl run, I got to thinking about the additional hardware that the Broncos picked up following their Super Bowl 50 run. What I am talking about are the gold 5 and 0 that accompany the Lombardi trophy from that Super Bowl in just about every picture since the win. Plenty of teams win Super Bowls. Only the Broncos got multiple trophies for doing so. #SB50 pic.twitter.com/nOIpfQr9DD — Andrew Mason (@MaseDenver) April 28, 2016 Sure, leading up to Super Bowl 50, everyone saw these gold numerals with the Lombardi at various press conferences and whatnot, arranged proportionally to match the logo from that Super Bowl. There was never any indication they would be awarded alongside the Lombardi and, during the trophy presentation, the numbers were not part of the ceremony. So what, exactly, are they? Wikipedia says : In addition to the Vince Lombardi Trophy that all Super Bowl champions receive, the Broncos also received a large, 18-karat gold-plated “50”. Each digit weighs 33 lb (15 kg) for a total of 66 lb (30 kg). Like the Lombardi Trophy, the “50” was designed by Tiffany & Co. So how did they go from press conference display pieces to prominent components of the Broncos trophy display case? Well, that’s a great question, because internet research and AI assistance don’t provide a clear answer. Like I said, they weren’t a part of the postgame presentation and they don’t appear in any of the clips online during the parade or rally. In fact, the first time (that I can find) that they were seen, not in a promotional context and with the Broncos organization, was during the end-of-year press conference with legendary Broncos Gary Kubiak and John Elway. They are currently behind glass in the Broncos trophy case labeled “Super Bowl Trophy and Lombardi Trophy.” Probably the only time in the history of football, past or future, that the Lombardi trophy gets second billing. These bonus trophies clearly were handed off sometime between the end of the trophy presentation and that press conference. One wonders if someone with the NFL saw them and wondered, “What am I going to do with these?” and sent them to Denver. It’s also entirely possible there was more than one set made since the NFL’s golden anniversary was such a big deal. If so, where are those? The Hall of Fame in Canton, Ohio seems like a logical choice, but research and AI are unable to confirm or disconfirm. So, Broncos Country, that Super Bowl 50 win got us not only a Lombardi, but two bonus trophies that are pretty awesome in their own right. No other team has ever received bonus trophies for winning a Super Bowl and so, if you ask me, that is just another reason why the Denver Broncos are the best team in the NFL… bur do we need any more reasons? If you know anything about these bonus trophies, please share in the comments!

title: Detroit Lions try out three defensive players
summary: On Friday, the Detroit Lions tried out a trio of defensive players: defensive tackle Folorunso Fatukasi, and cornerbacks Ryan Cooper and Anthony Kendall. As of Saturday morning, none of the three have signed with the team, but we’ll see if Detroit makes a move during their day off in preparation for Sunday’s training camp practice. […]
full_text: Jacksonville Jaguars defensive tackle Folorunso Fatukasi (94) greets defensive end Dawuane Smoot (91) Dawuane Smoot during training camp Monday, Aug. 7, 2023 at Miller Electric Center at EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville, Fla. This was the 11th day of training camp. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co On Friday, the Detroit Lions tried out a trio of defensive players: defensive tackle Folorunso Fatukasi, and cornerbacks Ryan Cooper and Anthony Kendall. As of Saturday morning, none of the three have signed with the team, but we’ll see if Detroit makes a move during their day off in preparation for Sunday’s training camp practice. Fatukasi is an eight-year veteran with 90 games and 64 starts of experience. Though he lost most of his 2025 season to a shoulder injury, he started a combined 55 games in the previous four seasons. At 6-foot-4, 318 pounds, Fatukasi is a capable nose tackle who, at his peak, posted some of the best PFF run defense grades in football (81.6 in 2019, 80.1 in 2020). However, he has not graded out paritcularly well in that category as of late (61.0 in 2023, 32.4 in 2024). Detroit could be in the market for a nose tackle type of player, depending on the reason for Aidan Keanaaina’s absence during Friday’s practice. At this point, it’s not entirely clear if he’s even dealing with an injury. Cooper went undrafted in 2024, bounced around a handful of teams over the past two years, and spent last season playing cornerback for the UFL’s Birmingham Stallions. There he posted 25 tackles, four pass breakups, and an interception in nine game appearances. COOPER PICKS IT ‼️🔥 pic.twitter.com/G5NggFmnsA — Birmingham Stallions (@UFLStallions) May 23, 2026 Kendall went undrafted in 2023, and played for two seasons with the Tennessee Titans—making all 16 of his NFL game appearances during his rookie season as a core special teamer (323 snaps). He has yet to make the field since, despite stints on the Ravens practice squad and the training camp roster with the Browns in 2025. Kendall was a small-school prospect, playing cornerback at Baldwin Wallace in college. He’s put up decent athletic scores and production in his final year in college: 15 pass breakups, three interceptions, 56 tackles, and four tackles for loss.

title: Discussion: What should the Detroit Lions do with rookie QB Luke Altmyer?
summary: For the past two Detroit Lions training camp practices, veteran backup quarterback Teddy Bridgewater has been sidelined. At this point, we don’t have any clarity on why Bridgewater has been absent, but it’s been a great opportunity for undrafted rookie quarterback Luke Altmyer to get a ton of reps—including some key situational work. During Friday’s […]
full_text: Detroit Lions quarterback Luke Altmyer (2) practices during mini camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Wednesday, June 17, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co For the past two Detroit Lions training camp practices, veteran backup quarterback Teddy Bridgewater has been sidelined. At this point, we don’t have any clarity on why Bridgewater has been absent, but it’s been a great opportunity for undrafted rookie quarterback Luke Altmyer to get a ton of reps—including some key situational work. During Friday’s scrimmage-like practice, Altmyer even got to run the second-team offense against the first-team defense several times—a phenomenal opportunity to get reps against the best defensive players the Lions have to offer. It’s been a pretty impressive camp for Altmyer. Nothing seems too big for him; his accuracy and arm strength have been more than acceptable, and practice hasn’t slowed down at all with Bridgewater absent. While Friday’s scrimmage wasn’t Altmyer’s best day , it was undoubtedly his biggest learning experience, and one he’ll be better off for down the line. Going into training camp, I didn’t think there was much question that Altmyer would be heading for the practice squad this year to continue his development. But I’m starting to wonder if I should reconsider that position. Today’s Question of the Day is: What should the Lions do with Luke Altmyer? My answer: Let me be clear: I am not suggesting Altmyer should be this team’s Week 1 backup quarterback. While I’ve been impressed with Altmyer, being one Jared Goff injury away from starting an undrafted rookie is just not a good idea for a team with Super Bowl aspirations. Admittedly, Bridgewater hasn’t been overly impressive in camp, but he’s undoubtedly got a better handle on the offense and will avoid all the mental errors that Detroit would risk by unfairly putting Altmyer out there. But I am starting to consider the possibility of keeping three quarterbacks on the roster. Altmyer has been impressive enough for me to believe that a long-term backup quarterback role could be in his future, and Detroit may not want to risk losing a developmental player like that to waivers. I may make that move in next week’s Bubble Watch. However, before I completely fall in line with that thinking, the preseason will be critical for Altmyer. If he can continue the path he’s currently on, he may not give the Lions much of a choice—especially with all of his film out there for everyone to see. If he shows some of the rookie mistakes that are more than common, maybe the Lions can get by waiving him and signing him to the practice squad. Point being: Altmyer is already making this an interesting conversation. I know most of you haven’t seen Altmyer play yet, but what are your thoughts? Would you be okay if the Lions kept three quarterbacks? Can Altmyer actually contend for the backup job? Or do the Lions simply need to invest more heavily in the backup job? title: Detroit Lions fans hope to see starters vs. Bengals… but not much of them
summary: Earlier this week, we published our latest SB Nation Reacts survey, sponsored by the folks at FanDuel Sportsbook, and asked Detroit Lions fans: How much should Lions’ starters play in the first preseason game? The Lions will be traveling to Cincinnati next Thursday night to take on the Bengals in both teams’ first preseason game of […]
full_text: Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell watches drills during Rookie Minicamp Saturday, May 13, 2023. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Earlier this week, we published our latest SB Nation Reacts survey, sponsored by the folks at FanDuel Sportsbook , and asked Detroit Lions fans: How much should Lions’ starters play in the first preseason game? The Lions will be traveling to Cincinnati next Thursday night to take on the Bengals in both teams’ first preseason game of 2026. Detroit has taken a back-to-basics approach to the offseason, and through the first 10 days of training camp, they’ve stayed true to their words. However, coach Dan Campbell said that while he would like to play his starter in the preseason, he has yet to make a decision on that matter. While Campbell is still debating playing his starters against the Bengals, Lions fans have weighed in on the topic: A whopping 95% of the fan base would like to see the Lions starters play a quarter of the game or less, with the majority of fans looking for them to play just a series or two. Just one percent of the voters are hoping to not see the starters at all. Let’s take a look at the comment section of our original article and The Feed post to see fans’ explanations for their selections (lightly edited for clarity). Professor Holmes : “A series or two is what I would prefer. Coach C should know best, though.” Itsbeen55years : “1 or 2 series at most…. but I think the O-line should be out for a quarter or so. I know it’s risky, but I would love to see the O-line in sync with each other for the start of the season.” Defend The Den : “A series or 2 should be enough for the starters to get their feet wet, while also limiting their risk for injury. The majority of the game should be for evaluating the roster bubble players and getting the new faces some live game team chemistry.” Schmipper: “Starters need to play. New coaches, new schemes, new personnel. I say one quarter for the first game and go from there.” Marvol : “Full quarter in the first 2 games. If they score twice before the quarter ends, take them out. Defense plays a whole quarter unless they get 2 three-and-outs back to back.” As a reminder, this survey was sponsored by the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook , who currently have the Lions listed as +1900 to win this year’s Super Bowl, +900 to win the NFC Championship, and +150 to win the NFC North as the current favorites. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in Detroit Lions fans and fans across the country. If you want to receive these surveys by email weekly, you can sign up here .

title: Green Bay Packers Roster: Post-Family Night 53-man projection
summary: We’re only about a week into padded practices, so I don’t want to make too big of a deal about what’s happened in the Green Bay Packers’ training camp so far, but we have gotten a couple of hints at how the team’s Week 1 roster will shake out. Between the Family Night stream and […]
full_text: Green Bay Packers tight end Messiah Swinson (48) dives for a pass in the end zone during Family Night on Saturday, August 2, 2025, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wis. Tork Mason/USA TODAY NETWORK-Wisconsin | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co We’re only about a week into padded practices, so I don’t want to make too big of a deal about what’s happened in the Green Bay Packers’ training camp so far, but we have gotten a couple of hints at how the team’s Week 1 roster will shake out. Between the Family Night stream and the reports from practice, some position groups that once appeared to be fairly wide open now consistently have the same small group of players breaking into playing time with first-team units. So after Family Night, this is my best guess at how the Packers’ 2026 roster will shake out. Quarterback Jordan Love Tyrod Taylor So far, there haven’t been many opportunities for Kyle McCord and rookie Kyron Drones to play with the second-team offense in training camp. At this point, Jordan Love is the clear number-one quarterback and Tyrod Taylor is the clear number-two quarterback, with McCord and Drones splitting time with the third-team offense. Running Back Josh Jacobs MarShawn Lloyd Chris Brooks Both Josh Jacobs and Chris Brooks are dealing with what have been described as short-term injuries, but if either isn’t ready to go in the regular season, expect Pierre Strong Jr., who is getting most of the reps as the next man up behind the Packers’ top trio, to start pushing into the rosterable conversation. Receiver Christian Watson Matthew Golden Jayden Reed Savion Williams Bo Melton Skyy Moore General manager Brian Gutekunst came out strongly for receiver/returner Skyy Moore in his first press conference since the pads came on, stating that he “expects” Moore to contribute to the team in 2026. There’s still time for Isaiah Neyor, who drew praise from head coach Matt LaFleur this summer, or rookie UDFA J. Michael Sturdivant to make up ground, but it seems Moore has the edge right now for the sixth receiver spot. For what it’s worth, Moore’s snaps with the first-team offense on Family Night exclusively came from the slot, so he’d be Jayden Reed’s backup on offense. Tight End Tucker Kraft Josh Whyle Drake Dabney The one injury suffered this offseason that might be a long-term issue for the Packers is to tight end Luke Musgrave, who is working through a neck injury. When Green Bay’s decision-makers have spoken about Musgrave’s availability, they’ve spoken in vague, longer-term timelines. It wouldn’t surprise me (NOT A DOCTOR) if Musgrave started the regular season on the PUP list. Right now, the next man up is Drake Dabney, who has been primarily playing the Y position in camp (with Tucker Kraft also sidelined for team drills) and was called one of the team’s most improved players by offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich in his opening press conference of training camp. Offensive Line Jordan Morgan (LT) Aaron Banks (LG) Sean Rhyan (C) Anthony Belton (RG/T) Zach Bako-Bewele (RT) Darian Kinnard (T) Jacob Monk (G/C) Jager Burton (G/C) Donovan Jennings (G) John Williams (C/G/T) The Packers’ preferred offensive line clearly seems to be Jordan Morgan, Aaron Banks, Sean Rhyan, Anthony Belton and Zach Bako-Bewele (left to right). Behind them, the top backups in the first-team rotation in camp have been Darian Kinnard, Jacob Monk and Jager Burton, with Donovan Jennings surprisingly getting some first-team snaps over Travis Glover, who the team seemed high on going into last season prior to his season-ending shoulder injury. Now, John Williams’ versatility of playing all five offensive line positions might leave Glover on the outside looking in, if the team keeps just 10 offensive linemen on their Week 1 roster. Defensive Line Devonte Wyatt Javon Hargrave Karl Brooks Chris McClellan Warren Brinson Nazir Stackhouse Jordon Riley is going to start (and maybe end) the season on the PUP list after tearing his Achilles late in the 2025 season. For the most part, the four defensive linemen behind Devonte Wyatt and Javon Hargrave in the pecking order have filled in the majority of the first-team reps on defense while Wyatt and Hargrave have been continuing to rehab their knee injuries this summer. The sleeper here is Anthony Campbell, who has been making some noise in camp by racking up pass breakups and chasing down Tyrod Taylor from behind on “sacks.” Keep an eye out for him in the preseason. Edge Defender Lukas Van Ness Barryn Sorrell Brenton Cox Jr. Dani Dennis-Sutton Collin Oliver Micah Parsons is going to start the year on the PUP list and miss at least the first four weeks of the regular season, and it seems pretty clear at this point that the Packers’ top five edge rushers will be Lukas Van Ness, Barryn Sorrell, Brenton Cox Jr., Dani Dennis-Sutton and Collin Oliver. The team might have to drop one of them when Parsons returns, but that’s what it’s looking like for Week 1. Linebacker Zaire Franklin Edgerrin Cooper Isaiah McDuffie Ty’Ron Hopper Nick Niemann This is another group that seems pretty locked in, barring injury. Nick Niemann, who is on the team more for his special teams ability than his defensive depth, is even getting first-team reps with the punt team (probably the most important unit, in terms of a “starting job” translating to a roster spot) in camp. Quay Walker is out after signing with the Las Vegas Raiders in free agency, and Zaire Franklin, who the Packers traded for from the Indianapolis Colts, is in. Otherwise, Green Bay is running it back in 2026. Cornerback Keisean Nixon Carrington Valentine Brandon Cisse Benjamin St-Juste Domani Jackson An open-ended question here is whether the Packers will keep five or six cornerbacks on the team, with Domani Jackson and Kamal Hadden being the potential fifth or sixth cornerbacks on the roster. So far, neither has practiced in team drills during training camp, though, so it’s difficult to know where they stand. Jackson suffered an injury this offseason while Hadden is coming off two fractures in his leg, an ankle dislocation and also dislocated his pinky in training camp. Safety Xavier McKinney Evan Williams Javon Bullard Kitan Oladapo Johnathan Baldwin Without Zayne Anderson, who signed with the Miami Dolphins in free agency, the Packers have room to keep Johnathan Baldwin, who is currently the backup slot defender behind Javon Bullard. Previously, Kitan Oladapo had played limited slot reps for Green Bay, but it now looks like Oladapo has been passed over by Baldwin (in the slot but not at safety), which could be enough for Baldwin to make the team. Specialist K: Trey Smack P: Daniel Whelan LS: Matt Orzech There’s only one kicker and one punter in camp, so it doesn’t take a rocket scientist to figure out those positions for the Packers. Currently, Matt Orzech is dealing with a calf injury, which led to the signing of veteran long snapper Cal Adomitis. If any spot is up for grabs, it’s Adomitis making the most of his opportunity while Orzech has been sidelined. — Let us know what you think of this projection, or what you would change about it, in the comments section. title: Colts legendary PK Adam Vinatieri enshrined into football immortality
summary: On Saturday, former legendary Indianapolis Colts placekicker was enshrined into football immortality in Canton, Ohio, as part of the Pro Football Hall of Fame’s Class of 2026: You can find Vinatieri’s entire Pro Football Hall of Fame speech here, which included humorous quips regarding his former New England Patriots head coach Bill Belichick, as well […]
full_text: CANTON, OHIO - AUGUST 08: Adam Vinatieri speaks during the 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame Enshrinement Ceremony at Tom Benson Hall Of Fame Stadium on August 08, 2026 in Canton, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Saturday, former legendary Indianapolis Colts placekicker was enshrined into football immortality in Canton, Ohio, as part of the Pro Football Hall of Fame’s Class of 2026: Vinny’s first look at his HOF bust. 👀 @ProFootballHOF Enshrinement on ESPN/NFLNStream on @NFLPlus and ESPN App pic.twitter.com/V6zpvShF3L — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) August 8, 2026 You can find Vinatieri’s entire Pro Football Hall of Fame speech here , which included humorous quips regarding his former New England Patriots head coach Bill Belichick, as well as his All-Pro special teams mate Pat McAfee. While fellow Hall of Famer, and his former general manager Bill Polian, presented him with his gold jacket on Friday night, it was Colts team owner and CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon, who was his presenter on Saturday, as a token of Vinatieri’s appreciation for her late father Jim Irsay and what his family did for him throughout his illustrious pro kicking career. A number of Vinatieri’s former Colts teammates were in attendance for his enshrinement including fellow Pro Football Hall of Famers Peyton Manning and Dwight Freeney, his Hall of Fame head coach Tony Dungy, as well as Dallas Clark, Andrew Luck, Matt Hasselbeck, and McAfee, among others. From 2006 until 2019 with Indianapolis, Vinatieri converted 336 of 394 his field goal attempts (85.3%) and 507 of his 524 extra point attempts (96.8%). He appeared in 205 career games with the Colts, and his 19 postseason games are the most by any player in Indianapolis franchise history. He will be inducted into the franchise’s Ring of Honor during Week 6 at home against the Tennessee Titans on October 18th of this upcoming season. Vinatieri is the greatest kicker in NFL history. He should’ve been first ballot last year, much like Mariano Rivera was as a closer for the New York Yankees, because he’s unquestionably the greatest to do it at his position ever. Just like #42 for the New York Yankees had ice in his veins to close out games in the biggest moments and stages of his sport—which for Vinatieri included multiple game-winning Super Bowl field goal kicks, and challenging playoff field goals in difficult road and/or weather conditions. Still, Vinatieri’s wait, as the NFL’s all-time leading scorer with 2,673 total points scored wasn’t long, even if having such a wait at all was pretty unnecessary. The 4x Super Bowl Champion (including Super Bowl XLI with the Colts), 3x First-Team NFL All-Pro, and 3x NFL Pro Bowler will now have his bronze bust speak to the other legends enshrined into the Hall at night for as long as pro football’s greatest honor still exists as a living and breathing museum.

title: Sauce Gardner exhibits ‘no excuses’ mentality as Colts defense denies offense inside red zone
summary: WESTFIELD, Ind. — With six practice periods stuffed into an hour-long practice Saturday morning, the Colts dedicated Day 8 of training camp to red zone and two-minute drills. There was no room for error as the defense continued to cover every single inch of the field from the opening snap. Starting quarterback Daniel Jones used […]
full_text: WESTFIELD, IN - AUGUST 6: Indianapolis Colts cornerback Sauce Gardner (1) runs through a drill during the Indianapolis Colts training camp practice on August 6, 2026 at the Grand Park Sports Campus in Westfield, IN. (Photo by Zach Bolinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images WESTFIELD, Ind. — With six practice periods stuffed into an hour-long practice Saturday morning, the Colts dedicated Day 8 of training camp to red zone and two-minute drills. There was no room for error as the defense continued to cover every single inch of the field from the opening snap. Starting quarterback Daniel Jones used the play action to try and catch the defense off guard with a throw toward the goal line, but free safety Camryn Bynum recovered just in time to break up the pass. The Colts finished the morning practice with a competitive two-minute drill that used the length of the field. Jones spread the ball around, igniting the drive by hitting tight end Tyler Warren on an out route for eight yards. Laiatu Latu should have secured his third sack of the hour-long practice on the next play, but the referees let it play on and Jones found receiver Nick Westbrook-Ikhene in the flat just to move the sticks. Latu could have secured another sack inside the red zone with just 18 seconds left on the play clock, but he instead forced a hurried throw that was ultimately broken up by cornerback Sauce Gardner. With 10 seconds remaining, the defense dropped eight back near the goal line, so Jones simply dumped off a pass to running back Jonathan Taylor underneath to put kicker Blake Grupe in range for a 30-yard chip shot. After Thursday’s practice, Gardner signed his shoes for an Army veteran, then mentioned there are times he wishes he could get targeted more often to make those kinds of plays. Gardner has been adamant that he wants quarterbacks to test him this season. Last season, Gardner allowed just 22 completions on 45 targets (49%), which was the tenth-lowest completion rate among qualified cornerbacks. Despite Gardner playing in a career-low 11 games between the New York Jets and the Colts in 2025, 45 targets mean he gets thrown at just four times per game or essentially once per quarter. “I don’t even give myself no excuses no more,” Gardner said. “I just be like, ‘Man, if I get two targets, I need two picks.’” Gardner established his name as a true lockdown cornerback with a Defensive Rookie of the Year campaign in 2022, along with consecutive First-Team All-Pro seasons to start his NFL career. Although Gardner has just one interception over his last 50 NFL games, he understands it gets etched into the weekly gameplan of opposing coordinators to target receivers on the opposite side of the field as him. “I don’t know who ran it, but we had watched the game where we played the Falcons. Drake London basically ran like a little out route and I had looked back, perfect position, the ball didn’t get thrown. There was somebody else in the meeting, who had ran and the ball got thrown and they made a play. I’m like, ‘Dang, I just wish I could have got the ball thrown to me on that specific play.’” you know 1️⃣ pic.twitter.com/msYplDaHbb — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) August 7, 2026 Latu’s ability to squeeze the pocket in the blink of an eye forces quarterbacks to make hasty decisions, while defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo’s mix of coverages also disrupt the post-snap reads for even the veteran QBs. With receivers Alec Pierce, Josh Downs and Laquon Treadwell all sidelined, it also allowed the secondary to play tight coverage in the red zone and erase any opportunities to find open receivers Saturday morning. The pressure intensified because Latu repeatedly found his way into the backfield, beating second-year right tackle Jalen Travis off the line of scrimmage. The third-year edge rusher appeared to secure a sack on the final play of the first team period before returning for another sack in the final two-minute drill. If Jones hadn’t been sporting a red jersey and it were a real game, Latu could have honestly had four sacks in four team periods. With more time to let the play develop in the red zone 7-on-7 period, Jones was able to deliver strong throws to his receivers. Jones found receiver Ashton Dulin for consecutive completions, including a 10-yard touchdown on an out route against cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt. The pair connected again back in an 11-on-11 session, when Jones escaped what appeared to be instant pressure from Latu and found Dulin on a corner route near the goal line. For the second-unit offense, Riley Leonard continued to make the most of his opportunities and certainly received more reps than Anthony Richardson amid the battle for backup QB. Leonard opened his first team session with an impressive pass down the sideline to receiver Coleman Owen, who had created separation from linebacker Jaylon Carlies. Leonard later layered a pass over the reach of cornerback Rob Carter Jr. and into the hands of tight end Will Mallory for a 10-yard gain to drop the sticks for goal-to-go. Carter later jumped a curl route near the pylon to pick off Anthony Richardson on his first throw with the second-team offense. Richardson’s work was more limited after he received just two plays in the initial red zone team period with the third unit. Since only the second-team went out for one final two-minute drill, it was Leonard who commanded the offense to midfield. Leonard did complete three passes outside the numbers to pass catchers Eli Pancol, Will Mallory and Coleman Owen, but the second-unit stalled after moving the ball into opposing territory. Grupe then got another chance to put his own stamp on the scorching morning workout and drilled a 55-yarder to close the practice. The windows were nearly shut on Day 8 of training camp and the mistakes became more magnified with limited opportunities. There are just five more training camp practices the Colts will host at Droplight Grand Park, including another morning practice on Sunday at 10 a.m. There are also just five days left before the preseason officially begins in Foxborough against the rival New England Patriots.

summary: This week, we asked Jacksonville Jaguars fans to predict how many turnovers the defense will force in 2026. Two-thirds of respondents said 20-29 turnovers, and the other third said 10-19 turnovers. “We’re just continuing to improve our physicality and the X’s and O’s behind the game,” linebacker Foye Oluokun said after Friday’s mock scrimmage. “When […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 07: Foyesade Oluokun #23 of the Jacksonville Jaguars celebrates a interception during the second quarter against the Carolina Panthers at EverBank Stadium on September 07, 2025 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images This week, we asked Jacksonville Jaguars fans to predict how many turnovers the defense will force in 2026. Two-thirds of respondents said 20-29 turnovers, and the other third said 10-19 turnovers. “We’re just continuing to improve our physicality and the X’s and O’s behind the game,” linebacker Foye Oluokun said after Friday’s mock scrimmage . “When we know that and everybody can trust the communication, we can all fly around. So, I like what I saw in terms of being in the right spots and stuff and kind of ramping up, getting ready for a real game. Kind of get that energy behind it with the mock game feel, but it’s always good to see us back out there playing football, talking with each other and flying around.” While the defense was among the league’s best at creating takeaways last season, head coach Liam Coen is hoping that consistently sticky coverage on the backend will help out the pass rush. “I really have felt like that [defensive backs] group has gotten better and better. I think that Araujo and Perk and Drew Lascari have done a great job coaching those guys and working on some technique of maybe being able to challenge people a little bit more and be able to play a little bit more man, or just match coverages. I think that only helps the rush in how much those two are usually tied together. But I’ve been very pleased.” According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Jaguars have +3000 odds to win Super Bowl LXI.

title: Chiefs training camp notebook Day 10: Tempers flare after long week
summary: The tenth practice of Kansas City Chiefs training camp was the second straight in full pads and was the last of a six-day stretch featuring daily practice. It was a sunny, hot morning in St. Joe. The team will welcome an off day on Sunday before returning to the fields at Missouri Western State University […]
full_text: ST. JOSEPH, MO - JULY 30: Kansas City Chiefs defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah (91) walks to the field during training camp on July 30, 2025 at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The tenth practice of Kansas City Chiefs training camp was the second straight in full pads and was the last of a six-day stretch featuring daily practice. It was a sunny, hot morning in St. Joe. The team will welcome an off day on Sunday before returning to the fields at Missouri Western State University on Monday. Arrowhead Pride analyst Caleb James and I watched practice together; I recommend scanning Caleb’s timelines on X for all the observations and clips he got out of Saturday’s practice. Here’s everything to know from the work done by the Chiefs on the field: Attendance report The injury status for the Chiefs stayed mostly the same since the update given by head coach Andy Reid after Friday’s practice . The only player returning to practice on Saturday was linebacker Jeffrey Bassa (groin); rookie wide receiver Cyrus Allen (shin bruise) worked closer to full participation in his second day back from injury. Tempers flare after sixth consecutive day on the field It was a long week of practice up in St. Joe, and it showed on the field throughout Saturday’s practice. During one full-team period, a pass play ended with left guard Kingsley Suamataia full-on swinging at defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah. Tempers flare. This is the aftermath. FAU in the middle of it. Comes after a pass play where FAU bull rushed Kingsley well pic.twitter.com/8SCCmcbq2r — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) August 8, 2026 In the aftermath, Anudike-Uzomah came back angrily towards Suamataia before defensive line coach Joe Cullen pulled him off the field and walked him to the sideline. The fourth-year player, looking to prove something this preseason, returned to the field shortly thereafter. Anudike-Uzomah has been lining up inside as a three-technique rusher (outside shoulder of the guard) in certain looks for the Chiefs’ starting defense throughout camp. He bull-rushed Suamataia on this particular snap before the fight broke out. Boys, I’m a K9 guy. pic.twitter.com/66WQpsfUsU — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 8, 2026 During head coach Andy Reid’s famous long-drive drill that followed an already long practice, running back Kenneth Walker was ready to scrap when safety Alohi Gilman showed him some extra physicality after a run down the sideline. It was the second time Walker has thrown a football at a defender after extra physicality to finish a play. On Saturday, exhaustion was especially a factor for Walker; he was the featured player on a handful of snaps before this play. “How about that 16-play long drive?” Toub asked local media after practice. “That’s how you know it’s hot,” Toub elaborated. “That happens. It’s football sometimes.” The team is a week away from its first preseason action, clearly ready to hit and tackle another set of football players. Still, quarterback Patrick Mahomes sees the positive of that feisty energy. “Six straight days of just going against the same guys,” Mahomes smiled. “I think that’s what’s been great about this camp is it has been super competitive on both sides. A little scuffles here and there but nothing crazy. As long as we keep it like that and keep competing, that’s when you get the best football team you can get.” Dave Toub lists the team’s 4 returners Throughout camp practices, there has been a clear foursome of return men for special teams coordinator Dave Toub: Running back Brashard Smith “Brashard has really taken a nice step as far as a punt returner,” Toub told reporters. “He’s catching the ball a lot cleaner.” Wide receiver Nikko Remigio “Nikko just keeps getting better,” Toub said. Wide receiver Cyrus Allen “[Allen] was doing a good job until he got hurt; now he’s back out there again,” Toub shared. “We have to continue to develop him.” Wide receiver Jacob De Jesus “De Jesus is solid, great catcher, just not a real big guy,” Toub acknowledged. “He’s going to be exciting in the preseason games, for sure.” A fringe-roster player to watch: Kevin Knowles Second-year defensive back Kevin Knowles was often a silver lining in the Chiefs’ disastrous end of the season last year. Out of Florida State, undrafted, Knowles earned a starting spot in Toub’s punt-coverage unit last season. “He’s an established guy,” Toub said. “He was a starting gunner last year for us all year long. Great player for us.” On defense, Knowles plays almost entirely as a slot defender. Of course, that position has been addressed this offseason, whether it was signing veteran Kader Kohou or drafting Jadon Canady in the fourth round. Knowles will have to prove himself on defense to continue being a piece of Toub’s special-teams puzzle. The long-time coach knows that. “On the defensive side of it, that’s where he has to pick it up,” Toub said. “He has to know his job over there, be somebody that Spags can depend on; if somebody got hurt, he could throw him in there. “He has established himself with me, as far as last year goes,” Toub reiterated. “He’s a good player.” The Chiefs will be back on the practice field in pads on Monday morning at 9:15 a.m. after a rest day Sunday.

title: Chiefs rookie QB Garrett Nussmeier on playing preseason: ‘I’ll be ready’
summary: A year can be an eternity at any level of football. Few predicted 12 months ago the current status of Kansas City Chiefs’ rookie quarterback Garrett Nussmeier. Last August, Nussmeier led the preseason No. 9-ranked LSU Tigers and was an early co-favorite to win the 2025 Heisman Trophy. Many predicted Nussmeier’s senior season would boost […]
full_text: ST JOSEPH, MISSOURI - JULY 26: Quarterback Garrett Nussmeier #14 participates during Kansas City Chiefs Training Camp at Missouri Western State University on July 25, 2026 in St Joseph, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images A year can be an eternity at any level of football. Few predicted 12 months ago the current status of Kansas City Chiefs ’ rookie quarterback Garrett Nussmeier. Last August, Nussmeier led the preseason No. 9-ranked LSU Tigers and was an early co-favorite to win the 2025 Heisman Trophy. Many predicted Nussmeier’s senior season would boost him to the top of the NFL Draft. It was not meant to be. Nussmeier attempted to play through a season-long abdominal injury, but he was ineffective and eventually replaced as LSU’s starter. On draft weekend, the player once seen as a certain top-ten selection lingered deep into the process until the Chiefs called his name with the 248th selection. Speaking after Friday’s training camp practice at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, Nussmeier admitted that his current gig is a bit different than how he entered last season at LSU. He remains thankful for the opportunity in Kansas City to continue his playing career. Rookie QB Garrett Nussmeier is getting some work today. He finds TE Mason Pine for a nice catch and throw. #Chiefs l #ChiefsKingdom pic.twitter.com/TJHcSyBlsd — Sports Radio 810 WHB (@SportsRadio810) August 7, 2026 “It’s an awesome experience,” remarked the rookie. “I’m super grateful to be here. This is something I’ve dreamed about my entire life. At the end of the day, I’m super blessed and am super grateful that I’m in the NFL. I thank God each and every day when I wake up that this is my life right now. I try to make the most of it. It’s definitely different. It’s a little bit of a humbling experience, but it’s awesome.” Nussmeier suddenly finds himself behind the face of the league in starter Patrick Mahomes and another veteran backup in Justin Fields. “I’m in such a great room,” declared Nussmeier, “with two great quarterbacks — two great vets in front of me — with Justin and Pat. I’m just trying to learn everything I can from them. I spend as much time around Pat as I can to see his routines and things like that. I just continue to try and make myself better by being around them.” The son of New Orleans Saints offensive coordinator Doug Nussmeier also appreciates what he can take in from the league’s longest tenured head coach in Andy Reid. “I’m just trying to learn and grow in many different areas of my game,” Nussmeier explained. “Being around a legendary coach like that who’s had a lot of experience with some really great quarterbacks — anything that he says, I try to listen and take notes. Even if he’s not talking to me — if he’s talking to Pat or if he’s talking to Justin — I’m trying to soak up as much knowledge as I can around him.” Speaking on Friday, Reid praised the quarterback for everything he has shown in St. Joe. “Every time he’s in, he moves the ball,” the coach observed. “I look at that. Any of the mistakes we’ll correct as we go, but his pass production has been a real positive. He gets it. He works hard at it. His dad’s a coach. He grew up that way knowing about detail. He’s doing a nice job — and we’ve loaded him up. We haven’t pulled back on anything with him as far as volume, and he’s handled it.” The rookie would not want Reid to pull back on him in any way. “It’s been awesome,” Nussmeier stated. “It’s a lot of thinking. There’s a lot of complexity in our offense. That’s how I would want it as a quarterback. I’m a coach’s kid. I’m a kid who has grown up around this game. I love the different schemes. I love the different ways to attack. We do so many different awesome things here. It’s been awesome for me and a good challenge for me — and it’s helped me grow my knowledge of the game.” Chiefs fans will likely see plenty of Nussmeier over the team’s three-game exhibition slate — beginning on August 15 at Arrowhead Stadium against the Los Angeles Rams . Reid essentially confirmed on Friday that Mahomes would not play in the preseason opener as he continues his way back from a season-ending knee injury last December. Reid also did not commit to the star playing at all in the preseason. As of Friday, Nussmeier had no insight on how the other three quarterbacks in camp would divide passing duties next weekend. But Chiefs fans should expect to see his best whenever his name is called. “I’m super grateful for the opportunity,” said Nussmeier, “and whenever I get to play, I’ll be ready.”

Why Felix Anudike-Uzomah’s Chiefs comeback hopes look different this summer | The Kansas City Star To help prepare him for such an important season, Anudike-Uzomah sought out Karlaftis for peer workouts ahead of the offseason program. So he’s doing everything he can to improve every single day and show not just Kansas City but the whole league what he’s got and what he’s made of.” Five Observations from Friday’s Practice | Chiefs Training Camp 8/7 | The Mothership 2. The rookie defensive back got his fingertips on the ball to disrupt an otherwise likely completion, logging another impressive play in what has seemingly been a strong camp. Elsewhere on defense, safety Jaden Hicks recorded a pass-breakup on a deep crossing route during 7-on-7 drills. Linebacker Kam Arnold also made a noteworthy play with a pass-breakup during the 7-on-7 segment, punching the ball away from the intended receiver at the catch point. He took full advantage of his matchups against Kahlil Benson at right guard, including one standout repetition where he tossed Benson into the backfield. As much as he offers rushing the passer, he looks to be very stout in the run game. This came a day after Steve Spagnuolo said the rookie had a ways to go. How to get Chiefs’ free summer kids poster featuring Mahomes, Kelce and others | KCTV5 Training Camp Posters are available for Chiefs Kingdom Kids members at the Kids Zone entrance during all fan accessible training camp dates. You’ll need to show the email announcement from Chiefs Kingdom Kids received on August 5 to get a poster. Families who sign up for Chiefs Kingdom Kids on site at training camp will also be eligible. Chiefs training camp risers and fallers: Kahlil Benson’s surprise push, Mansoor Delane’s setback and more | The Athletic Riser: Tight end Jake Briningstool We haven’t seen much from second-year tight end Jake Briningstool, who took the equivalent of a redshirt season in 2025 while battling a hamstring injury. The 2025 undrafted free agent put two of his best practices together in a row this week, though, earning some first-string reps with quarterback Patrick Mahomes on Wednesday while also impressing Tuesday with a twisting catch over the middle. Reid complimented Briningstool Wednesday for his recent progress. Chiefs RB2 Position Battle: This Returning Tailback Is Running Away With the Job | Sports Illustrated The Athletic’s Jesse Newell says that Johnson has been the fourth-preferred running back among the coaching staff in training camp thus far. That makes him quite a long shot to become a clear RB2 by the time the regular season arrives. Although Smith is only entering his second season, experience plays a huge role in K.C.’s offense. He has already learned what Andy Reid expects from his players and how to earn more playing time. Around the NFL NFL Network: Titans sign Skoronski to four-year, $100M Deal | NFL Network Skoronski’s extension includes $88 million in guaranteed money, Rapoport added. The team confirmed the signing Friday afternoon. It’s a good time to be an ascending guard in the NFL. Skoronski’s contract resets the market at the position less than a week after Atlanta handed a four-year, $96 million extension to guard Matthew Bergeron, marking a relatively rare instance in which two interior linemen received top-of-the-line contracts in the same week. Cousins, Crosby scuffle during Raiders practice on Friday | ESPN Defensive end Maxx Crosby hit quarterback Kirk Cousins twice during the team period. And when Crosby hit Cousins’ arm a second time, the 15-year veteran had had enough. Cousins got into Crosby’s face, grabbing the All-Pro’s jersey, while both exchanged words before it was broken up. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said it’s a part of camp, but he wants his players to be smart when those situations occur. Josh Allen still feels guilty about Sean McDermott’s firing | Pro Football Talk “I think about that all the time,” Allen told Mike Silver of The Athletic . “There are certain plays throughout the game — and that’s going to be every game — where you’re like, ‘I could have done more.’ And I always feel like I can do more.” Allen had four turnovers in the 33-30 loss at Denver. Moore is on the books for $18.6 million this year. Only Chris Jones, Mahomes, Smith and Nick Bolton have larger cap hits for the 2026 campaign. Kristian Fulton ranks seventh on the team with a $13 million cap hit. Moore and Fulton combine for $32 million against the cap.
