He spoke candidly about the dichotomy between all football gave him and the potential risks of playing the game.” 49ers rookie De’Zhaun Stribling reveals what he’s learning from Brock Purdy, Mike Evans, others “Backup quarterback Mac Jones recently praised Stribling’s ability to maintain his speed as the ball approaches, something rookie wide receivers don’t always demonstrate. Stribling said that skill comes from getting plenty of repetitions. “It’s just been repping it, working on it, being confident, knowing that I can still run full speed and also track the ball in the air,” he said. “It’s just really a confidence thing and also just a rep thing, so I’m comfortable with it.” Kyle Shanahan to coach 49ers-Titans preseason game “In addition to answering questions regarding the car accident that led to his absence to start camp, Shanahan said he will be coaching the 49ers’ preseason game against the Tennessee Titans on Thursday, August 13. “Oh yeah,” Shanahan said. “I’m doing the same stuff, guys. I just try to not come in here every day [the media room].” Shanahan elaborated, saying his reasons for interview absences were to not throw off his routine of watching film.” 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan addresses the media during training camp “I’ve really tried to eliminate stuff that I would say is just the fake work stuff, which is a big important thing, but like talking to the media, having to break down the team every day. Doing stuff like that I’ve kind of taken it a little bit easier on. One thing I haven’t missed anything of is film. I watch every single play with the coaches after, with the players. I have had a few team meetings. Normally, I do it every day, but I do lose a little when I do stuff like that, so I’ve just picked and choosed a little bit more. As far as the film and everything, being out there for all the practice periods of going against each other, those are, to me, the most important things in my job and I’ve been able to do those every day.”” Kawakami: ‘No doubt I will be there’ — Kyle Shanahan on his healing process and return (paywall) “The concussion stuff was just weird; you feel more emotional and stuff,” Shanahan said. “Don’t take this the wrong way, but I joke with my wife, it feels like you’re in menopause. It’s just different. “You’re emotional and it’s emotional to get in front of groups. But once you do that and you get past the hard parts of it, it becomes pretty easy and you’ve just got to get back to it and get used to it. The main thing, I thought after my first team meeting, I was like, ‘Perfect, I’m out of the woods, I’m good.’ I felt good most of that day and then it hit me real bad that night. Then the next day, I was, like, ‘Alright, maybe I don’t want to do that every day.’ And that’s kind of how everything has gone in this.” 49ers’ defense gets revenge on Brock Purdy with pair of big training camp plays “During a red-zone session, Lenoir stepped in front of Purdy’s pass intended for Demarcus Robinson at the goal line. Once Lenoir secured the ball in his hands, he was off to the races with a 100-yard interception return for a touchdown. Near the end of practice, it was Stout’s turn to pick off Purdy and take it all the way. Stout had strong coverage against Robinson and made the interception. He returned it 25 yards into the end zone, and punctuated the effort with a front flip over the goal line.” 49ers ‘evaluating’ reason for Nick Bosa’s soreness as pass rusher remains sidelined (paywall) “Saturday teased a new possibility: Deebo the punt returner. He was among several players who caught punts during the session. His last punt return came during his sophomore year at South Carolina, where he returned only two punts in his college career. Samuel has not returned a punt in his seven NFL seasons.”

title: Roger Craig reveals dementia diagnosis during Pro Football Hall of Fame induction speech
summary: Former San Francisco 49ers running back Roger Craig has officially been inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame, but there were no speeches to a crowd at a podium. Instead, Craig sat with other greats such as Joe Montana and Steve Young as former 49ers teammate Jamie Williams presented him. Craig delivered his induction […]
full_text: CANTON, OHIO - AUGUST 06: Former NFL running back Roger Craig is introduced prior to the 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame Game between the Carolina Panthers and the Arizona Cardinals at Tom Benson Hall Of Fame Stadium on August 06, 2026 in Canton, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Former San Francisco 49ers running back Roger Craig has officially been inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame, but there were no speeches to a crowd at a podium. Instead, Craig sat with other greats such as Joe Montana and Steve Young as former 49ers teammate Jamie Williams presented him. Craig delivered his induction speech via pre-recorded video — one where he revealed he has been diagnosed with vascular dementia. “The changes were gradual,” Craig said during the video. “At first, they were easy to dismiss as normal aging. Over time, my family noticed, too.” Craig said doctors believe concussions suffered during his NFL career could be linked. “Two things can be true,” Craig said. “Football gave me opportunities beyond anything I could imagine. It helped shape the man I became. At the same time, we know more today about brain health than when I played. “And I hope, sharing my story encourages people to pay attention to their health.” Craig was selected by the 49ers in the second round of the 1983 NFL draft and thrived in Bill Walsh’s West Coast offense. He was the first player in NFL history to have both 1,000 yards rushing and receiving in a single season. Add this along with his three Super Bowl rings, and it could be argued a Hall of Fame introduction has been long overdue. “I want people to know this diagnosis doesn’t define me. I am still Roger Craig. I am still a father, a husband, a teammate, a friend and someone who loves this game and the people who brought it to my life. If sharing my story helps even one family or one former player, then it’s worth it.”

summary: San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan took to the podium for the first time in training camp to answer questions, and fans may get to see him a bit more frequently. In addition to answering questions regarding the car accident that led to his absence to start camp, Shanahan said he will be coaching […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - MAY 8: Head Coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers on the field during Rookie Minicamp at SAP Performance Facility on May 8, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan took to the podium for the first time in training camp to answer questions, and fans may get to see him a bit more frequently. In addition to answering questions regarding the car accident that led to his absence to start camp, Shanahan said he will be coaching the 49ers’ preseason game against the Tennessee Titans on Thursday, August 13. “Oh yeah,” Shanahan said. “I’m doing the same stuff, guys. I just try to not come in here every day [the media room].” Shanahan elaborated, saying his reasons for interview absences were to not throw off his routine of watching film. It’s unclear what specifically Shanahan will be coaching during the game. Last year, he let his offensive coordinator, Klay Kubiak, call the offensive plays. There might be other responsibilities he may delegate as well so he’s not overwhelmed. It sounds like Shanahan plans on doing everything he’d normally do coaching a game. Shanahan’s absence at the start of training camp was due to a concussion sustained from a car accident on July 14. Shanahan dropped his phone, and it fell to the back seat. While the Tesla he drove was on autopilot, the automation failed, and he collided with an SUV. Shanahan suffered the aforementioned concussion in addition to a broken nose and three ribs. At one point, he was at risk for losing his right eye. Shanahan has also claimed— and emphasized—being at fault . Shanahan said he is no longer sensitive to noise and has only been dealing with headaches and fatigue. The 49ers face the Titans on Thursday, August 13 at Levi’s Stadium.
author: Patrick Holloway

title: The 49ers’ simplified defense under Raheem Morris is worth a word of caution
summary: This week there has been a lot of praise for new 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris and the defense he’s installing. Safety Ji’Ayir Brown has been vocal about it saying it’s put him in a position to succeed. The defensive backs as a whole seem to be turning over a new leaf after 2025’s six-interception […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - JULY 27: Raheem Morris defensive coordinator of the San Francisco 49ers talks with the media following a training camp practice at SAP Performance Facility on July 27, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images This week there has been a lot of praise for new 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris and the defense he’s installing. Safety Ji’Ayir Brown has been vocal about it saying it’s put him in a position to succeed. The defensive backs as a whole seem to be turning over a new leaf after 2025’s six-interception dissappointment. The consensus is the defense Morris is installing is simplified and much eaiser for the defensive backs to thrive in. NBC Sports Bay Area’s Matt Maiocco summed it up best : The 49ers’ changes on defense include expanded usage of five defensive linemen and a simplified set of coverage assignments designed to enable the cornerbacks and safeties to play fast without being required to make too many split-second adjustments. This can be good or bad, and we really won’t know until the season begins. There’s a reason NFL offenses and defenses are complex to begin with. It’s also possible they can get too complicated. We’ll start with what the players are loving right now, and what hopefully translates into the regular season: simplified coverage assignments. This has to be a welcome change from what has been happening in the previous years. Especially when some of the split second decisions may have been a result from a massive miscommunication. How bad was the miscommunication? Let’s go way back to 2018. One of the most-oft used reasons for the defensive drop in performance was communication and how the team needed to communicate better. Miscommunications was a common theme in October that year. This was the season the 49ers brought in Richard Sherman who always praised then defensive coordinator Robert Saleh’s gameplans, but also said the team needed to communicate better. As pointed out by Maiocco, there is less need for a split second adjustment in the Morris defense, and that doesn’t fall into communication, but both can be placed into a bucket of complexity. That was a young 49ers defense and miscommunications were expected. That said, it seemed like a reason every week. As the losses piled up, I peeled a layer back and asked “Why aren’t they communicating? What’s the issue with communication?” Basically if every week the defense wasn’t on the same page and communicating properly, that seems to be a coaching issue. The results were (wrong) split second decisions and things falling apart at the worst moments. As you know in year three of Robert Saleh, the 49ers went to the Super Bowl and lost for other reasons. Even after Saleh’s departure and return, miscommunications were a common theme of the defense. So point to Morris. Robert Saleh’s defenses are so complex, maybe dialing it back might be a good thing, even at the NFL level. Or maybe things are still complicated when they are called for coverage assignments, but everything they have to look after isn’t near as large as what Saleh’s defensive backs had to. Again, we don’t know. Of course, this could also go the other direction. “Dumbing it down” and leading to disastrous results. 2016, Chip Kelly’s first and last season with the 49ers. Now before we go any further, let’s all agree the offense itself was destined for mediocrity. Simple or complicated, the 49ers had one of the worst rosters in football. Keeping that in mind, it doesn’t help when offense being installed is simpler. A big example of this simplication came with how the 49ers dealt with the playcall. This was a team that went from Jim Harbaugh’s playcall by comittee, to Geep Chryst who called the plays minus the comittee, but keeping all the delay of game penalties. Well, this new offense fixed it, and tight end Garrett Celek broke down how much better it was with Kelly: “In the past we had a lot of delay-of-games because either we’re not getting the play in time from upstairs or it’s just taking the quarterback too long to read the whole play out. Where now, it’s a lot quicker. We have hand signals, so you can’t have 15 words through hand signals, stuff like that. It’s got to be boom, boom, boom. So when you got less verbiage, it’s easier to remember. It’s kind of genius.” That was just a taste of the offense coming. An offense that finished last in yards gained and points scored. It’s fair to remind everyone the 49ers’ defense isn’t starting from the same place that offense was. The point is a more complicated defense or offense is almost a necessity at the NFL level, but it can get too complex at times. Where on the spectrum does this simplification fall? Will the 49ers be too predictable or is it really going to keep everyone in a better position to succeed? We just won’t know. I do know my biggest criticism of Saleh (who is a terrific defensive coordinator) is that when starters go down, things take a massive step back. There seems to be more turbulent a decline when injuries happen on his defense with just one player as opposed to others. The pushback can be on the depth of his defenses, to be fair. I’m just saying when Nick Bosa went down last year, the 49ers pass rush vanished along with it. Basically, when the cheat codes get turned off, things fall apart. If Morris’s simplified defense can solve that problem — a defense that doesn’t collapse when the cheat codes are gone — then maybe the players—not just the defensive backs— are onto something. We’ll find out in September.
author: Patrick Holloway

title: 49ers News: Congratulations to Hall-of-Famer Roger Craig
summary: Roger Craig’s path from kickball to Hall of Fame, with a lifelong teammate along for the ride (paywall) “Bill Walsh saw no reason to wait. Never mind that players were still in their tuxedo jackets on the night they received their Super Bowl rings after winning it all in 1984. The San Francisco 49ers coach […]
full_text: PALO ALTO, CA - JANUARY 20: Roger Craig #33 of the San Francisco 49ers carries the ball against the Miami Dolphins in Super Bowl XIX on January 20, 1985 at Stanford Stadium in Palo Alto, California. The 49ers won the Super Bowl 38-16. (Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images) | Getty Images Roger Craig’s path from kickball to Hall of Fame, with a lifelong teammate along for the ride (paywall) “Bill Walsh saw no reason to wait. Never mind that players were still in their tuxedo jackets on the night they received their Super Bowl rings after winning it all in 1984. The San Francisco 49ers coach pulled Roger Craig aside during the gala and looked him in the eyes. “Roger, we’re going to need 1,000 yards from you next season,” the running back remembered him saying. This inspired Craig but also befuddled him. He was coming off a year in which he amassed 600-plus yards as a runner and as a receiver. “I was fired up. I knew I couldn’t let him down,” Craig once said. “But then I started to wonder if he meant he needed 1,000 yards rushing or receiving. “I wanted to cover my ass, so I figured I better shoot for both.” Craig did as instructed, delivering the first 1,000-1,000 season in NFL history in 1985, a milestone matched only by Marshall Faulk (1999) and Christian McCaffrey (2019). That distinction goes a long way toward explaining why Craig will be enshrined in the Pro Football Hall of Fame on Saturday.” Williams will stand onstage with his best friend when Craig’s bust is unveiled. What will he feel in that moment? Williams said he didn’t know. Then he became emotional. “You can’t write the script,” he said. “Facts get stranger than fiction. Somebody lives half a block from you, and you start out down by the docks trying to catch catfish. Then you both go on this long journey in life.” Montana wasn’t the first future Hall of Fame player who wondered what was up with Craig and Williams. In 1983, at the Hula Bowl in Honolulu, Pittsburgh quarterback Dan Marino and SMU running back Eric Dickerson were fascinated by the inseparable Nebraska teammates. “They couldn’t get their heads around the fact that we were two Black guys from Iowa,” Williams said. “Marino was like, ‘Man that sounds so boring. What did you all do?’ Then I started going down the list and they got jealous.” They rode horses. Fished. Roller-skated. Blasted the Jackson Five. They hid Roger in the trunk on trips to the drive-in, saving the admission money for candy. ….In the offseasons, Craig worked out five days a week, starting at 6:30 a.m., beginning four weeks after the 49ers’ season ended. Track work. Weight room. Three days of hill work. Craig’s trainer, Raymond Farris, calls Craig “Mr. Football” due to his devotion. Craig would be so eager to start their early morning sessions that Farris would often need to remind him: “Roger, you have to stretch.” Jerry Rice is synonymous with “The Hill,” but he learned how to conquer it from Craig, a 1983 second-round pick who arrived two years before Rice was drafted. “I’ll never forget the first day Jerry showed up and he couldn’t do it,” Farris said. “He hurt so badly afterward that he didn’t come back for the rest of that offseason.”…..“Roger was the only guy who loved training camp and looked forward to it,” wide receiver Mike Wilson said. “I dreaded going to Rocklin. I would be like, ‘Roger, really? You’ve got to be kidding me, man.’” How Romello Height’s winding path to the 49ers made him no ordinary rookie (paywall) I would go up against some good really good players at Auburn — I was on the scout team — and I got scout team player of the year my freshman year. So that’s honestly when I realized, ‘Man, I got it. All I gotta do is just continue to stack the days, work hard and my time will come.’ ” He transferred to USC, where … well, let’s not criticize a young man too much for having fun, but Height began having trouble showing up on time for classes and team meetings. “I was just all over the place, and I knew I had to change and mature in so many ways,” Height said. He often thought of his dad, Ronnie, the ex-Marine. “If he could have gotten his hands on me around that time, he probably would’ve strangled me,” Height said. “I got caught up in a lot of stuff, and that wasn’t how I was raised. I had to find myself, and once I did, man, I was on the right road.” The next stop was Georgia Tech, close to home in Dublin, Ga. Height loved it there. “They told me as soon as I came in the building, like, ‘Mello, just get off of the ball and play how you want. Go get the quarterback or whoever has the ball,’ ” Height said. “They fit the scheme around me.” He would have stayed at Georgia Tech, but like a far-off dinner bell, the pull of NIL was drool-inducing. So, Height became a Texas Tech Red Raider, and the school got its money’s worth — a player who was the product of his father and his previous three stops. “Four schools is a lot, and I was just trying to find myself,” Height said. “All those stops came with maturing. And by the time I got to Texas Tech, I was a totally different person. “I was taking care of my body. I was living in the building. I was creating bonds with my teammates. I was finally the best version of myself.” ….. “I’ve never seen a (rookie) come in and get the scheme as quickly and seamlessly as he has,” Bosa told KNBR radio. “Even when vets come in who haven’t played in this scheme. He’s gotten it even quicker than I did. “He’s super explosive. He’s got a bag of tricks in pass rush that you could tell he’s been coached well. He’s a little older for a rookie, so that might be part of it, but I think he’s going to contribute pretty quick.” Height credits the staff at Texas Tech with stuffing his bag full of pass-rush moves, especially the chop. During training camp, he has been focused on making blockers pay for being on their heels waiting for a speed rush. “I’ve been just trying to throw power in my tool bag,” he said. “That makes tackles more vulnerable to inside moves, more vulnerable to the speed that I’m gonna use because they’re just gonna sit on speed if I’m just showing continuous speed.” 49ers DC Raheem Morris explains the term ‘fever backer’ in his defense “Morris also referenced the term “spinner,” which is something Pete Carroll did with the Seahawks when they had a bunch of pass rushers early in the LOB days. Their “spinner” was mainly Bruce Irvin. To me, that’s who I envision the 49ers think Romello Height will be. More recently, that was Jalon Walker for the Falcons last season. A spinner is an edge rusher in name, but the defensive lineman who will move around the line of scrimmage. The uber-athlete who will line up everywhere, whether it’s over the left guard, right tackle, or blitzing from the stacked linebacker spot…..The 49ers won’t be nearly as static as they’ve been if they are anything like the Falcons from a season ago. There are several benefits to late movement or crowding the line of scrimmage with different body types. You can manipulate protections, create confusion, and get the offensive line to set or slide the wrong way. It’s a way to create free runners. It also gives the defense a way to tee off on the running back in 1-on-1 situations. Occasionally, we’ll see Height drop into coverage, but if his usage is anything like Walker’s last season, he’ll be one of the key pieces to the 49ers’ defense in 2026.” Five bright spots from 49ers training camp inspire optimism amid glut of injuries (paywall) “Rookies tend to err on the quieter side. Defensive tackle Gracen Halton has been in pads only for the past couple of days, returning from a knee bone bruise that sidelined him for five practices. Loud and proud is more his style. The 49ers drafted Halton, listed at 6-foot-2 and 293 pounds, in the fourth round out of Oklahoma. He started his college career as a defensive end and boasts noticeable explosiveness off the snap for an interior lineman. Starting center Jake Brendel, among others, saw as much…

title: Commanders injury news: Laremy Tunsil reportedly suffers torn triceps
summary: Commanders left tackle Laremy Tunsil suffered a torn triceps during Saturday morning’s training camp practice and will likely need surgery that will sideline him for a large portion of the season, NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo and Steve Wyche reported later that evening.   This is a major blow for the entire team, one that will […]
full_text: Commanders left tackle Laremy Tunsil suffered a torn triceps during Saturday morning’s training camp practice and will likely need surgery that will sideline him for a large portion of the season, NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo and Steve Wyche reported later that evening. This is a major blow for the entire team, one that will have a significant and lasting impact on the 2026 campaign. Sources to me and @wyche89 : #Commanders five-time Pro Bowl LT Laremy Tunsil suffered a torn triceps in practice today during 1-on-1 pass-rush drills. He’ll likely require surgery and will miss at least a significant portion of the regular season. pic.twitter.com/mvj4EGEzxk — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) August 9, 2026 Tunsil suffered the injury during a 1-on-1 rep with edge rusher Odafe Oweh. He dealt with a bull rush and the pair locked arms, per a fan video of the incident, but Tunsil awkwardly disengaged and immediately clutched his right arm and elbow. The five-time Pro Bowler was immediately taken to the medical tent and went with trainers inside the Commanders training complex shortly after for further evaluation. Mike Garafolo of NFL Network, who was on-site at Commanders camp, reported that Tunsil would need further testing to inform the extent of the injury. The results came back with bad news. Tunsil will likely require surgery and his exact recovery timetable remains unknown. Overall, though, the prognosis is not good. If he needs surgery, Tunsil should miss an extended period of the 2026 season. There is a possibility that he misses the whole year, but further evaluation is required before making definitive statements about his recovery. Reserve offensive lineman Andrew Wylie filled in at left tackle after Tunsil left practice, but he’s not the answer at the position. Brandon Coleman was in a camp battle with Chris Paul to be the starting left guard, but he’s likely the best option on the roster to move to left tackle. Coleman made 12 starts at left tackle in 2024, before the Commanders traded for Tunsil in the 2025 offseason, and he filled in for Tunsil for the final three games of last season. Coleman will surely shift over there in the short term. The Commanders will monitor that performance closely before looking outside the organization for help General manager Adam Peters gave Tunsil a massive, two-year, $60 million contract extension this offseason, rewarding a stellar 2025 campaign and ensuring that the Tunsil trade wasn’t for a rental. Tunsil is widely considered among the NFL’s elite left tackles, and there is no replacing a player of that caliber. There is certainly no one on the street who could step right in and play at an upper-tier level. Right tackle Josh Conerly, a 2025 first-round pick and a standout left tackle at Oregon , could switch sides. That scenario seems less likely at this stage — new signing Daniel Brunskill has also played some right tackle — though the Commanders will consider all possible solutions now that the offensive line has lost its anchor for a significant stretch. What’s your reaction to this news? What should the Commanders do at left tackle with Laremy Tunsil sidelined? Let us know in the comments below:
author: Scott Bair

title: Commanders camp: What Jayden Daniels said about Stefon Diggs addition
summary: The Commanders made a huge addition to the passing game. Veteran receiver Stefon Diggs is now a Commander, after agreeing to a one-year deal earlier this week.   Head coach Dan Quinn said the Diggs addition was a “big deal,” for the Commanders. He has received positive reviews after formally joining the team on Friday. […]
full_text: The Commanders made a huge addition to the passing game. Veteran receiver Stefon Diggs is now a Commander, after agreeing to a one-year deal earlier this week. Head coach Dan Quinn said the Diggs addition was a “big deal,” for the Commanders. He has received positive reviews after formally joining the team on Friday. We’ve seen quarterback Jayden Daniels throw to Diggs and work with him after practice, but Saturday marked the first time Daniels had spoken publicly about Washington’s new receiver. Diggs, as you might expect, made a solid first impression on his new quarterback. “It’s great, man,” Daniels said during an interview on the Commanders’ Next Man Up podcast . “The guy came in with a lot of focus, energy – he’s hungry and willing to get better and push everybody. His resume, his career, speaks for itself. I’m excited to be able to work along with a guy like that, who has been so great over all these years. He overcame adversity from where he was drafted in the league, to all the stuff he has been through on the field – his (ACL) injury – and I’m excited to learn from him, too.” Diggs said on Friday that he and Daniels will build chemistry organically over the summer, with extra work and a steady dialogue about how the two can work well together. Daniels agrees that’s the core of what must happen. a fist bump for the ages 👊 pic.twitter.com/IE1CK0zisq — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) August 8, 2026 “Open communication, constant communication, watching film and talking through a lot of different routes,” Daniels said. “The work after practice (is key). We need to put in the work and the time to get better each and every day. I know he’s willing to do that, too.” While this is Daniels’ team and his offense to orchestrate and execute, he’s willing to listen to someone with Digg’s experience level. Jayden Daniels —> Stefon Diggs looks so good pic.twitter.com/Jn3xzXkYjK — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) August 7, 2026 “It’s just his feel for a lot of things he has seen throughout his career,” Daniels said. “He’s had a lot of different coverages thrown at him. He was the top guy in this league for some time. So, to pick his brain on stuff that he sees and why he runs certain routes in certain ways, I’m excited to learn from that.” Diggs joins a group of pass catchers that includes top-tier receiver Terry McLaurin and will help create a formidable pairing that should help Washington’s offense thrive. When asked what to expect from that pairing, his answer was simple. “Hopefully,” he said, “a lot of touchdowns.” Daniels also talked to NFL Network about Diggs. Here’s what he had to say: Jayden Daniels is already a fan of his new receiver Stefon Diggs 😏 @MikeGarafolo | @BaldyNFL | @Commanders pic.twitter.com/r8motsmF6q — NFL Network (@nflnetwork) August 8, 2026

title: Commanders free agency: Daniel Brunskill among three veteran OL signed
summary: The Commanders are ramping up the competition level in their offensive line room. Head coach Dan Quinn cited that reason for Washington adding three new offensive linemen to the roster prior to Saturday morning’s training camp practice.   Washington signed center Daniel Brunskill, offensive tackle Nicholas Petit-Frere and guard Max Scharping.   The Commanders released […]
full_text: The Commanders are ramping up the competition level in their offensive line room. Head coach Dan Quinn cited that reason for Washington adding three new offensive linemen to the roster prior to Saturday morning’s training camp practice. Washington signed center Daniel Brunskill, offensive tackle Nicholas Petit-Frere and guard Max Scharping. The Commanders released receiver Chris Hilton Jr. and guard Timothy McKay in corresponding moves. Defensive tackle D.J. Davidson was the other one. He has decided to retire, and was placed on the reserve retired list. That’s the third player to retire during training camp, and Dan Quinn said that was typical as player’s assess their careers. We have made the following roster moves: – Signed C Daniel Brunskill, T Nicholas Petit-Frere and G Max Scharping – Released WR Chris Hilton Jr. and G Timothy McKay – Placed DT D.J. Davidson on the Reserve/Retired List pic.twitter.com/58xxgGWsYp — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) August 8, 2026 We reported on the Scharping addition on Friday evening, and it turns out that was one of three additions to the offensive front. They’re all veterans with significant frontline experience. “We actually wanted to see if we could raise up the competition level in that back group, to see who could go,” Quinn said in a Saturday morning press conference . “It was not injury related. It was more like, ‘let’s battle this thing out and see where we can go.” The Commanders signed 3 OL today and Dan Quinn said it was for competition, not injury related. Also noted that center Nick Allegretti will miss another week with a calf injury that his sidelined him for most of training camp. pic.twitter.com/G2s3b9v5eb — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) August 8, 2026 The Brunskill addition is a big one. He has 71 starts in 108 games and has played most offensive line spots, including significant time at center. He also has a history with Commanders GM Adam Peters, who was in San Francisco during Brunskill’s 49ers tenure starting in 2019. Brunskill has prized versatility and can snap, with long stints playing center in Tennessee. Petit-Frere has 28 starts in 34 games , all with Tennessee from 2022-24. He was largely out of the NFL in 2025, save a brief offseason stint with the 49ers. Quinn also provided a related injury update for Commanders projected starting center Nick Allegretti, who suffered a strained calf during camp’s first practice, and tight end John Bates, who’s dealing with a hamstring issue. “They’ll probably be another week or so out of their assessment, as we get into Wednesday and Thursday,” Quinn said. “They’re getting closer, but not today, though it’s not long-term, either.”

Mike Sainristil and Treylon Burks are scheduled for Q&As after practice, along with players getting interviewed on the field. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo and Brian Baldinger were also at camp today and they did post-practice interviews with Jayden Daniels, Sonny Styles, and Stefon Diggs. Dan Quinn talked about some of the roster moves that were made today, including signing three new offensive linemen. He said that was more for competition on the backend of the roster than injury concerns for other players. He noted that C Nick Allegretti(calf) and TE John Bates(hamstring) will both miss another week. Quinn said there was some concern for the amount of time Allegretti is missing affecting play strength and working with Jayden Daniels. summary: The Daily Slop – August 8, 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. full_text: The Daily Slop – August 8, 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/moSEJlCUzs — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) August 7, 2026 Articles Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) How might Stefon Diggs fit in David Blough’s new offense? Yesterday, I broke down what Diggs brings to Washington but today, I thought I’d look at how he might fit in David Blough’s new offense. The Commanders have one established receiver set in stone in Terry McLaurin. McLaurin will most likely be the X receiver in this offense, as he has been since he was drafted. That leaves the Z receiver and slot receiver roles up for grabs. Those two roles can be quite different, but there is also some overlap in there too. Diggs is very much capable of playing both roles, having done so for the Patriots last year. He spent similar numbers of snaps in the slot as he did on the outside in New England That gives the Commanders some flexibility. They’ll be hoping that rookie receiver Antonio Williams can develop quickly enough to claim the slot receiver role and become their version of Amon-Ra St. Brown in this offense . That would then leave Diggs to the Z receiver spot on the outside. But if Williams isn’t quite ready, Diggs can easily slide inside and open up the Z spot for the likes of Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown or Luke McCaffrey to try and win. I suspect what we’ll see from Diggs is he’ll split time in both roles and while there is some overlap, they do require different things too. So lets see how he fits in both roles. Z Receiver Earlier this offseason, I wrote a post looking at what the role of the Z receiver might be in David Blough’s offense and if Treylon Burks might be the receiver to win the job . We’re expecting Blough’s offense to look similar to the 2023 Detroit Lions offense under Ben Johnson, where Blough was on the practice squad in his final year as a player before transitioning to coaching. That offense focused the majority of its targets to an interior trio of slot receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, tight end Sam LaPorta and running back Jahmyr Gibbs. The outside receivers still had an important role, but the focus was inside and over the middle to those three. The Z receivers in that offense were primarily used to stretch the field vertically and to attack the intermediate parts of the field on deeper crossing routes while the defense focused on that interior trio of weapons underneath. This meant that the Z receivers in that 2023 Lions offense ran a lot of deep overs, high crossers and deep dig routes. Last year with the Patriots, Diggs proved he was very much capable of doing that type of work. The other major part of the Z receiver role in this offense is to stretch the field vertically. Diggs doesn’t have blazing speed to run by coverage at age 32, so he’s not going to be as dynamic as other options in that aspect. But he can still be a vertical threat in other ways. His use of route tempo can help lure defenders into a false sense of security before he suddenly bursts by them. He also has great ball skills, with the ability to track the ball down the field and adjust his body to however the ball is thrown to him. That means while he might not be a candidate to run by defenders down the sideline, he is an option to target with back-shoulder throws. Yesterday, I broke down what new Commanders WR Stefon Diggs brings to Washington. Today, I'm looking at how he might fit in David Blough's new offense, with the flexibility to play Z or slot. Full breakdown: https://t.co/NXzV8AAU9r pic.twitter.com/jKm4ez8ZOu — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) August 7, 2026 The Athletic (paywall) Stefon Diggs begins new era with the Commanders: ‘I want to win’ “My numbers have always spoken for themself,” he said. “No matter who you like or what you say, the production has been there. … Numbers-wise, I mean, I’m not no mathematician, but …” Diggs’ first practice with the Commanders was intentionally light. Quinn lauded the four-time Pro Bowler’s conditioning, but said the team would ease him in to allow him to get up to speed with the playbook. So, on Friday he was a full participant in the individual period, but did only a couple of receiver one-on-ones against defensive backs, and took only a few reps in 11-on-11. Afterward, he stayed on the field with Jayden Daniels to catch extra passes and talk through some of the nuances of routes and timing. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE From Last Man Standig: There were other NFL teams interested in the efficient target coming off the seventh 1,000-yard season of his career and a Super Bowl appearance. Other teams could offer comparable money or quality quarterback play. None could match the chance to return home. The 32-year-old said he felt “little chills” when reporters reminded him of his local Pop Warner and prep past. “I can’t write a better story at this point in my career,” said the Gaithersburg native. “What I wanna do and being able to be healthy coming off of ACL [surgery in 2024]. Having success and going to your hometown team, you wanna shine for them. I wanna put on for my city.” For more from Ben Standig, click here The Athletic (paywall) The NFL thinks Jayden Daniels is the 13th-best QB. In 2026, he’ll be way better than that It has taken only six practices to watch Jayden Daniels and come to a way-too-quick-but-still-definitive conclusion: There aren’t 12 NFL quarterbacks better than this guy. More than that: The player who had maybe the best rookie quarterback season in NFL history is ready to put himself squarely in the top tier of QBs — en route to annually becoming one of the best. Daniels spent the first six sessions of training camp — during which the offense has looked better and better in 11-on-11 work — placing plenty of balls exactly where they need to be. These aren’t just completed passes. They’re passes that are either dropped in the only area where a receiver can snag them or are timed so perfectly that the pass catcher doesn’t have to break stride and can gain significant yards thereafter. [I]f Daniels plays somewhere between 15 and 17 regular-season games…then it says here he will reprove it. He’s too talented, too dedicated and too bright not to. The bet is we get to January, and Commanders fans — along with coaches and execs across the league — are saying, “There aren’t five quarterbacks I’d rather have than Jayden Daniels.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated The Good and Not So Good From Commanders’ Seventh Training Camp Practice Amos participated in team work , while Armstrong’s workload was heavier on individual drills because Washington plans to ease him back more gradually. Way resumed his holding duties on every field-goal attempt Friday, an important step after the pectoral injury kept him out during the opening week of camp. It truly is ironic that all three players entered training camp with injury issues, and all three became available on the same morning. After today’s practice, Stevens sits firmly in the driver’s seat after going perfect in practice once again, with his longest being 56 yards, while Moody missed his two longest attempts on the day from 53 and 56. The kicking competition now has Stevens at 28-for-30, and Moody at 24-for-29. With Moody now having five misses to Stevens’ two, the pressure to answer is something Moody will feel now. Marcus Mariota throwing two interceptions really set the stage for failure on the day. One interception could be credited heavily to a defender making a good read, but two in the same practice give Mariota and the second-team offense film that needs correcting. summary: Follow our daily updates from Falcons training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Atlanta Falcons ' camp is taking place in Flowery Branch, Georgia, and Falcons reporter Marc Raimondi has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Falcons camp. We will update this file often. How will the QB battle play out between  Michael Penix Jr . and  Tua Tagovailoa for QB1? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Falcons stories 
 
 Sources: Falcons, RB Robinson reach 3-year deal worth up to $75M 
 Falcons sign Matthew Bergeron to four-year, $96M extension 
 Falcons' Jalon Walker tore ACL, out for season 
 Wife of DC Ulbrich dies of cancer 
 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa had his best practice of camp, though it did not last long. The practice, that is.

 Lightning halted the Falcons' open practice at Lanier High School in Sugar Hill, Georgia, early on Saturday night. There was still more than 30 minutes left when things were called on the field of a packed stadium.

 Tagovailoa was 6-of-8 passing in 11-on-11 drills, including his best two passes of training camp: a 30-yarder with touch to wide receiver Jahan Dotson and a play-action rollout lob to wide receiver Drake London .

 Tagovailoa returned to full practices earlier this week after dealing with a tight back to start camp.

 
 

 
 
 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa hit running back Bijan Robinson on a wheel route that would have gone for a 90-yard touchdown or so during an 11-on-11 session Friday. The series was situational. The Falcons offense was backed up against the opposite goal line and Tagovailoa floated it nicely to Robinson, who had complete daylight.

 It was just another play in another practice this summer here in Flowery Branch, Georgia. But it also felt like more than that, something symbolic. Like a sigh of relief.

 For the first time this training camp, Tagovailoa and Robinson were both full participants in practice. Tagovailoa has been dealing with a tight back and Robinson was a hold-in before signing a three-year contract extension Wednesday that is worth up to $75 million. Robinson got his first carries in 11s Friday.

 More observations: 

 
 Quarterback Michael Penix Jr . is still not cleared for 11s, but has looked sharper lately in 7-on-7 work. On Friday, he was 6-of-9 in the red zone, helped out by a diving catch from wide receiver Keelan Marion . 
 Matt Ryan, the team's president of football and former franchise quarterback, threw to wide receivers Drake London and Jahan Dotson separated from everyone else during a drill Friday. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 Michael Penix Jr . explained his current situation in the clearest way possible Wednesday.

 "If I can't be on the field," Penix said, "how am I going to be the starter?"

 Penix has been on the field. He has done individual drills and 7-on-7 sessions. But what the Falcons third-year quarterback means is that he has yet to be cleared for 11-on-11 work. And until he does, there cannot be any kind of quarterback competition.

 That is not necessarily news. The Falcons coaching staff made that clear in the spring. But back then there was some expectation Penix would be fully ready for training camp. That has not been the case and Penix said it could be another several weeks before he's good to go.

 Tua Tagovailoa (tight back) took another step toward a full return Wednesday with more work in 11s. He went 5-of-7 passing. At this juncture, it's fair to say Tagovailoa will be the team's Week 1 starter unless something major changes.

 More observations: 

 
 Edge rusher Jalon Walker was officially confirmed as out for the season with a torn ACL after getting injured Tuesday at practice. It's a major blow for a pass rush that was depending him on to make a major impact. He had 5.5 sacks as a rookie last season. 
 Running back Bijan Robinson officially put pen to paper on his three-year extension, which is worth up to $75 million. He is still limited in practice and has not done any 11s as the team ramps him up. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Falcons running back Bijan Robinson returned to practice after a five-day hold-in Tuesday. Robinson got a three-year extension worth up to $75 million and is now the highest-paid running back in the NFL.

 Head coach Kevin Stefanski referred to Robinson's hold-in as "very amicable." Robinson had been at every practice on the hip of running backs coach Michael Pitre prior to actually coming back.

 "He wants to be out there practicing," Falcons running back Brian Robinson Jr . said. "You know he wants to be competing. So, I used to just tell him, 'Yo, take your time, handle your business. Whenever your time comes, it's going to come. I know you want to be out there with us, but we going to hold it down until you come back.'"

 Bijan Robinson didn't do much Tuesday. He worked a bit with the running backs in individual drills and did a play-action drill after practice with quarterback Michael Penix Jr . Pitre said they will work to ramp Bijan up over the next few days based on recommendations by the training and medical staff.

 More observations: 

 
 Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa (tight back) said he continues to make progress and expected to be practicing fully Wednesday. Tagovailoa has eased into 11-on-11 sessions the last two days, but has only thrown seven passes. He was 3-of-4 in 11s on Tuesday. 
 Quarterback Cooper Rush , who signed with the Falcons last Wednesday, got reps with the first-team offense in a two-minute drill near the end of practice. Penix has still not yet been cleared for 11s, but got reps again in 7-on-7 work Tuesday. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa participated in 11-on-11 team sessions Monday for the first time this training camp. Tagovailoa has been dealing with a tight back and was still limited. He did two series, going 3-for-3 passing in 11s with individual drills, as well.

 Michael Penix Jr . (right knee) had his best 7-on-7 session Monday, going 6-of-8 with two drops, working mostly with younger players and reserves. His best throw of camp came on the final play of practice. Penix found  Antwane Wells Jr . for a long touchdown pass down the left side.

 Penix has still not been cleared for 11s. The majority of those reps still went to Jack Strand , followed by veteran Cooper Rush . Strand was 7-of-11 passing in those sessions, while Rush was 3-of-7.

 More observations: 

 
 Defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich returned to practice Monday. Ulbrich's wife Cristina died last week after a battle with cancer. "He's a father figure, older brother for me," Falcons linebacker Divine Deablo said. "So, I was glad to have him back out here. I hugged him as soon as I seen him. Everybody just wants to play for 'Brich' at the end of the day." 
 This was the first camp practice with pads. 
 Offensive tackle Wanya Morris and defensive tackle  Da'Shawn Hand  both left practice with apparent injuries. 
 Michael Jerrell , Brandon Walton and rookie seventh-round pick Ethan Onianwa  rotated at right tackle. Free agent signee Jawaan Taylor is not yet cleared to practice after elbow surgery last season. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Cooper Rush has only been with the Falcons for a little more than 72 hours, but he is starting to get himself acclimated fairly well.

 The veteran quarterback got reps with the first-team offense for the first time Saturday morning in 11-on-11 team sessions. Overall, Rush was 6-of-10 with a red zone touchdown to tight…

title: 2026 Baltimore Ravens training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Ravens training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Baltimore Ravens ' camp is taking place at Under Armour Performance Center in Baltimore, and Ravens reporter Jamison Hensley has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Ravens camp. We will update this file often. Can new coach Jesse Minter get  Lamar Jackson  and the Ravens to the Super Bowl? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Ravens camp 
 
 Zay Flowers, Ravens agree to four-year, $140M extension 
 Derrick Henry, entering 11th year, not thinking about retirement 
 Ravens waive rookie Diego Pavia to make room for Ethan Pocic 
 Ravens' Madubuike (neck) practices for 1st time in 10 months 
 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 On a day when  Zay Flowers ' injury scare headlined practice, wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane continues to record one of the most impressive training camps by a Ravens rookie with more highlight-making receptions.

 Lane caught a deep touchdown pass from Lamar Jackson on a go route in a one-on-one drill against top cornerback Nate Wiggins and then made a one-handed catch on a back-shoulder throw by Tyler Huntley 25 yards down the field. After Lane's latest one-handed grab, running back Derrick Henry leapt in the air to give a shoulder bump to the impressive third-round pick.

 "There is consistency of making really contested, nice catches -- being a really friendly target for the quarterback," coach Jesse Minter said. "He's certainly starting to see a vision of maybe what he can become in the offense."

 Lane's strong camp has solidified a spot in Baltimore's three-wide formation, along with Flowers and Rashod Bateman .

 

 Other observations:  

 
 Running back Justice Hill called first-year playcaller Declan Doyle "the most detail-oriented" offensive coordinator that he's been with. In Hill's previous seven seasons, he's had two offensive coordinators: Greg Roman, who directed the NFL's highest-scoring offense in 2019, and Todd Monken, who guided Baltimore to the No. 1 offensive ranking in 2024. 
 The Ravens' defense got its hands on a lot of passes. T.J. Tampa , Malaki Starks and Amani Oruwariye all recorded pass breakups. Tampa is having an impressive camp and provides quality depth at cornerback behind Wiggins and Marlon Humphrey . 
 The best route of the day came from rookie tight end Josh Cuevas , who faked outside before running to the middle to shake free of safety Keondre Jackson for the easy catch. The Ravens are hoping for one of their rookie draft picks -- Cuevas and Matt Hibner -- to step up and provide another pass-catching target at tight end behind Mark Andrews . 
 The Ravens signed inside linebacker Jamon Johnson , a local product who attended St. Frances High School in Baltimore. He played in two games last season, making 10 tackles. The Ravens waived undrafted rookie cornerback Matthew McDoom to make room for Johnson on the 90-man roster. 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 The Ravens' third practice of the week in full pads was also their chippiest.

 The first dust-up of camp came when outside linebacker Tavius Robinson shoved offensive tackle Carson Vinson after the play. This caused the offensive and defensive players to converge in the middle of the field before they were quickly separated.

 There were no punches thrown, but coach Jesse Minter huddled the team together shortly afterward.

 "It was just a reminder of [how] the whole reason we are out here is to make each other better [and] help us get ready to play when we are playing against somebody else," Minter said.

 In what was the longest practice of camp at 2 1/2 hours, Minter intentionally scripted long drives of eight and nine plays, which can take a toll on a day when the heat index reached 92 degrees.

 "You want to be able to do all that with a high, high level of physicality and also keep your wits about you," Minter said.

 Other observations: 

 
 Ferran Torres, the star of the World Cup, watched practice and spoke to the players afterward. Torres came off the bench to score the winning goal in Spain's World Cup triumph. "Talk about just being ready when your number is called [and] being at your best when your best is needed -- that is like the ultimate," Minter said. 
 Kyle Hamilton showed why he is one of the best -- and most versatile -- safeties in the league. During team drills, Hamilton was constantly in the backfield and even recorded a sack of Lamar Jackson . Then, in one-on-ones, Hamilton intercepted Jackson after blanketing Elijah Sarratt on a fade route. 
 In one of the most hands-on drills the Ravens have ever had, Baltimore had its defensive backs work on tackling by hitting coaching interns. As Minter pointed out, the coaches were holding a pad and landed on a pad. "I think coaches will do anything to make players better, and we have a great group of coaches," Minter said. "All [of] those guys are willing to do whatever it takes." 
 T.J. Tampa made an impressive play by getting off a block and ripping the ball away from running back Rasheen Ali . Tampa has used camp to solidify himself as the team's No. 4 cornerback behind Nate Wiggins , Marlon Humphrey and Chidobe Awuzie . 
 Kicker Tyler Loop was a perfect 7-of-7, including ones from 53 yards and 61 yards. Last season, Loop was 1-of-4 on kicks beyond 50 yards. 
 
 
 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 Rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane continues to be the talk of Baltimore Ravens training camp after another highlight reel catch.

 During red-zone drills, Lane leapt high in the back of the end zone to grab a Lamar Jackson throw for a touchdown. The way Lane is consistently pulling in passes has drawn lofty comparisons.

 "The guy that I was around that his hands remind me of is [former NFL great] Mike Thomas ," Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle said. "Mike Thomas had these strong hands where he could pull it down in a way. You threw it in the vicinity, and you felt like he was going to go get it. There is a lot of that feeling. He is a very friendly guy to throw to."

 Doyle was in New Orleans with Thomas from 2019 to 2022 as an offensive assistant. Thomas led the NFL in receptions in 2018 and 2019.

 Now, in his first season as the play-caller in Baltimore, Doyle has been impressed with the Thomas-like catch radius of Lane, who has been the headliner through the first seven practices of camp. He made a leaping, 30-yard reception over the middle last week and then wowed fans with a one-handed catch on Tuesday.

 When Doyle left the field Wednesday, Lane approached him to say he wasn't pleased with how he messed up at practice.

 Doyle told him, "Hey, you recognized what you made a mistake on. Now, the next step is let's fix it before that happens."

 Other observations:  

 
 After watching the Ravens not practice well in the rain during the spring, Doyle was pleased with how the players performed during the steady downpour on Wednesday. "We play in the AFC North," Doyle said. "In order to win games late in the year, you are going to play in some weather games." 
 Middle linebacker Roquan Smith is reacting to the ball better than he did a year ago. Smith ended the first team drill by picking off Lamar Jackson and then lateraling the ball on the return. 
 Wide receiver Zay Flowers added 8 pounds this offseason and is up to 186 pounds. What was the reason for the added weight? "Everybody gets mad at me when I'm running sideways," Flowers said. "So [now I can] run through some more tackles."

title: 2026 Buffalo Bills training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Bills training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Buffalo Bills' camp is taking place at St. John Fisher University in Pittsford, New York, and Bills reporter Alaina Getzenberg has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Bills camp. We will update this file often. How will the transition to Jim Leonhard's defense go? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Bills camp 
 
 Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson carted off with leg injury 
 Josh Allen on Bills' alternate uniforms: 'Stop hating on the jerseys' 
 Bills unveil new 'Nickel City' alternate uniforms 
 2026 Buffalo Bills training camp preview 
 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 On Saturday night, the Bills held their annual "Return of the Blue and Red" practice at Highmark Stadium. It was the Bills' first football activities in their new $2.1 billion home.

 The official welcome featured plenty of fireworks, quite literally.

 One of the biggest came during a two-minute drill, when quarterback Josh Allen found wide receiver Khalil Shakir , as he darted past safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson  and twisted his way into the end zone. Moments later, Allen joined him in the celebration by sliding into the end zone.

 As coach Joe Brady described it, "Josh throwing an unbelievable play to Khalil."

 The night went smoothly, outside of a brief downpour midpractice, and players later marveled at the arena.

 "Wow," tight end Dawson Knox said. "... I got here four hours early. I was just walking around on the field, taking myself on a little tour around everything, just kind of looking at all the details and just taking it in, because it still doesn't feel real yet. ... It's the coolest place I've ever played football in."

 More observations: 

 
 Nickel corner Dee Alford had a nice interception off Allen. The defense made a show of celebrating the pick, even being a bit late to get to the next play. 
 RB Ty Johnson went down during one-on-one drills with a right leg injury. He was helped off the field by athletic trainers and did not return to practice. 
 Starting center Connor McGovern also was injured on the first play of 11-on-11 drills. He returned to play, but then needed further attention from athletic trainers, who were looking at his right leg. McGovern then walked off the field and did not return. Lloyd Cushenberry III filled in for him (outside of a brief appearance by Sedrick Van Pran-Granger ). Brady did not have an update on McGovern or Johnson after practice. 
 Cornerback Maxwell Hairston missed a second straight practice because of an undisclosed injury. Rookie DT Zane Durant , P Mitch Wishnowsky , DB D.J. Miller and WR Mac Dalena also did not participate. 
 The punting job remains Tommy Doman Jr .'s to lose. With Wishnowsky out, Doman punted and held for kicker Tyler Bass , who made all eight of his field goal attempts. The rookie had one fumble, but otherwise a solid day. 
 Rookie undrafted free agent CB Kani Walker  continues to be a surprise in camp. 
 

 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 The Bills wrapped up training camp at St. John Fisher University with a shorter practice in pads.

 Quarterback Josh Allen said one of his takeaways from the time away from Buffalo is how close the team has gotten.

 "This group from offense to defense is the tightest knit group that I've been around really since I've entered the league," Allen said. "The defense is meshing so well together. Just even when you walk in the dorm room or walk in the cafeteria, guys sitting down, talking, really getting to know each other. 
 
"There's just a lot of love on this team and that'll show on the field."

 Allen pointed to the veteran leadership new OLB Bradley Chubb brings as well as the growth of two-time captain ILB Terrel Bernard  in helping the team get to where it is.

 The Bills now head back to Orchard Park, New York, and camp practice starts with the first football work in the new Highmark Stadium on Saturday night.

 Other observations: 

 
 Two defenders took trips to the medical tent during practice. Rookie defensive tackle Zane Durant went in briefly but returned to the sideline with his helmet. Projected starting nickel Dee Alford was slow to get up after defending a pass by Allen to wide receiver Joshua Palmer . He returned to the sideline without his helmet, and second-year DB Jordan Hancock filled in during the absence, but practice ended quickly afterward. 
 LT Dion Dawkins had a veteran rest day. Backups Tylan Grable and then Jude Bowry spent time with the first-team offense. Bowry dealt with penalty issues from the officials present at the session. 
 No practice for CB Maxwell Hairston , WR Mac Dalena or DB D.J. Miller . Coach Joe Brady said the Bills were being precautionary with Hairston after an injury Thursday. Rookie CB Davison Igbinosun worked with the first-team defense in Hairston's place. 
 Former Bills pass rusher Von Miller has posted photos recently alluding to a desire to re-sign with Buffalo. Bills GM and president of football operations Brandon Beane said, "I talk to Von all the time. We're buds. But yeah, I mean, listen, I love Von. You could name 10 other ex-Bills that if everything lined up right, you wouldn't say no to a guy like that. But beyond that, there's nothing imminent or nothing going." 
 
 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 A significant first came from kicker Tyler Bass at practice. Returning after missing the entire 2025 season with a sports hernia, Bass practiced kickoffs and field goals on the main training camp field for the first time this camp. He went 5-of-7, with both misses coming from 45-plus yards. Bass had kicked once in a practice open to the media in the spring.

 Special teams coordinator Jeff Rodgers said earlier in the week that Bass had been kicking outside of open practices and that it was not planned for him to kick in practice until this point.

 "Just the whole organization, I think, Joe [Brady], Jeff ... have done a great job of just integrating me at the right pace," Bass said. "And just letting me be the best version of myself, and that's where I'm seeing a lot of growth in."

 Other observations: 

 
 Safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson (calf) and defensive tackle Deone Walker (left elbow) participated in the individual and team periods of practice. Walker is wearing a brace on his left arm. 
 WR Keon Coleman had an up-and-down day with a nice catch on a pass from quarterback Josh Allen  but also a drop later that left him vocalizing frustration. 
 The splash play of the day came from Allen with a deep pass to recently acquired WR Dante Pettis . If the play had taken place during a game, it would have drawn flags and a review. 
 ILBs Dorian Williams and Terrel Bernard are back participating in 11-on-11 drills, and defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard made it clear there would be roles on the defense during the season for both of those players and rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr , who has taken advantage of significant practice time due to other injuries. "The physical skill set of those three guys, I think it's going be a lot of fun to work with." 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 The Bills wore full pads during 11-on-11 drills for the first time in training camp. And with the pads came the fighting.

 Players had to be separated several times, with the back-and-forth talk starting between the offensive and defensive lines even before the team periods. One big altercation came when rookie inside linebacker Kaleb Elarms-Orr didn't realize the play was over and made…

title: 2026 Chicago Bears training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Bears training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Chicago Bears ' camp is taking place in Lake Forest, Illinois, and Bears reporter Courtney Cronin has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Bears camp. We will update this file often. Will the defense step up and lead the Bears back to the NFC North title? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Bears news 
 
 Darnell Wright agrees to record deal 
 New Bears safety Coby Bryant out 8-10 weeks with injury 
 Bears CB Johnson views 2026 as 'definitely a contract year' 
 Ben Johnson: Bears motivated to spurn 'regression' label 
 
 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 The Bears were already without defensive end Montez Sweat , left tackle Braxton Jones and cornerback Jaylon Jones when they suited up for Saturday morning's padded practice. The injury hits kept coming during the 105-minute session.

 On the final rep of red zone one-on-ones, wide receiver  Luther Burden III and cornerback  Tyrique Stevenson got tangled up while the defensive back broke up a pass from Caleb Williams . Stevenson landed awkwardly on his back while Burden appeared to sustain a lower body injury.

 After several moment where Stevenson laid on the ground in visible pain, the cornerback was helped to his feet and received treatment on the sideline from a trainer, who rubbed ointment on the lower right side of his back. Stevenson fought through pain to finish practice despite having to pull himself out of an 11-on-11 period.

 Burden, on the other hand, walked gingerly toward the weight room under his own power flanked by a trainer. He did not return to practice.

 Chicago can't afford another injury to its secondary that has been without nickel corner Kyler Gordon (calf) all of training camp and lost safety Coby Bryant for an expected eight to 10 weeks Monday. Backup safety Elijah Hicks remains on the PUP list with a calf injury.

 Cam Lewis , who is filling in for Bryant at safety, left practice during the final period with an apparent leg injury. Lewis was guarding wide receiver Rome Odunze in the red zone when he got hurt and rode away on the back of a cart. Lewis was replaced by Skyler Thomas at safety.

 Other observations: 

 
 Jedrick Wills Jr . got first-team reps at left tackle with Braxton Jones sidelined. He struggled during OL/DL one-on-ones, getting beat twice and false starting once. 
 With Jaylon Jones sidelined, rookie Malik Muhammad was once again with the first-team defense at nickel. Muhammad broke up a pass during 11-on-11 and almost came away with an interception later. 
 Sixth-round defensive tackle Jordan van den Berg was a part of the rotation with the first-team defense during low red zone drills. He excelled with his bull rush against center Logan Jones during one-on-one drills. "I think he's going to be a hell of a football player," defensive tackle Neville Gallimore said. 
 Colston Loveland caught two touchdown passes from Williams while covered during 7-on-7. His second TD grab came in the corner of the end zone with a defender draped over him as he dove to catch the ball. 
 The focus at the end of practice was three end-of-game situations. Tyson Bagent dropped a dime into  Jahdae Walker 's hands on fourth down for a touchdown. Williams ended practice with an exclamation point when he bought time upon dropping back with 12 seconds on the clock before throwing a 17-yard laser to Odunze in the back of the end zone. Odunze caught the pass with multiple defenders around him. 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 The longest practice of training camp to date was also the most physical. The Bears were in pads Thursday for 130 minutes and commenced team periods with old-school 9-on-7 and 9-on-9 running drills. With music blasting across the practice fields closest to Halas Hall, the physical, downhill running session turned up the temperature in practice between the offense and defense with a handful of shoving matches after plays were blown dead.

 "Shoot, we love it," defensive end Austin Booker said. "That's our mentality this year: We're getting off the ball, we're being aggressive and getting in the backfield."

 The intensity carried over to one-on-ones between the offensive and defensive lines. Two days after becoming the highest-paid right tackle in NFL history ( four years, $116 million ), Darnell Wright won all three of his reps taken against defensive end Montez Sweat .

 Braxton Jones , who began practice at left tackle with the first-team offensive line for a fourth straight day, sustained an injury during his second one-on-one rep with Booker. Jones threw his helmet and was visibly upset as he tried to walk it off before heading inside with a trainer. The initial belief is that Jones didn't suffer a long-term injury.

 Caleb Williams finished practice on a high note after the offense struggled with operation issues in 11-on-11. There were multiple false starts, and when Rome Odunze slipped on a route, the ball headed in his direction landed in cornerback  Tyrique Stevenson 's hands for an interception.

 The Bears closed out practice with a two-minute drill. Williams marched the offense 65 yards downfield in 1:41 and went 6-of-6 while connecting with Odunze, Colston Loveland , Kalif Raymond ,  D'Andre Swift and Luther Burden III . Despite having time left on the scoreboard, practice ended immediately after Burden's touchdown in the back of the end zone given the session was right at the 2 hour, 10 minute mark.

 
 Multiple players exited early with injuries including Sweat, who was seen walking into the building under his own power. Defensive backs Dallis Flowers and Gervarrius Owens sustained significant leg injuries. 
 Cairo Santos went 6-for-6 during the field goal period and connected on kicks from 56, 50, 40 and 33 yards. 
 Defensive lineman Shemar Turner , who is on PUP while recovering from ACL surgery, appeared at practice for the first time in training camp and worked with a strength and conditioning staffer off to the side. 
 Kaden Davis continues to impress with his opportunities. The former Division II receiver had several big catches, including a touchdown in the corner of the end zone from QB Case Keenum . Davis punted the ball in celebration and was immediately flagged. 
 Rookie corner Malik Muhammad played nickel during the two-minute drill. He had several reps with the first-team defense. 
 Raymond, a 10-year veteran, believes  Zavion Thomas ' work habits reflect that of an older player. Two nights ago, the rookie wide receiver sent Raymond a series of ankle mobility exercises to help strengthen the muscles in his lower leg and foot. "It's a vet-type mindset to be disciplined and do something like that," Raymond said. "And when he showed me that video, I was just happy to know that that's who he is." 
 Ben Johnson said there is no update on Kyler Gordon (calf), who is on PUP, and when he might return to practice. "We're just continuing to rehab," Johnson said. 
 The Bears signed 10-year veteran safety  Xavier Woods  and worked out nine defensive backs. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 One day after becoming the highest-paid right tackle in NFL history, Darnell Wright got ribbed by coach Ben Johnson, who congratulated Wright on his four-year, $116 million extension ($93 million guaranteed) in front of the team before practice.

 Johnson joked that Wright "owed" offensive line coach Dan Roushar a loan. Wright agreed with Johnson's assessment and credited his position coach for…
