title: 2026 Cleveland Browns training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Browns training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Cleveland Browns  camp is taking place at the CrossCountry Mortgage Campus and Browns reporter Daniel Oyefusi has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Browns camp. We will update this file often. The biggest question for Cleveland remains who will be the starting QB? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Browns stories 
 
 What are the Browns looking for in their QB competition? 
 Jerry Jeudy clarifies viral video, says he talked to Browns QBs 
 AJ Epenesa grateful to be Eagle after 'weird' Browns situation 
 Deshaun Watson: Preseason is 'great opportunity' after injuries 
 Deion Sanders gives Browns 'insight' on Shedeur Sanders 
 GM Andrew Berry 'hopeful' Browns can reunite with Jadeveon Clowney 
 Sources: Browns, Grant Delpit agree to 3-year, $48M extension 
 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 The Browns made a major change to the quarterback rotation in their 10th practice.

 Despite Shedeur Sanders being scheduled to lead the No. 1 offense in his alternating reps with Watson, it was Watson who took every starting rep in team drills. Sanders split the remaining reps with Dillon Gabriel .

 Before practice, coach Todd Monken indicated that there might be a 7-on-7 session in which Watson threw to the team's top pass-catchers but added that "Shedeur will take the majority of the 1 reps today."

 The Browns are off Sunday, and Monken said the coaching staff would use that time to discuss which quarterback will start the preseason opener against the Bears next Saturday in Chicago.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Watson had another productive practice to cap a bounce-back week for him. His highlight throws included a deep completion to wide receiver Isaiah Bond in 7-on-7 after he got a step ahead of cornerback Tre Avery , then a short touchdown pass to rookie wideout Denzel Boston on a back-shoulder fade in 11-on-11, beating corner Tyron Herring . 
 Right tackle Tytus Howard left practice early with a member of the team's medical staff. Rookie Austin Barber took Howard's spot with the starting offense in team drills. 
 Elgton Jenkins and Teven Jenkins returned to team drills after being limited to individual drills Friday. 
 Fifteen players did not practice: Justin Jefferson (new absence), Joe Royer , Myles Bryant , Michael Burton , Damarri Mathis , Carson Schwesinger ,  Mike Hall Jr ., Parker Brailsford , Izavion Miller , Elijah Chatman , Zak Zinter , Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis , Maliek Collins and Kendrick Green . 
 

 
 Friday, Aug. 7 
 The Browns had a lighter practice indoors and in helmets on Friday, as they are set to practice in pads for more than two hours on Saturday. It was still an eventful session, with all the quarterbacks pushing the ball downfield in team drills.

 Deshaun Watson looked his most comfortable attempting deep passes in camp so far. He connected with wide receiver Isaiah Bond for a long gain in 11-on-11s and also found wideout Jerry Jeudy for a 40-yard touchdown in 7-on-7s. Toward the end of practice during a two-minute drill, Watson evaded the pass rush and rolled out to his left before throwing a pass into the end zone that Bond leapt up and caught.

 

 More observations: 

 
 While Watson had some accurate downfield passes, he was also intercepted by cornerback Denzel Ward on an errant pass that went over the head of Bond; it's Watson's eighth interception in nine practices. 
 The Browns signed offensive lineman Jack Conley and cornerback Jeadyn Lukus , claimed defensive tackle Patrick Jenkins , waived wide receiver Jamari Thrash (injury designation) and linebacker, and placed guard Kendrick Green on injured reserve. 
 Rookie safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren recorded his first interception of camp, picking off Shedeur Sanders after he overthrew tight end Jack Stoll in 11-on-11s. 
 Safety Donovan McMillon intercepted Dillon Gabriel in 11-on-11s on an underthrown deep ball to rookie wide receiver Kole Wilson . 
 Linebacker Winston Reid forced a fumble on running back Raheim Sanders and recovered the ball to end the two-minute drill led by Sanders. 
 Elgton Jenkins , Mason Graham and Teven Jenkins returned to practice, but both Jenkinses were limited to individual drills. 
 Thirteen players did not practice: Joe Royer , Myles Bryant , Michael Burton , Damarri Mathis , Carson Schwesinger , Mike Hall Jr ., Parker Brailsford , Izavion Miller , Elijah Chatman , Zak Zinter , Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis , Maliek Collins . 
 
 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
The Browns' eighth day of practice concluded the installation of coach Todd Monken's offense. Going forward, Monken said practices would focus more on situational football, "premier plays," and work against defensive looks that Cleveland will see from opponents this season.
 "What we're trying to do is stack as many good plays as we can within what we're asking them to do on a given day," Monken said. "I'd much prefer stacking really good days, but as the head coach, if the offense is stacking really good days, it probably means the defense wasn't stacking a very good day. So, within every practice there's usually give and take, some ebb and flow of practice -- some things you all don't see, and some things that at the moment we don't see until we see it on tape. So it's really about how many plays in a row can we stack?"

 

 More observations: 

 
 Deshaun Watson  and Shedeur Sanders both threw an interception in team drills. Cornerback Tyson Campbell intercepted Watson in 7-on-7 drills, while cornerback Myles Harden intercepted Sanders in red zone 11-on-11 drills. Safety Grant Delpit broke up a pass intended for rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston , which led to the pick. 
 Two plays after his interception, Sanders threw the lone touchdown in team drills when he found rookie receiver KC Concepcion in the end zone after he located an opening in Cleveland's zone defense. 
 Guard Zak Zinter left practice on a cart. 
 Sixteen players did not practice Thursday: Joe Royer , Myles Bryant , Michael Burton , Damarri Mathis , Carson Schwesinger , Mike Hall Jr. , Parker Brailsford , Kendrick Green , Izavion Miller , Elijah Chatman , Elgton Jenkins , Teven Jenkins , Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis , Mason Graham , Maliek Collins . 
 
 
 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 Quarterback Deshaun Watson had a slow start to training camp but had his best day to date on Wednesday. After two consecutive practices in pads, the Browns practiced in shoulder pads and helmets and ran extensive red zone and goal line 7-on-7 drills. Watson excelled, throwing multiple touchdowns, but he also looked more in sync and confident pushing the ball downfield in other team drills.

 "I think to say who's ahead is a little extreme," Browns coach Todd Monken said before practice. "But we evaluate every day where our roster is, who's where. We try not to knee-jerk react on the one day; that's hard to do. We want every day to go as smooth as it can, and it doesn't, so you have to fight that part of it. We also have to fight; we're in install. We see what you see, and we see a little more in-depth because of the film. But the reality is we're always talking about personnel and the roster; the quarterbacks just happen to be part of that."

title: 2026 Dallas Cowboys training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Cowboys training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Dallas Cowboys ' camp is taking place in Oxnard, California, and Cowboys reporter Todd Archer has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at the Cowboys' camp. We will update this file often. Will Dallas turn around the NFL's worst defense from 2025? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Cowboys camp 
 
 Cowboys' Dak Prescott not shying away from setting lofty goals 
 Jones optimistic about Cowboys, likes 'what we put together' 
 Source: Ex-Cowboys QB Will Grier returns as offensive assistant 
 Quieter offseason has Cowboys focused on the right things 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 Practice was not very old when coach Brian Schottenheimer wanted to get a point across to the players.

 While in the middle of individual drills, he called the group together from both practice fields and appeared to light into the players, expletives and all. After the Cowboys were in pads for three straight practices, perhaps Schottenheimer wanted to remind the players that padless practice doesn't mean less effort.

 Whatever it was, the message was received.

 "[He was] just reminding us that we have to have a productive day," pass rusher Donovan Ezeiruaku said. "It was nothing that really happened. It just felt as though he needed to do that as the head coach, and that's what he did. I think we had a pretty good day."

 Said wide receiver  George Pickens , "Just pushing guys to be better."

 Other observations:  

 
 QB  Dak Prescott had a sharp day, completing 15 of 19 passes, including 5 of 6 in a red zone period that saw him throw touchdown passes to Jake Ferguson and Pickens. Ferguson and Pickens were able to use their size to their advantage to beat S P.J. Locke and CB  Shavon Revel Jr . 
 Jerry Jones made the long flight back from the Pro Football Hall of Fame on Friday night to be in attendance for Saturday's practice. 
 Schottenheimer spent most of the practice observing on the sideline as offensive coordinator Klayton Adams called the plays from behind the line of scrimmage. It's the second time Adams has called the plays. Schottenheimer's comfort level with the offensive staff has grown. 
 CeeDee Lamb had two touchdown catches, including one on a route where he was able to out-leverage CB DaRon Bland to the outside by quickly getting out of his break. On the second, he and Prescott connected on a perfect back-shoulder throw on Revel. 
 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 

 After he was tossed from Tuesday's practice for throwing a punch, second-year edge rusher Donovan Ezeiruaku had a conversation with coach Brian Schottenheimer.

 Schottenheimer said it was a "long talk."

 "I just talked to him about [how] we're playing this the way you would play a game. And I said, 'For an incredible player, you run hot'; that's part of his edge," Schottenheimer said. "He's an incredible play-style guy. He plays the game the right way, but at the same time, we have to have a plan that when he gets hot and when he feels his temperature rising, what is the plan?

 "So he and I discussed a couple different options. I think we've got a good thing in place, but again, I don't want to take away the edge that he plays on. But you throw a punch, you've gone over the edge, therefore you're going to get ejected.

 Schottenheimer said Ezeiruaku's reaction was "great."

 In Thursday's practice, Ezeiruaku was as active as he has been, providing pressure off the edge. And he didn't throw a punch.

 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 With the Cowboys holding their Military Appreciation Day at training camp Thursday, Dak Prescott was presented with a gift from a fan.

 It was a Cowboys hat with a picture of his brother Jace on the side. At first, Prescott said he just thought it was a normal hat until he saw Jace, who died in 2020 . Prescott's Faith Fight Finish Foundation, which honors his brother as well as his mother, addresses mental health and suicide prevention.

 "That actually means a lot," Prescott said. "I wish I knew who did it because I would've said thank you. I just thought it was a hat. I didn't see it until I go with my daughters [after practice]. 
 
"It's badass."

 

 More observations: 

 
 Coach Brian Schottenheimer wanted to clarify the state of the left tackle competition. Tyler Guyton hasn't been named the starter yet, but Nate Thomas needs to up his level to make sure there is a competition. Guyton took part in Thursday's work with his right elbow taped after he didn't finish Tuesday's practice. Guyton and Thomas had false-start penalties leading to their departures for a play. 
 Tight end  Jake Ferguson is off to a strong start in camp. He and Prescott have had a clear connection on the intermediate and seam throws, and they connected four times Thursday with one completion coming on a "free" play when the defense jumped early that led to a decent gain. 
 Rookie LB Jaishawn Barham did not finish practice because of a groin injury. A source said it wasn't believed to be serious, and Barham was able to return to the field to watch the final parts of the workout. 
 It did not rise to the level of the Donovan Ezeiruaku punch, but cornerback Caelen Carson and rookie receiver Anthony Smith got into a tug-of-war and needed to be separated by teammates. It was brewing with both players after a particularly physical play early in team drills. 
 LB Curtis Robinson had a near interception of a Sam Howell pass down the seam to tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford , reaching high with his right hand to knock it down. The ball nearly fell into Robinson's lap as he landed on the ground. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 A year ago at this time, the Cowboys were learning about how  Javonte Williams  fit into their run game. They found out what he did well, as he rushed for 1,201 yards in 2025. Then they rewarded him with a three-year, $24 million contract in the offseason.

 As Williams enters his second season with the Cowboys, offensive coordinator Klayton Adams is looking to expand the list of what Williams does best.

 "Obviously the guy's pretty good on direct runs and he's hard to get down behind the line of scrimmage, but I think that he is a more diverse runner than he probably gets credit for," Adams said. "I think the guy does a really nice job with some of the outside zone stuff, particularly the weak side.

 "He's got really quick feet. He's able to get in and out of cuts really well. And he's one of those dudes that's not scared to run through the smoke, and that's what you're going to have to do on some of the time. I think he's good at a lot of things."

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Sometimes coaches can be inventive when it comes to putting players through drills. On Tuesday, wide receivers coach Junior Adams had CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens catching passes off the Jugs machine during a special teams portion of practice while wearing what looked like a mosquito net or beekeeper's hat.

 The goal is to limit the receiver's vision and force him to concentrate longer on the catch. Lamb dropped one pass but figured it out. The first pass went through Pickens' hands, and he was finished.

 Longtime tight ends coach Mike Pope, who had a stint with the Cowboys, said he had 478 different drills for his tight ends. He would throw ice water at shirtless players while wearing a helmet. He had them wear swim goggles to limit their peripheral vision.

 Let's see if Adams has more tricks in his bag.

title: What can Quinnen Williams bring to Cowboys' D in 2026?
summary: Acquired during last season, Williams aims to make an even bigger impact in 2026 and ideally "for the long haul" in Dallas.
full_text:
OXNARD, Calif. -- Comfort matters to Quinnen Williams .

 When the defensive tackle arrived to the Dallas Cowboys in a trade from the New York Jets in November, he had to get accustomed to a new city, new defense and new teammates. In the seven games he played for the Cowboys, Williams had 20 tackles, 33 quarterback pressures, 1.5 sacks, a pass breakup and two tackles for loss.

 He was still named to the Pro Bowl for the fourth straight year, but he admits he could be better.

 "I didn't have my best year when it comes down to statistically, as a pass rusher, last year and I want to be better," Williams said. "I want to do better. Not for myself but for this team, and I know I can be better. Definitely one of those things -- I will never stop learning, I will always continue to learn, continue to grow and try to get better every single year."

 Entering his first full season with the Cowboys and in the midst of his first training camp as the Cowboys learn a new scheme, Williams' influence on the field and in the locker room has grown.

 When last season ended, coach Brian Schottenheimer and Williams had a number of conversations about the importance of winning, the philosophy they will have on defense and some other things Schottenheimer kept private.

 "The other day he was telling me how excited he was about this system," Schottenheimer said. "He's going to get a bunch of one-on-ones. He's going to get a bunch of situations where he's having to get blocked by guards with him and Kenny [Clark] working in there together. But I see his leadership style now, I mean, I feel him. Quinnen, he doesn't speak a lot, but boy, the way he works, the way he practices is impressive. But he's a grown-ass man."

 

 At 28 years old, Williams is entering his prime where his physical skills match up with his knowledge of the game. Dallas has a new coordinator in Christian Parker, so this will be Williams' third different defense in less than a calendar year, but Williams has high expectations.

 "I think the skill set I have, I kind of fit any defense," Williams said.

 The Cowboys are not concerned. Executive vice president Stephen Jones said the Cowboys want to keep Williams, who is signed through 2027, "for the long haul." There have been preliminary talks but nothing that is close to being done. Williams said he wants to be with the Cowboys long term as well.

 

 "I'm not really focused on no contract," Williams said. "I definitely want to be here for the long haul. I definitely will enjoy and love being here for the long haul, but I want to win. And that's kind of the only thing I'm really focused on is winning and kind of getting this defense into the groove where we can win football games for this team."

 Parker's defensive line is asked to do similar things to what Williams did at Alabama when he became the No. 3 overall pick in 2019 by the Jets. New defensive line coach Marcus Dixon coached Aaron Donald with the Los Angeles Rams . Parker was around tackles such as  Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis with the Philadelphia Eagles .

 "Man, a complete defensive tackle," Clark said of Williams. "He works hella hard. He understands the game. He's smart. He's physical. And he's eager to get better too. He don't feel like he's got all the answers. He wants to do more for himself. He knows he can do more. The other day he's playing all of the blocks true and all that and just playing the double-teams. [Later] he switched it up. It's cool to see him evolving in his game."

 When the Cowboys had a DeMarcus Ware or Micah Parsons , opposing offenses had to know where Nos. 94 and 11 were on each play. Schottenheimer believes that's the same with Williams' No. 92.

 "If you try to single him, it's going to be a long day for whoever the guard is," Schottenheimer said.

 Noticeable on the field, Williams is quiet off it, but he said his leadership abilities have grown over the years. He is a member of Schottenheimer's leadership council.

 

 At the start of the offseason program back at The Star, Schottenheimer moved Williams' locker to the middle of the room, near quarterback  Dak Prescott 's, a sign of what the coach thinks of Williams' influence.

 "It's super easy to kind of come to work and work hard when you got guys with the same mindset as you," Williams said. "But if you got guys you got to drag along and really babysit, it's kind of hard in that case. [But] we have a bunch of guys on our team and in our room that have the same mindset and the ultimate goal is to win."

 Winning is one thing that has eluded Williams in the NFL. He never made the playoffs with the Jets. New York never had more than seven wins in a season and never finished better than third in the AFC East. The Cowboys finished 7-9-1 last season, missing the playoffs and finishing third in the NFC East.

 "As a competitor, man, I want to win it all," Williams said. "I compete in this sport. I'm an ultimate competitor and I want to win every single game if I can. I was bred to win from Coach [Nick] Saban and do the things that we can do there at Bama. And I wanted to bring that same mentality, especially to this defense because the offense have that mentality. Just trying to develop a new defensive culture, a defensive mindset."

 In training camp practices, the battles between Williams and All-Pro guard Tyler Smith have had Schottenheimer saying he would pay to watch it every day as a football junkie. Williams has displayed strength to handle the double-teams and the agility to split gaps.

 "He keeps pushing us," Clark said, "and we keep pushing him. I think the sky can be the limit. He's going to do wonderful things this year. I can't wait to see what he can do."

title: 2026 Denver Broncos training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Broncos training camp, including intel on the QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Denver Broncos camp is taking place in Englewood, Colorado, and Broncos reporter Jeff Legwold has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Broncos camp. We will update this file often as we track the Broncos' push toward getting to the Super Bowl after falling one game short last season. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Broncos camp 
 
 Payton to talk to Taysom Hill about interest in Broncos 
 Broncos QB Bo Nix won't be afraid to run on repaired ankle 
 How will Broncos' Sean Payton adjust to not calling plays? 
 Cooper practices Wednesday despite legal troubles 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 When the Broncos went through a scripted scrimmage, it was safety Brandon Jones who was 3-of-4 in field goal attempts.

 Why? Broncos special teams coach Darren Rizzi said most of the Australian punters he has worked with in his long coaching career, including the Broncos' Jeremy Crawshaw , have not kicked field goals.

 So the Broncos need a contingency plan in case  Wil Lutz gets injured in a game. And with Lutz and several Broncos coaches, including Sean Payton, in Canton, Ohio, to see Drew Brees be enshrined into the Hall of Fame, it was Jones getting the kicks.

 Rizzi said Jones' longest made field goal was 39 yards, but Jones said he made a 50-yarder in OTAs. At one point, as Jones moved into position before the snap, the crowd of several thousand people chanted his name.

 "Have a lot of respect for kickers when the crowd started chanting my name, I got really nervous, and I'm like, 'I'm about to shank this,' but thankfully it went in," Jones said.

 Jones was 2-of-2 from the center of the field, 1-of-2 from the left hashmark.

 Other observations: 

 
 With wide receiver  Courtland Sutton getting some rest days in camp to go with recent injuries to Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims Jr ., Pat Bryant has consistently made play after play as a reliable option for quarterback  Bo Nix . Bryant's leaping, get-the-toes-down scoring grab in red zone work was just another example. Bryant leaped over a double-team of Ja'Quan McMillian and Jahdae Barron to make the catch. Offensive coordinator Davis Webb said, "Man, Patty Ice has had some really, really good practices." 
 The Broncos closed out a stretch of six consecutive days on the practice field with a scripted scrimmage, but held out some of their healthy high-profile players, including cornerback Pat Surtain II , tackle Mike McGlinchey , safety Talanoa Hufanga and running back J.K. Dobbins . 
 The defense shut down both two-minute drives by the offense to close out the practice -- the situation was offense trailing by four with 1:14 left in the game. Nix led the first group, and  Sam Ehlinger led the other, which made it to the 8-yard line before the defense was credited with a sack to end the drive. 
 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 If Broncos coach Sean Payton checks his phone on his flight to Canton, Ohio, on Friday he isn't going to like some of the messages. It was a rugged day of practice, as wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr ., tight end Nate Adkins and defensive lineman Matt Henningsen left with injuries.

 Mims pulled up after running a deep route and hopped off the field before he went to the locker room. Adkins walked into the locker room with Mims and a trainer while Henningsen, who missed last season with a ruptured Achilles he suffered in last summer's camp, was carted to the locker room with an apparent leg injury.

 That comes in addition to the other injuries the Broncos suffered already this week to wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (leg) and edge rusher Nik Bonitto (ankle/foot). Bonitto returned to practice Friday on a limited basis.

 More observations: 

 
 Payton, several assistant coaches and kicker Wil Lutz left during Friday's practice to head to Ohio for the events surrounding Drew Brees' enshrinement into the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Payton will be Brees' presenter at the Gold Jacket dinner Friday night and at the enshrinement ceremony Saturday. The group had all been with the New Orleans Saints during Brees' career. 
 Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph ran practice after Payton left and will run Saturday's workout in which the Broncos will go through a controlled scrimmage. Joseph spoke to the team at the end of practice as Payton usually does and cornerback Ja'Quan McMillian said he told Joseph "head coach looks good on you." 
 Wide receiver Courtland Sutton practiced fully Friday, while offensive tackle  Garett Bolles , defensive tackle D.J. Jones and defensive tackle Malcolm Roach had rest days. 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle , who left practice Wednesday with what appeared to be a left leg injury, did not practice Thursday and moved gingerly between drills as he watched practice. Coach Sean Payton said after practice Waddle had suffered a "strain" and "I think we'll see him back in the next four to five days."

 The Broncos practice Friday and Saturday before a player's off day Sunday. They have three full practice days next week before a travel day for their Aug. 14 preseason opener in Atlanta. Waddle's status for that preseason opener, which is when Payton typically plays starters at least one quarter, is still a question mark.

 More observations: 

 
 Courtland Sutton , who had been held out the previous two days for rest, participated on a limited basis and is expected to practice fully Friday. Payton said Sutton is not injured, but the rest schedule is "our protocol" for Sutton and that other veteran players in the coming weeks will have similar schedules. Sutton said the team's training staff showed him tracking data from practices late in the season last year to talk to him about trying to pace him better through the season. "Last year I kind of got ran into the ground going into the end part of the season ... just trying to make sure the body stays as fresh as possible as late in the season as possible," he said. 
 Former Broncos coach Mike Shanahan, the franchise's winningest coach, including back-to-back Super Bowl wins to close out the 1997 and 1998 seasons, was at practice Thursday and received a tour of the team's new $178 million facility. 
 

 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle left Wednesday's practice and did not return. The Broncos' main offseason addition slowed down during a play in a team period and walked off to the locker room. He did not return to practice. Coach Sean Payton said after the workout that Waddle would be "fine" after the initial exam by the team's medical staff. "But we'll evaluate him ... he had some muscle tightness," he added.

 Payton has said repeatedly "we'll be smart" about returning players to practice after injuries. With the Broncos still nine days away from their preseason opener, Waddle could be held out of some practice time in the remainder of the week. Courtland Sutton was also given his second consecutive off day, so Marvin Mims Jr ., Troy Franklin and Pat Bryant got the bulk of the work with the starters after Waddle left the field. Payton said Sutton would practice Thursday.

 More observations: 

 
 Franklin and Bryant each had explosive plays in team drills Wednesday and Franklin might have had his best day of camp overall. The receiver combination of Sutton, Waddle, Mims, Franklin and Bryant -- if healthy -- looks like it will be the top five, so the Broncos would have to keep six receivers for another wideout…

title: Looking at Russell Wilson's complicated Hall of Fame case
summary: Wilson looked to be well on his way to the Hall after 10 seasons, but a rough end to his career has complicated his candidacy.
full_text:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- When the Denver Broncos formally introduced Russell Wilson as their new starting quarterback in March 2022, there were many with the team and around the NFL who believed Wilson already had a résumé worthy of the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

 In 10 seasons with the Seattle Seahawks , Wilson had won a lot. He led Seattle to eight playoff appearances and two Super Bowls, culminating with a Super Bowl XLVIII win over the Broncos to conclude the 2013 season. He also excelled individually, making the Pro Bowl nine times and having four consecutive seasons of 30-plus touchdown passes from 2017 to 2020, including a league-leading 34 in 2017 and a career-best 40 in 2020.

 Then Denver sent a package including two first-round picks to Seattle to acquire Wilson . The Broncos believed he could help break a then-six-season playoff drought and return them to Super Bowl contender status, showering Wilson with a franchise-record five-year, $245 million deal . Wilson was giddy in the introductory news conference , saying his goal was to play "10 or 12 more years and hopefully win three or four more Super Bowls."

 But Wilson struggled mightily in two seasons with the Broncos and two more with the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Giants before retiring this offseason . And with the Hall's Class of 2026 -- a class that includes a first-ballot quarterback in Drew Brees -- set to be enshrined Saturday, Wilson's future Canton possibilities seem cloudy, with his late-career struggles casting doubt on whether he'll make it to the Hall.

 Wilson, who signed on to be an analyst for CBS after his retirement, now faces an uphill Hall of Fame climb because of a historic plunge in performance and a narrowing process for selection that has added difficulty for players to be enshrined, especially at a competitive quarterback position. Wilson won't be eligible to be inducted until the Class of 2031, but ESPN spoke to two dozen people -- some in the league and some involved with the Hall of Fame process -- to get an idea of where his case stands.

 

 WILSON'S PRIME WAS Hall of Fame level. His combination of passing ability, mobility and a penchant for late-game heroics was key to the Seahawks' considerable success in the 2010s. Along with eight 10-win seasons from 2012 to 2021 and nine playoff victories, Wilson also produced on the stat sheet. He threw for 4,212 yards and 40 touchdowns while rushing for 513 yards in 2020. He also ran for 849 yards in 2014, a season in which he rushed for 47 first downs.

 Wilson's 292 touchdown passes from 2012-21 was the second most in league history for a quarterback in his first 10 NFL seasons, behind only Peyton Manning's 306. And Tom Brady (324) and Aaron Rodgers (317) were the only two players with more touchdown passes than Wilson during his 10-year run in Seattle. Wilson's 113 wins as a starting quarterback (regular season and postseason combined) was the most for any NFL player in his first 10 seasons, too.

 

 But while quarterbacks typically see a drop in performance in the final years of their careers, Wilson barreled over a statistical cliff. The last four seasons of his career saw him frequently benched , and his teams went 17-27 in games he started. His production nosedived as his mobility waned. He was sacked an astounding 143 times in 47 games from 2022 to 2025, including 100 times in two seasons (30 starts) with the Broncos.

 Four of Wilson's five lowest yards per attempt totals of his career came after he left Seattle. Over his last five seasons, including his final one with the Seahawks, Wilson's completion percentage over expectation was in the negative three times, with a career-low minus-4.3% in 2022 in Denver.

 That rough finishing kick has made an impact on Hall of Fame voters.

 "Russell Wilson was a good quarterback for two-thirds of his career, a very good quarterback,'' longtime selector Ron Borges said. "[But] the Hall of Fame is not the Hall of Very Good, it is where the best to ever play their positions go.

 "Was Wilson ever considered the best of his era? If he was not, and I would argue he was not, how can he be judged one of the best of all time?"

 Sure, Wilson's counting stats are certainly Hall worthy. His 46,966 career passing yards ranks 16th (right behind Hall of Famer Fran Tarkenton), and his 353 passing touchdowns ranks 12th (ahead of Tarkenton and fellow Hall of Famer John Elway). But there is little precedent for the type of statistical drop-off Wilson had at the end of his career.

 "In short, can you play your way out of the Hall of Fame? His final four years are really bad, and they are made even worse by the whole move to force his way out [of Seattle] and prove himself,'' said Jason Cole, a selector for over a decade who says he believes Wilson is a Hall of Famer. "It exposed so many of the flaws that were covered up in Seattle. At the same time, his first 10 years are really pretty damn exceptional."

 Wilson was never a first-team All-Pro selection -- he was a second-team selection once -- and was not selected to the 2010s All-Decade team. And there is also the perception that the Seahawks' success was more a product of Seattle's "Legion of Boom" defense than of Wilson. The Seahawks' defense allowed fewer than 300 points in the first five seasons of Wilson's tenure (2012-2016), leading the league in scoring defense in four of those years (2012-2015).

 Players from that team's defense will be on the Hall ballot when Wilson becomes eligible for induction. One of them is former All-Pro cornerback Richard Sherman , who gave his thoughts on Wilson's legacy during a "Thursday Night Football" broadcast discussion with Tony Gonzalez last season.

 

 "I think you got to judge his career off when the Legion of Boom was there," Sherman said.

 Sherman is one of several high-profile Seahawks teammates who have levied public criticisms of Wilson, including him being potentially coddled by then-coach Pete Carroll . The Broncos' release of Wilson in March 2024 (and the then-record $85 million dead money hit that resulted from it) is also the type of thing that looms large in Hall of Fame discussions.

 Broncos wide receiver Courtland Sutton , who had a career-best 10 touchdown receptions in 2023 while playing with Wilson, said he believes the quarterback's approach and commitment to the game should matter in these discussions despite how things played out at the end.

 "He was a professional at every level, everything we did, how we met, how we practiced, how we spent post-practice, just to be able to see that from the perspective of being a receiver and being able to work with him,'' Sutton said. "People can say what they want to say about the outcome of how things went, I know what he gave to the game because I saw it day in and day out, how he prepared to go play."

 
 SO WHERE DOES  all this leave voters and Wilson's case?

 Perhaps Kurt Warner (Class of 2017) might have the closest statistical profile in terms of drop in performance to Wilson's among enshrinees from the past three decades. Warner's career had peaks in the beginning and end of his 12 seasons -- with a five-year stretch from 2002 to 2006 in which he didn't exceed 10 starts in any season. But that middle was surrounded by two peaks in which Warner was a two-time league MVP and went to three Super Bowls, winning MVP of Super Bowl XXXIV after leading the St. Louis Rams to the championship.

 Wilson doesn't have the hardware of Warner, but he finished with a QBR of 60 or higher in nine of his first 10 seasons, finishing third behind Manning and Brady with a 74.8 QBR as a rookie in 2012 and fifth with a 71.8 in 2019. He combined for 65 touchdown passes in his final two seasons in Seattle after the Seahawks' Legion of Boom defense started to break apart.

title: 2026 Green Bay Packers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Packers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Green Bay Packers ' camp is taking place in Green Bay, Wisconsin, and Packers reporter Rob Demovsky has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Packers camp. We will update this file often. Will the revamped WR corps help QB Jordan Love and the offense take another step? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Thursday.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news out of Packers camp 
 
 Micah Parsons: Playing vs. Cowboys in Week 6 'realistic' 
 Packers RT changes last name to Bako-Bewele to honor heritage 
 Packers star TE Tucker Kraft activated off PUP after ACL recovery 
 Better, worse or the same: Packers defense 
 Packers CEO: Team needs financial bump to stay competitive 
 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 

 Nothing like a deep-ball touchdown to cover up an offense's warts. That's what  Matthew Golden 's 52-yard touchdown catch from Jordan Love did on Friday night, when the annual Family Night crowd at Lambeau Field otherwise didn't have much to get excited about when it came to the Packers' offense.

 Everyone, however, probably left the stadium with visions of what Love and Golden can do in their second year together. Now, it's possible that edge rusher Brenton Cox Jr . could have blown up the whole play if tackling was allowed because he appeared to be closing in on Love, but everything else about it was picture-perfect. From the throw that sailed through the air to the over-the-shoulder catch by Golden, who got safety Javon Bullard turned around, it was the kind of play that Golden didn't make much last season as a rookie. He's expected to have a much bigger role in the offense this season.

 

 "I feel real confident just taking it day by day and just building chemistry with Jordan, being on the same page with him, communicating as much as I can," Golden said. "I feel like each and every day we go out there in practice, I feel like the chemistry between us is growing for sure."

 
 Trey Smack might have taken some of the pressure off himself after a solid showing. The rookie kicker, who came in 8-for-13 on field goals so far in camp, went 6-for-7 on Friday night. His lone miss was a 51-yarder wide left. Instead of kicking one after another like he had been doing in practice, the coaches gave Smack just a single rep at the end of each team period, making it more game-like. "Definitely, built a little bit of confidence up tonight," Smack said. "But we can always kick better." He will get only one more chance to kick in Lambeau in front of fans before the season because the Packers have just one home preseason game this year. 
 For a defense that wants to increase its takeaways from last year, there sure were some missed opportunities. Both Evan Williams and Xavier McKinney dropped potential interceptions during the team periods. The Packers had only 13 takeaways on defense last season after getting 29 in 2024. 
 Brandon Cisse , Bo Melton , Jacob Monk and  Chris McClellan  all dropped out of practice. Cisse, the rookie second-round pick who was at right cornerback with the No. 1 offense, said he was cramping and needed to hydrate better. McClellan, the rookie defensive lineman, who made a few tackles got rolled up on but said he was fine. Coach Matt LaFleur did not know what happened to Monk, who was the starter at right guard. 
 LaFleur said one of the best parts of Family Night -- besides the post-practice fireworks show and a near-packed stadium -- was having referee Shawn Hochuli and his crew officiate the practice. The Packers have local officials work training camp, but this was the first visit by an NFL crew this summer. "In terms of how they call defensive holding there was a number of those, there was a couple offensive holdings," LaFleur said. "So I think that was really good for our guys to get exposed to that." 
 A local high school football player tied Golden and Will Sheppard by catching five punts off the Jugs machine while having to hold each ball as he caught the next. With four in his arms and one between his knees, he couldn't hold onto No. 6. 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 It would be hard to blame running back  MarShawn Lloyd for getting excited after he scored a touchdown in practice on Thursday.

 
And it would be hard to blame coach Matt LaFleur for telling his oft-injured running back to find a different way to celebrate it.

 
After he caught a touchdown pass from  Jordan Love , Lloyd celebrated with a backflip in the end zone.

 
When the period ended, LaFleur walked over to Lloyd on the sideline.

 
"He said it was cool," Lloyd said. "But he said let's not do that."

 
Receiver Christian Watson has used the same move to celebrate.

 
"And he told him the same thing: Stop doing them," Lloyd said.

 
Lloyd, a third-round pick in 2024, has already made it further into camp than he did last season, when a recurring hamstring injury kept him out the entire season. Previously, he had hip and ankle injuries along with appendicitis that limited him to 10 snaps as a rookie.

 
"Got a long way to go, but when he's out there, he's making plays and he's turning heads," GM Brian Gutekunst said before Thursday's practice. "He always kind of has done that since he's been here, when he's been able to be out there. So yeah, excited for where he's going."

 More observations: 

 
 It's looking more and more like Skyy Moore will have a spot on the opening-day, 53-man roster. And not just as a return specialist. The Packers have liked what they've seen in him as a receiver. The Packers gave Moore a $1 million signing bonus in free agency, but they've cut players with similar bonuses before; kicker Brandon McManus was released this offseason only weeks after he was paid a $1 million roster bonus. "I think Skyy's going to help us as a returner and as a receiver," Gutekunst said. "I expect him to be part of our squad moving forward." 
 Speaking of backup receivers, Isaiah Neyor made an impressive touchdown catch from backup QB Kyle McCord . Neyor fought off tight coverage from safety Kitan Oladapo and spun in the air to bring in the ball. Neyor, who was on the practice squad last season, and undrafted rookie J. Michael Sturdivant could be fighting for the last receiver spot on the roster. Studivant also has been impressive. 
 The coaches want to take a long look at offensive lineman Jacob Monk . With left guard Aaron Banks (knee) still not doing any team drills, Monk has been with the starters. He had been mostly at left guard but moved over to right guard Thursday, which meant Anthony Belton bounced out to right tackle, where regular starter Zach Bako-Bewele (knee) is also not doing team drills. "I love Monk's playstyle," offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said. "He's got the right mindset. He tries to get after people and plays the game the right way. So I've been happy with how he's played so far this camp." 
 Running back Josh Jacobs (groin) missed his first practice of camp. However, the injury is not expected to be a long-term concern. 
 The Packers closed Thursday's practice to fans but are expected to have nearly 60,000 in Lambeau Field for Friday's annual Family Night practice. 
 J.J. Watt was a visitor at practice. The Milwaukee-area native never got the chance to play for his home-state team, although he was reportedly interested in doing so before he signed with the Cardinals in 2021. Watt is expected to be part of the CBS broadcast crew for the Week 1 game against the Vikings.

title: 2026 Houston Texans training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Houston Texans training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Houston Texans ' camp is taking place in Houston at at NRG Park., and Texans reporter D.J. Bien-Aime has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Texans camp 
 
 Tank Dell returns to practice for first time since 2024 
 Houston bringing back former No. 1 pick Clowney 
 Texans have 'productive' contract talks with Stroud 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 The Texans held a night practice on Saturday. It was not pretty for the Texans offense as quarterback C.J. Stroud had many incompletions and the run game had little running room.

 However, the defense displayed the potential of a top-three unit in the NFL. There were plenty of sacks, an interception from Pro Bowl safety  Calen Bullock  and pass break ups. But most importantly, they're not satisfied. Texans defensive coordinator Matt Burke's assessment of the defense was "okay."

 Burke said Houston is chasing perfection defensively.

 

 
 Friday, Aug. 7 

 After an off day, the Texans dialed back their intensity as they went through drills without pads, but notably, wide receiver  Tank Dell practiced for the second straight day of training camp, albeit in a limited capacity.

 It's another step in Dell's recovery, with Wednesday being his first time practicing since he suffered multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap in Week 16 of 2024.

 Speaking to the media for the first time, Dell said he had no fear in the strength of his knee, pointing towards Houston's doctor stating his knee is "100 percent stable." 

 "Trusting the work you put in prior to going out there," said Dell when asked about trusting in his health. "Going out there to put your foot in the ground, trusting the process with the training staff and what they had set out for me. So when I got out here, I wasn't scared."﻿

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 Wideout Tank Dell made his return to the practice field, participating in limited capacity. It marked the first time he engaged in any sort of team padded practice since Week 16 of 2024 after the 2023 third-round pick suffered multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap against the Chiefs.

 He caught a few passes from quarterback C.J. Stroud during individual drills and ran full speed routes.

 Dell didn't do much more after that, but this is the step in the right direction. Coach DeMeco Ryans won't rush Dell back and said "Tank is on the right plan." The goal is have him ready for team 11-on-11 contact reps. He still has a ways to go, but this is positive progress.

 Other observation:  

 Wideout Jayden Higgins continue to flash throughout practice. He made another impressive catch with Derek Stingley Jr . in coverage. It was a tightly contested catch but that's always a positive because it's against an All-Pro corner.

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 Texans wideout Jayden Higgins is starting to blossom as he's entering Year 2. When Pro Bowl wideout Nico Collins  was asked about Higgins' progression he said "He's hooping right now, and I can't wait to see him rock out when it really matters."

 During Tuesday's practice, Higgins made multiple catches with All-Pro cornerback  Derek Stingley Jr . in coverage. One of those receptions occurred during a team third-down period for a 20-yard gain. The other one was during 1-on-1s -- where Stingley tried to aggressively jam Higgins, but he avoided the powerful jab and broke free for an easy toss from quarterback C.J. Stroud .

 Early in camp, Stroud said he expected Higgins to have a "dominant" Year 2, and so far we are starting to see it.

 Other observation:  

 Linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair was slow to get up after a collision with tight end Dalton Schultz . Al-Shaair was fine shortly after.

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 This was Day 1 of padded practices, and the defense shined. Quarterback C.J. Stroud  was forced to hold the ball longer than he would like as the secondary coverage was stout.

 Stroud occasionally scrambled more than usual to buy time to make throws and the defensive line forced a few sacks. Safety Calen Bullock intercepted Stroud.

 Also coach DeMeco Ryans used exotic blitzes throughout the day, and the offense sometimes had answers and other times didn't. Ryans deemed the first day in full pads as "successful." 

 Other observation: 

 First-round pick Keylan Rutledge is adding an extra juice of aggression to the unit. He got into a mini tussle with defensive end Danielle Hunter after a successful run play by running back Woody Marks .

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Saturday's padless practice featured more back and forth from the offense and defense. Some periods the defense dominated and others, the offense was able to counter their blitzing.

 The Texans start padded practices on Monday and that will be a "big part" of the evaluation process for the team according to coach DeMeco Ryans.

 The fourth-year head coach said: "There's a lot of all-stars in shorts," and later added the staff wouldn't be fooled by what players have done without pads.

 Another observation: 

 
 Cornerback Derek Stingley Jr collided with linebacker Henry To'oTo'o and was slow to get up, but he shook it off and was back on the field. 
 

 

 Friday, July 31 
 It was mainly walk-throughs for the Texans. It's a theme that's been consistent for coach DeMeco Ryans throughout the offseason -- where he has focused on helping his team mentally work toward executing deep in the playoffs.

 "I've grown as a head coach," Ryans said in June. "For me, it's more so now about how much smarter can we play as a team. How can we be more elite on our execution? Our communication, can it be louder? Can we echo it more? Can we truly be tied together every time we line up? That's what I've seen when I talk about the process of us this year being better."

 Saturday's practice will be the first day with fans in attendance since training camp has opened. That will be a longer practice with more intensity compared to today's practice that was roughly a little over an hour.

 

 

 Thursday, July 30 
 The passing attack was centered around the quick game time to throw on Day 2 of practice. Quarterback C.J. Stroud was quick and decisive with his throws with all but one of his throws being made under 2.8 seconds, and his only rep over three seconds was when he extended the play and tried to find wideout Jayden Higgins in the back of the end zone.

 It fell incomplete, but the majority of his throws came with precision and decisiveness. Stroud was able to connect a few times with Higgins, who's development in Year 2 will be huge for the offense.

 Other observation:  

 
 Backup cornerback Alijah Huzzie was able to make a nice interception off of backup QB  Davis Mills  -- where took the ball away from the intended receiver. 
 
 
 Wednesday, July 29 
 The Texans were more forthcoming regarding contract discussions than normal. General manager Nick Caserio said there's a "possibility" the team and quarterback C.J. Stroud can reach a contract extension. Stroud isn't focused much on contract discussions; he's letting his agent handle it as he is "keeping the main thing the main thing."

 Stroud is going into Year 4 and is eligible for an extension for the first time in his career. Coach DeMeco Ryans said he doesn't get into a lot of deep discussions with guys when it comes to contract situations.

 But he added, "I truly believe you get…

title: 2026 Indianapolis Colts training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Colts training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Indianapolis Colts ' camp is taking place in Grand Park Sports Campus, Westfield, Indiana, and Colts reporter Stephen Holder has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Colts camp. We will update this file often. Will quarterback  Daniel Jones return to early-2025 form after a serious injury? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Colts stories 
 
 Tons at stake as Colts' Daniel Jones enters proving ground 
 Colts won't give Richardson away 
 Colts extend Jonathan Taylor for 2 years, $44 million 
 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 The Colts are still working to identify their best lineup at linebacker, and it's beginning to look like they might not have the luxury of settling in with a consistent starting group.

 Defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo left open the possibility that the Colts might use a rotation of players at the position, with situations dictating who plays when. The issues are being currently exacerbated by the absence of projected starting middle linebacker CJ Allen (hamstring), the team's second-round pick.

 "At the end of the day, I think we're going to have a lot of guys in that room that play for us this year in different types of roles," Anarumo said.

 Having two rookies -- Allen and Bryce Boettcher -- among the leading candidates to start, is a factor, Anarumo said. Streamlining young players' responsibilities can allow for faster growth.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Receiver Josh Downs missed practice with a groin injury, leaving the Colts without their top two wideouts. Alec Pierce remains sidelined after offseason ankle surgery, and the Colts have provided no specific timeline for his return. 
 Riley Leonard was the second-team quarterback behind Daniel Jones , with Anthony Richardson Sr . playing with the third team. 
 

 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 Starting quarterback Daniel Jones had one of his best days in Thursday's evening practice, connecting on a number of aggressive, downfield throws. But the same could not be said of the quarterbacks behind him on the depth chart.

 Anthony Richardson Sr . and Riley Leonard , locked in a battle for the backup job, have yet to establish the consistency that coach Shane Steichen is seeking. That continued on Thursday, when Leonard threw an interception to linebacker Austin Ajiake and Richardson was inefficient in his time under center.

 "The guy that's most consistent is going to win that job," Steichen said. "Those guys are battling. It's back and forth right now." He added, "There's been flashes, but yeah, there's work to done for sure."

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 One week into camp and perhaps the biggest question is not a question at all.

 Quarterback Daniel Jones has not missed a single snap with the first-team offense and has not taken any days off from practice. This comes in spite of him only recently being fully cleared to practice in full-team drills following his Achilles tendon tear in December. If there were any uncertainties entering this camp, Jones has put them to rest.

 "I've felt good through the whole camp so far," Jones said. "I knew I would. You try to push yourself in the rehab in preparation for camp, knowing what to expect. I felt really good and I stay on the recovery part of it to make sure I'm available and out here every day."

 The Colts are five practices in and there are no known plans to pull back on Jones' workload.

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward have been making life difficult for the team's wide receivers so far in camp, much to the Colts' contentment.

 Gardner and Ward are expected to be among the best cornerback combos in the league this season if they can both remain on the field. That was not the case last season, when they spent just one full game on the field together because of respective injuries.

 The length of both players has been especially challenging for the receivers, a group that is trying to find its way with the No. 3 spot still up for grabs.

 "When you can go up against two of the best in the league in practice every day, it's going to make everybody better," coach Shane Steichen said.

 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 The Colts spent most of Saturday's workout focused on red zone play, with the offense and defense more or less playing to a draw in terms of success. Among the highlights was tight end Tyler Warren 's leaping catch in the end zone for a touchdown from quarterback Daniel Jones . Another impressive completion came when Jones delivered a strike to receiver Josh Downs in the corner of the end zone.

 But the defense held its own, too, forcing Jones and quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr . to scramble out of the pocket multiple times in 7-on-7 and in full-team periods.

 Additionally, cornerback Sauce Gardner had an athletic pass deflection against Downs to stop a red zone threat.

 More observations: 

 

 Friday, July 31 

 Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon spoke to reporters for the first time in several months and revealed the details of her address to the team this week. On the heels of last season's massive collapse -- a seven-game losing streak to end the Colts' season -- Irsay-Gordon emphasized the need to finish.

 "As we reflected on last season, this one phrase just kept coming to my mind," she said. "And that was 'Find a way.' So that was the mantra that we settled on for this season. And we came to 'find a way' because we thought about what are the qualities that successful people have? And those qualities are consistency, those qualities are resilience."

 The Colts lost quarterback Daniel Jones and players such as  Sauce Gardner and DeForest Buckner down the stretch last season. But Irsay-Gordon emphasized that injuries would not be a cop-out this season, when general manager Chris Ballard and coach Shane Steichen are considered to be on the hot seat.

 More observations from the day: 

 

 Thursday, July 30 

 Cornerback Charvarius Ward has had a strong start to camp, something that is especially notable given where he was just seven months ago: On the verge of retirement.

 Ward previously addressed his change of heart, deciding to return after the 2024 death of his infant daughter and a series of concussions in 2025 nearly pushed him to step away from the NFL. He now says he was "probably 85% sure I was going to retire. But I found a different why, a different purpose. Doing it for Junior [his son], doing it for Amani, my daughter. They bring me joy. They bring a smile to my face."

 Ward, 30, added, "I feel good, I've got a lot of energy. I feel like I still belong out here."

 More observations: 

 

 Wednesday, July 29 
 The last time running back Jonathan Taylor was entering a contract year, he effectively staged a hold-in during training camp, opting out of practice and citing an ankle injury. This time, Taylor is again seeking a new deal, but he was primed and ready to roll on Wednesday, the first day of camp.

 "I have faith," Taylor said. "There've been some good conversations and I have faith between my agent and the front office. Like I said, I've already said I would love to be a Colt for life. So, I have faith that things are moving in the right direction."

 Taylor, who rushed for 1,585 yards last season, is scheduled to become a free agent in the spring.

 More observations from the day:

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Kansas City Chiefs ' camp is taking place at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, Missouri, and Chiefs reporter Nate Taylor has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Chiefs camp. We will update this file often. Can coach Andy Reid get the Chiefs back into the playoffs? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Chiefs camp 
 
 Reid: Mahomes unlikely to play in preseason opener 
 Rookie wideout Cyrus Allen an early star of Chiefs training camp 
 Chiefs' Reid: Eric Bieniemy's wife out of ICU, 'doing great' 
 As training camp opens, Chiefs point to brighter future in 2026 
 
 
 
 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 More than halfway through camp, the Chiefs finally had a practice where multiple players had physical altercations. Coach Andy Reid doesn't want his players to fight, but he designs the Chiefs' camp to push the players, both physically and mentally.

 This was the sixth consecutive practice before an off day Sunday. After an 11-on-11 repetition, defensive end  Felix Anudike-Uzomah  and left guard Kingsley Suamataia , who kept engaging him after the play was over, got into it. Suamataia even threw a punch with his right hand while several teammates were trying to separate him and Anudike-Uzomah.

 "It's kind of unusual, and we haven't done that in the past," special teams coordinator Dave Toub said of the Chiefs' six straight practices. "It was a little bit of a grinder. It was chippy. That's how you know. It's hot and that's football sometimes."

 Toward the end of practice, the first-team offense was in the middle of the long-drive drill -- a period in which the projected starters had 16 consecutive repetitions -- when running back Kenneth Walker III became frustrated with safety Alohi Gilman . Walker felt Gilman hit more than was necessary when he had the ball near the sideline. After the repetition, Gilman put his face mask directly in front of Walker's. When Gilman shoved his teammate, Walker threw the ball at him and tackled him, which forced multiple teammates to separate them.

 "Going against the same guys and just being competitive, I think that's what's been great about this camp," quarterback Patrick Mahomes said. "It's super competitive on both sides, so little scuffles here and there but nothing crazy. As long as we keep it like that and keep competing, that's where you get the best team you can get."

 Other observations: 

 
 The players who missed practice were right guard Trey Smith (hip), cornerback  L'Jarius Sneed  (rest), linebacker Drue Tranquill (lower back spasms), defensive end Ashton Gillotte (strained right hamstring), defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee) and receiver Xavier Worthy (sprained right shoulder). 
 For the second consecutive practice, Kahlil Benson , the undrafted rookie from Indiana, had his repetitions at right tackle in place of Smith. Jaylon Moore , the five-year veteran, played at right tackle with the first-team offense. 
 Rookie receiver Cyrus Allen , who missed four practices with a left shin injury, participated in the 7-on-7 periods but was held out of 11-on-11 repetitions. Rashee Rice , the Chiefs' No. 1 receiver, participated only in the individual period and left the field early to receive more treatment on his right knee, the same knee he had surgery on in May to remove loose debris that was causing inflammation. 
 Toub revealed Saturday that his top kickoff returners are receiver Nikko Remigio and running back Brashard Smith . "Brashard has taken a really nice step as far as a punt returner," Toub said. "He's catching the ball a lot cleaner. Nikko just keeps getting better. [Allen] was doing a good job up until he got hurt. Now he's back out there catching again, so we've got to continue to develop him." 
 
 

 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 

 One player who is having a steady camp for the Chiefs is defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah , the team's 2023 first-round pick. For most of this week, Anudike-Uzomah has had his reps with the first-team defense, a result of him replacing Ashton Gillotte , who sustained a strained right hamstring in Monday's practice. Rushing from the left side, Anudike-Uzomah has had several strong 11-on-11 reps in which he has won the one-on-one battle with right tackle Kahlil Benson , an undrafted rookie out of Indiana.

 "His get-off is what jumps out to me," Reid said of Anudike-Uzomah. "He's bringing power with it. It's one thing to run around people, but there's a point, as a defensive end, you've got to physically blow things up a little bit. He's worked hard at that."

 Almost a year ago, the Chiefs had to place Anudike-Uzomah on season-ending injured reserve because of a strained right hamstring he sustained in the preseason -- an injury that required surgery. The Chiefs are hopeful that he can be a reliable contributor in the final year of his rookie contract.

 Anudike-Uzomah shared after Friday's practice that he believes he is the healthiest he's been since he entered the NFL.

 "I feel good, so I'm rolling," Anudike-Uzomah said. "I'm happy to work. Adversity happens with everybody. It's just how you respond."

 More observations: 

 
 Rookie receiver Cyrus Allen , who missed the past four practices with a left shin injury, returned to the field, but he was allowed to participate only in the individual period. "We're just easing him back in," Reid said. "He did a good job when he was out there, so that's a positive." 
 The players who missed Friday's on-field work were Gillotte, right guard Trey Smith (hip), cornerbacks Kristian Fulton (hip) and  L'Jarius Sneed  (rest), linebackers Drue Tranquill (lower back spasms) and Jeffrey Bassa (strained groin), defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee), and receiver Xavier Worthy (sprained right shoulder). "One positive about all these injuries is there's nothing that the guys aren't coming back from," Reid said. He later added of Smith: "We sent him to a specialist just to have it checked out. He's going to be OK." 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 The Chiefs had a light practice Thursday, the first such on-field work after three consecutive days in pads. The most significant change was that backup quarterback Justin Fields had his first 11-on-11 reps with the first-team offense, an indication that he might be the starter when the Chiefs have their preseason opener next Saturday against the Los Angeles Rams .

 "I've been learning a lot since I've been here and I'm excited to learn more, especially [coach Andy Reid] and [quarterback Patrick Mahomes ]," Fields said. "They definitely taught me a lot."

 Reid has yet to share if Mahomes, who has surgery in December to repair the torn ACL and LCL in his left knee, will be held out of the preseason, which would be a first in his 10-year career. During Thursday's practice, Fields spent time completing passes to running back Kenneth Walker III and receivers Rashee Rice , Tyquan Thornton and Andrew Armstrong .

 "I'm ready to get back on the field and in game mode, to be honest," Fields said. "It should be fun for the guys that are going to get out there and especially the rookies."

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 Rashee Rice , the Chiefs' No. 1 receiver, participated in 11-on-11 repetitions, a positive sign that his acclimation process is going well. In May, Rice underwent surgery on his right knee to remove loose debris that was causing inflammation. Since camp began, the Chiefs have been…

The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Los Angeles Chargers camp is taking place at The Bolt in El Segundo, California, and Chargers reporter Kris Rhim has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Chargers camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 
 Latest from Chargers camp 
 
 Players with the most at stake during Chargers' training camp 
 Tracking 2026 NFL hold-ins: Tuipulotu 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 8 

 Rookie left guard Jake Slaughter got his first reps with the group blocking for Justin Herbert in a padded practice this training camp. The Chargers drafted Slaughter -- who played only center in college -- to be the team's starter at left guard, but he seemed to fall out of favor through camp as veteran Kayode Awosika and second-year lineman Branson Taylor emerged.

 Slaughter fared well in his reps at guard, showing a firm anchor when pressured from defensive tackles and the ability to pick up defensive stunts. His best moment came on a pancake block of defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson , but he was also beaten badly on a rep by defensive tackle Justin Eboigbe .

 Other observations: 

 
 Offensve lineman Trevor Penning appears to be falling back in the competition for the starting left guard job. He continues to work largely with the group, blocking for DJ Uiagalelei , though that could still change. 
 Rookie wide receiver Brenen Thompson made an impressive toe-tap catch down the left sideline that drew a roar from the crowd. 
 Outside linebacker Khalil Mack was explosive throughout practice and had several would-be sacks. Tuli Tuipulotu and Nadame Tucker were also consistently disruptive off the edge. 
 Defensive tackles Jamaree Caldwell , Teair Tart and Eboigbe continued to disrupt the run game and generate pressure on the quarterback. 
 Uiagalelei, may have had the throw of the day, a 50 or so yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Derius Davis . 
 Herbert continues to be sharp and on target with his receivers. It appears he -- and the other quarterbacks -- has grown comfortable with the timing of McDaniel's offense. Receivers are getting passes early and in space. 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 The Chargers' five-man race for guard continued Thursday with a new twist, as second-year lineman Branson Taylor took all the reps with quarterback Justin Herbert 's group at left guard. Before Thursday, two players had rotated at left guard, but Taylor got all of the reps with the first group in the team's first true padded practice.

 Taylor, a sixth-round pick in last year's draft who didn't make the 2025 53-man roster, was mainly a practice squad player last season. One year later, it seems that he has impressed the staff enough to have a legitimate shot at starting. On Thursday, Taylor fared well, creating running lanes and protecting Herbert throughout, a much-improved version of the player at camp last year.

 Coach Jim Harbaugh said on Wednesday that veteran Kayode Awosika was leading the race to start, and that Taylor, Pipkins, Trevor Penning and rookie Jake Slaughter were in the mix.

 Other observations:  

 
 OLB  Tuli Tuipulotu participated in team drills during Wednesday's padded practice, his second day in a row after not participating in team drills for the first six days of training camp. Harbaugh originally said that Tuipulotu's absence was being "handled internally," then later said it was a "ramp up." Neither Tuipulotu, his representatives, or the Chargers have acknowledged a contract-related absence, but his return to the field signals that whatever matter was being handled internally is resolved. 
 Rookie S  Genesis Smith intercepted Justin Herbert after a pass went through Charlie Kolar's hands. 
 CB  Donte Jackson had an impressive diving pass breakup on a pass by QB  Trey Lance during 7-on-7 that led to an interception by safety Elijah Molden . 
 DT  Justin Eboigbe continued his strong camp, consistently generating interior pressure 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 Outside linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu , who has been a limited participant in practice this training camp amid ongoing contract negotiations, was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. The caveat is that the practice was a walkthrough, so Tuipulotu and the other Chargers players were going at half speed. He still has yet to participate in a non-walkthrough practice 11-on-11 period, but his participation on Wednesday could be a sign that things could be headed toward a resolution.

 Other observations:  

 
 After an injury scare Tuesday scare to the same left leg in which he sustained a season-ending patellar tendon rupture last year, left tackle Rashawn Slater was a full participant in practice Wednesday without any limitations. 
 Branson Taylor and Trevor Penning rotated at left guard, continuing the five man race for this starting job. Rookie Jake Slaughter continues to play center with the second group. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 

 The Chargers had their first major injury scare Tuesday as left tackle Rashawn Slater appeared to sustain an injury to his left leg at practice. Slater went to the medical tent with a trainer and then did some on-field testing but didn't return to practice. Branson Taylor and Trey Pipkins III rotated at tackle in his absence.

 Slater ruptured the patella tendon in his left knee during last year's training camp, which forced him to miss the entire season. He appeared in good spirits after practice, walking around and taking pictures with his family.

 Quarterback Justin Herbert said that Slater told him he was healthy enough to return to the field.

 "He said he wanted to be out there, so I think that's okay," Herbert said.

 Other observations: 

 
 OLB Tuli Tuipulotu participated in one 7-on-7 rep but did not take part in the remainder of team drills, marking his sixth straight practice with limited participation as his contract situation remains unresolved. 
 Coach Jim Harbaugh said that Kayode Awosika is leading the competition to start at left guard, but added that Pipkins, Jake Slaughter and Taylor are all in the mix. Harbaugh said that he'd like to name a starter after the next ten practices. 
 The offense came out sharp, with Herbert completing his first eight passes before safety RJ Mickens broke up a pass. From there, the offense and defense traded wins throughout the rest of practice. 
 S Kendall Williamson intercepted Herbert on a pass that was intended for wide receiver Ladd McConkey . "That was nice. He snagged it," Derwin James Jr . said. 
 OLB  Nadame Tucker  had one of his best practices of camp, consistently generating pressure and recording three would-be sacks. 
 DT Teair Tart was disruptive throughout, including what likely would have been at least one sack. The Chargers' interior defensive line generated pressure throughout the day. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Monday's practice was one of the better days for the defense, as they were constantly disruptive throughout. Undrafted cornerbacks Rodney Shelley and Avery Smith were among the stars. Smith continued his strong start to camp with another good day, as he intercepted quarterback DJ Uiagalele i and had an impressive pass breakup on a Justin Herbert pass. Shelley was sticky in coverage throughout and had a few pass breakups, celebrating after each.

 The rookies will have their first NFL training camp practice in pads on Tuesday at the University of San Diego, a chance to affirm the way they've been playing.
