full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Los Angeles Rams  camp is taking place at Loyola Marymount University in L.A. Rams reporter Sarah Barshop has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Rams camp. We will update this file often. Can the Rams live up to the hype? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Rams camp 
 
 Sean McVay praises Aaron Donald as Rams await DT's decision 
 Myles Garrett out third straight day with soreness 
 Puka Nacua says it 'never crossed my mind' to not take part in camp 
 Rams unveil two new alternate uniforms for 2026 
 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 In the Rams' return to their Woodland Hills facility for the remainder of the preseason, "the defense was outstanding," coach Sean McVay said.

 "There was great coverage, some great individual plays, disrupting timing and rhythm," McVay said. "It was a great day for the defense. Offensively they were able to run the football with some success, but throwing and catching was a real struggle."

 McVay said he was not discouraged by the performance by the offense, because the takeaways "were more of a reflection of great individual plays than necessarily poor execution."

 "What I get upset about is when the other opponent or whether the other side of the ball doesn't have to earn it because it's sloppy -- whether it's poor execution or communication on one side or the other," McVay said. "The plays that happened today, there was a handful of turnovers, but I thought it was a really great reflection of excellent execution defensively, some outstanding individual plays. And sometimes that's the price of doing business."

 And that defense might even get stronger as the Rams await the news of a possible return from defensive tackle Aaron Donald. McVay said Saturday that he did not have an update on Donald's decision.

 Other observations: 

 
 First-round pick Ty Simpson will "definitely" play in the first preseason game next Saturday against the Kansas City Chiefs , McVay said. 
 McVay said he has not made a decision on whether  Stetson Bennett IV  will play in the game. McVay typically does not play his starters or key backups in preseason games. Last year Jimmy Garoppolo , the Rams' established backup quarterback, did not play. Bennett and Simpson are competing to back up starting quarterback Matthew Stafford , but if Bennett does not play, that could be an indication he will start the season in the backup role. 
 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 Much of the talk during Rams training camp has been about a player not currently on the roster: Aaron Donald.

 On Thursday, as the Rams concluded training camp at Loyola Marymount University, coach Sean McVay said he didn't have an answer on whether the defensive tackle would come out of retirement.

 And if Donald does return? While defensive coordinator Chris Shula emphasized he's focusing on the roster guys now, he said, "I think I'd be lying if I said I hadn't thought about" the possibility of pairing up Donald and reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett .

 "You're anticipating, but at the same time, we're putting it in the core of our defense right now," Shula said. "We're building our defense step by step. If he decides to come, whenever that is, that's not going to affect exactly how we're doing it right now."

 McVay said Thursday that if Donald comes back, "those are things that you have to be able to figure out on the fly."

 "But what we are focusing on is the guys that are here," McVay said. "And then if Aaron is a part of it, it's obviously going to add value to our group, which is a positive."

 Another observation: 

 
 Thursday was the Rams' final practice at LMU before they head back to their team facility in Woodland Hills for the remainder of the preseason. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 The Rams had a familiar face at their team facility this week, as Aaron Donald's name appeared on the NFL's transaction wire on Wednesday as a player taking part in a tryout for the team.

 The workout had to be reported to the league because it was supervised by a member of the Rams' football staff. Defensive coordinator Chris Shula said he was not at the Woodland Hills facility for the tryout, but said he talked to defensive line coach Giff Smith afterward.

 Last week, Rams head coach Sean McVay said he doesn't expect Donald to make a decision about coming out of retirement until after the team returns to its facility in Woodland Hills. The Rams' final practice at LMU is scheduled for Friday.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Defensive end Myles Garrett returned to practice on Wednesday after missing the last four practices with a little "lower body soreness." Garrett said he feels good and that the Rams were just trying to make sure he got back "100%." 
 Garrett was asked whether he feels like he can play with more "freedom" during practices in Los Angeles. He said that was a good way to describe the way the coaching staff allows players to play. "Not being punished or critiqued for trying to make a play," Garrett said. "There's guidelines and boundaries you got to stay within in the defense, but as long as we put ourselves in the right spots, they're all for it." 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 
 The Rams finished their second training camp block on Monday with what head coach Sean McVay called more of an unscripted practice. Matthew Stafford and  Stetson Bennett IV  took all of the quarterback reps for the Rams, with rookie Ty Simpson only taking part in individual drills.

 The first-team offense and the secondary exchanged several standout plays, including a pass breakup on receiver Puka Nacua by cornerback Trent McDuffie . Later, Stafford found wide receiver Davante Adams for a completion down the sideline.

 "I thought there was especially some really good back and forth with the ones," McVay said after practice. "Some really good plays on both sides, but that's what we're looking for is good quality play where you can really see guys playing through the cycle of the snap."

 McVay pointed to "some big breakups down the field" by McDuffie and cornerback Jaylen Watson .

 "Guys made plays on both sides and it felt like it was a quality operation," McVay said.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 
 McVay said he hasn't determined how he will allocate reps during the preseason between the quarterbacks other than Stafford not playing in any preseason games. Last year, Stafford and Jimmy Garoppolo sat out of the preseason while Bennett started the first two preseason games.

 
 
 Rams tight end Davis Allen is dealing with a quad injury. McVay said the Rams will give Allen "some time" before he returns to practice because it's a soft tissue injury. "You don't want to rush him back," McVay said. "He's played a lot of football and it'll give ... some of these other tight ends an opportunity to get snaps they wouldn't otherwise. But Davis is going to be a big part of what we do this year."

 
 
 Garrett (lower body soreness) did not practice for the fourth straight day. The Rams will re-evaluate him after the Tuesday off day.

 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 2 
 Coach Sean McVay praised quarterback  Stetson Bennett IV 's growth from last training camp, pointing out "the ownership of the offense" he has now.

 Bennett got the majority of the second-team reps last training camp while Matthew Stafford was dealing with a back injury and Jimmy Garoppolo was with the first team.

title: 2026 Las Vegas Raiders training camp: Latest intel, updates

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Las Vegas Raiders  camp is taking place at Intermountain Health Performance Center in Henderson, Nevada, and Raiders reporter Ryan McFadden has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Raiders camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 
 

 Latest news from Raiders camp 
 
 Maxx Crosby's approaching Raiders training camp with intensity 
 Three-time Pro Bowl guard Andrus Peat announces retirement 
 Cousins gets nod over Mendoza to open Raiders camp 
 What's next for Crosby, WR and CB rooms? 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 With  Kirk Cousins and Maxx Crosby  not practicing for violating team rules ,  Fernando Mendoza  played with the starters for the first time in camp.

 Mendoza had his good and bad moments. He overthrew wide receiver Jack Bech a couple of times. And he had trouble securing the ball when snapped to him by Tyler Linderbaum and Jordan Meredith .

 Mendoza, however, didn't get flustered. He had one of his best throws of camp during the red zone period. He threw a touchdown pass to Tre Tucker , in which he zipped the ball through tight coverage by cornerback Taron Johnson .

 Mendoza also threw touchdowns to tight ends Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer .

 The highlight of the day was Mendoza's efficiency during the two-minute period to close out practice. He completed five straight passes, including a throw to Tucker in tight coverage, to set up a field goal from kicker Matt Gay .

 During Mendoza's reps with the first-team, quarterback coach Mike Sullivan said the biggest things he was evaluating were the rookie's command of the offense and not panicking in the pocket. Sullivan added that the team is pleased with Mendoza's development.

 Mendoza's comfort and command of the operation have grown since the spring. Sullivan has also noticed improvement in Mendoza's play from under center.

 Other observation: 

 Wide receiver Jalen Nailor and running back Dare Ogunbowale returned to practice after being sidelined Friday. Defensive ends Kwity Paye and Keyron Crawford , wide receiver Dont'e Thornton Jr.  and tight end Carter Runyon did not participate.

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Friday was an eventful morning at Raiders HQ.

 Las Vegas' eighth practice was highlighted by a scuffle between Maxx Crosby and Kirk Cousins . Other than that, both sides made plays throughout the team's third padded practice.

 Cousins was picked off twice in the red zone. First, Crosby disrupted Cousins' pass attempt, causing the ball to be picked off by safety Jeremy Chinn . On the following play, rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses intercepted Cousins in the back corner of the end zone.

 Cousins responded well. He connected with tight ends  Michael Mayer  and Brock Bowers on a few big throws in the middle of the field. He was even efficient during the two-minute period near the end of practice, quickly moving the offense down the field into field-goal range.

 Rookie running back Mike Washington Jr . had an explosive run, in which he ran over cornerback Jermod McCoy and continued to sprint down the field for a big gain.

 Fernando Mendoza  was sharp. His performance was highlighted by a touchdown pass to wide receiver Deven Thompkins during the red zone period. Mendoza zipped the ball through tight coverage

 Other observations: 

 
 Wide receiver Jalen Nailor , defensive ends Kwity Paye and Keyron Crawford , tight end Carter Runyon and running back Dare Ogunbowale did not participate in practice. Second-year wide receiver  Dont'e Thornton Jr . left practice early, but coach Klint Kubiak didn't sound concerned about the various absences. With Nailor out, rookie wide receiver Malik Benson took the majority of the first-team reps on the opposite side of Tre Tucker . "We had a few guys nicked up, and we're trying to be cautious," Kubiak said. 
 Jackson Powers-Johnson and Caleb Rogers alternated first-team reps at right guard. Kubiak said it's a part of the plan the team has in place to figure out the best starting offensive line combination. Right guard has been the only position on the first-team offensive line that has had changes. 
 Kubiak clarified that he didn't take the coaching staff to drinks after the Baltimore Ravens backed out of a trade agreement for Crosby. Making a guest appearance on the "Ball in the Family" podcast, hosted by NBA player Lonzo Ball, Crosby recalled Kubiak called him and said the coaching staff was going to celebrate after the announcement was made. "He is in big trouble for revealing that," Kubiak jokingly said. "We haven't gone out as much as a staff. We have been grinding. We probably need to do that more." 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 Tight end Brock Bowers keeps stacking up good practices.

 On Thursday, Bowers was problematic for the defense and made one of the best plays since the start of camp. During 11-on-11, Bowers caught a deep touchdown pass from quarterback  Kirk Cousins , in which he slipped behind the defense and was left completely wide open near the sideline. Bowers stopped running his route and waited until Cousins launched the ball across the field.

 There were multiple occasions where Bowers beat out linebacker Quay Walker to make catches in the middle of the field.

 Outside of Bowers, it wasn't the best morning for the offense. There were quite a few inaccurate throws and dropped passes. Fernando Mendoza recorded his second interception of camp after his pass slipped through  Malik Benson 's hands and cornerback Darien Porter dove to make a catch.

 Aidan O'Connell  also recorded two interceptions.

 The offense didn't do much during the two-minute period. Cousins' pass to Tre Tucker was broken up by rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses . Cornerback Eric Stokes broke up Cousins' throw to Benson. The offense was penalized twice during that period, as well.

 Other observations:  

 
 Rookie cornerback Jermod McCoy had a rest day and didn't participate in Thursday's practice. Tight end Michael Mayer returned after missing Tuesday's practice with a nose injury. 
 Defensive end Keyron Crawford left practice early after colliding with edge rusher Malcolm Koonce during the team period. Assistant head coach Mike McCoy did not have an update on the rookie's status. 
 The Raiders mixed things up with their starting offensive line for the first time. They had Caleb Rogers and Jackson Powers-Johnson alternate reps at right guard. 
 Rookie safety Treydan Stukes had his first reps with the starting defense. He had a nice pass breakup while working with the second team during the two-minute period. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 

 Through six practices, rookie wide receiver Malik Benson has made a strong case for meaningful snaps this fall.

 In a fairly thin wide receiver room, Benson has been a shining star, and that was the case on Tuesday. His and quarterback  Fernando Mendoza 's connection was on point. Mendoza repeatedly completed throws to Benson on crossing and comeback routes.

 During the one-on-one period, Benson matched up with fellow rookie cornerback Jermod McCoy on a few reps, in which the former Oregon pass catcher showed off his footwork and separation ability to make catches.

 Wide receivers Jalen Nailor and Tre Tucker are essentially options one and two in the room. Benson has emerged as WR3, outplaying Jack Bech and  Dont'e Thornton Jr . thus far. For wide receiver coach Zach Azzanni, the biggest improvement he has seen from…

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Miami Dolphins  camp is taking place in Miami Gardens, and Dolphins reporter Marcel Louis-Jacques has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Dolphins camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Dolphins camp 
 
 Dolphins top pick Proctor embracing NFL learning curve 
 Miami, All-Pro LB Jordyn Brooks reach 3-year, $51.3M extension 
 Dolphins, Aaron Brewer reach 3-year, $52.5 million extension 
 Why Miami's rookies can thrive 
 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 The Dolphins held Saturday's practice at Hard Rock Stadium, but a critical moment occurred before they even set foot on the field.

 Quarterback Malik Willis addressed his teammates Friday, to ensure players continued to uphold the team's standard.

 "I just wanted to talk to the offense and just have a man-to-man conversation," Willis said Saturday. "We got to understand this is a business, and we got to take what we do personally. We got to take pride in it, and we got to do it to the best of our ability -- regardless if we're calling plays to beat the defense or not.

 "We're not calling plays to beat the defense; we're calling the plays that we want to use throughout the year. We're trying to get better at those plays. Whether we win a down or not, are we doing everything that we can do to execute the playcall?"

 Rookie offensive tackle Kadyn Proctor reference Willis' speech unprompted after practice, so the message appears to have stuck.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Wide receiver Tahj Washington made receptions of 50 and 30 yards on balls from Cam Miller and Quinn Ewers , and rookie wide receiver  Donaven McCulley  brought down a 45-yard pass from Miller in traffic, shaking off a facemask penalty in the process. 
 Safety Tanner Wall , who signed with the Dolphins on Friday, wasted no time making his presence known in his first practice with the team. He broke up a pass in the end zone during red zone drills to save a touchdown. 
 Kicker Zane Gonzalez appeared to leave the practice field after special teams work and did not return. Riley Patterson handled all kicks during team drills at the end of practice. 
 Cornerback JuJu Brents missed practice after suffering an undisclosed injury Friday, while safety Dante Trader Jr . missed his third consecutive practice. The team hopes to get Trader back in time for next week's practice with the Commanders. 
 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley has stressed the importance of taking the ball away to his defense, and his players have responded with gusto this summer. Miami's defense recorded four interceptions during Friday's practice, including two by second-year cornerback Miles Battle -- both off quarterback Quinn Ewers . Linebacker Jackson Woodard continued his strong week of practice with a pick-six off quarterback Mark Gronowski , and UDFA safety Louis Moore added to his big play total with an interception as well.

 The Dolphins defense has forced multiple turnovers in nearly every practice this summer. It's a direct result of the team's coaching points on and off the field.

 "One of our assistant linebacker coaches, Wendel (Davis) -- he starts every meeting with taking the ball away," linebacker Tyrel Dodson said. "So he's made excellent emphasis on those takeaway points and we've honed in on it. We've studied different techniques, punching the ball out. Jacob (Rodriguez is) good at it. So we've studied the Peanut punch and all that stuff. So it's looking good."

 More observations: 

 
 Rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas had an explosive play on a sideline ball from Malik Willis during team drills. The third-round pick appeared to get behind cornerback Jason Marshall Jr and picked up some yards after the catch. 
 Right tackle Austin Jackson returned to practice after missing the past two practices with an undisclosed injury. As a result, defensive end Chop Robinson didn't wreak the same level of havoc he did with Jackson sidelined, but it was a fun matchup to watch. 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 Pressure, pressure and more pressure was the key word for the Dolphins in Thursday's practice. The team shed its shoulder pads, looking to ease back into work following Wednesday's off day, but it didn't stop coach Jeff Hafley's defense from attacking its offensive counterparts throughout team drills.

 Linebacker Jackson Woodard was a constant presence around the ball, while defensive end Chop Robinson continued his strong camp -- albeit against a banged up right side of the Dolphins' offensive line. Thursday also marked another strong performance from rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez ; defensive coordinator Sean Duggan said he could tell the game is starting to slow down for Rodriguez and the other rookie linebackers, Kyle Louis and Trey Moore .

 More conversations: 

 
 Running back Jaylen Wright broke of a couple strong runs during team drills. Speaking to the media earlier this week, he sounded calm and at peace with his career to date and ready to attack the best opportunity he's had for regular playing time since entering the league in 2024. 
 Linebacker Willie Gay Jr . intercepted quarterback Cam Miller and returned it for a long gain. We've seen Gay stand out at training camp before, the Dolphins are hoping his momentum carries into game day this preseason, and the regular season. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 If you were building a basketball team out of Dolphins players, defensive tackle Zach Sieler -- all 6-foot-6, 300 pounds of him -- might be a choice at power forward. But coach Jeff Hafley said the nine-year veteran is actually more of a point guard on the team's defensive line.

 Despite his 25.5 sacks over the past three seasons, Hafley said Sieler's ability and willingness to take on blockers and open rush lanes for his teammates really pops on tape.

 When asked about the comparison after Tuesday's practice, Sieler said it all comes down to being selfless and a team player.

 "You've got to be a leader, you've got to be vocal -- but you can't be selfish," he said. "The better we do as a unit, the better we'll do as a team ... If someone's making plays one day and you're not, the plays will come. Don't stress, because when you stress and try to force a play, that's when bad things happen."

 More observations: 

 
 Defensive end Chop Robinson goes through stretches where he's simply unblockable -- his speed off the line of scrimmage has given the Dolphins' offensive tackles fits all summer, and continued to do so Tuesday. Fellow defensive end Josh Uche also had a pair of sacks in team drills. 
 Right tackle Austin Jackson , tight end Greg Dulcich and safety Lonnie Johnson Jr . did not participate in Tuesday's practice because of what Hafley described as "day to day" injuries. Neither player is expected to miss much time, but rookie UDFA DT Rene Konga will miss the entire season with an undisclosed injury suffered Monday. 
 Quarterback Malik Willis threw an interception to Zayne Anderson on the first play of the team's red-zone drill, but followed it up the next play with a touchdown pass to running back De'Von Achane . 
 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Malik Willis still isn't scrambling in team drills as the Dolphins want him to focus on making plays from the pocket in training camp, but he's displaying a keen ability to evade pressure and keep his eyes downfield.

 On multiple occasions during Monday's practice, Willis kept…

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Minnesota Vikings ' camp is taking place in Eagan, Minnesota, and Vikings reporter Kevin Seifert has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Vikings camp. We will update this file often. Who will win the starting quarterback battle between incumbent J.J. McCarthy and free agent addition Kyler Murray ? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Vikings stories 

 
 What McCarthy-Murray QB battle means for Vikings' locker room 
 Vikings, O'Neill reach $96M extension 
 Top Vikings storylines after minicamp, from QBs to new GM 
 Will Vikings start Caleb Banks, other rookies on defense? 
 Jefferson says decision on Vikings starting QB 'coach's call' 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 Two members of the Vikings' draft class -- both Day 3 picks -- made splash plays during a low-key practice.

 Rookie tailback Demond Claiborne ran about 70 yards off left tackle using a nifty jump cut to get outside. Claiborne, a sixth-round pick from Wake Forest, has mostly worked with the third team behind Aaron Jones Sr . and Jordan Mason . He could also get some work as a kick returner during the preseason.

 Meanwhile, cornerback Charles Demmings -- a fifth-round pick from Stephen F. Austin -- broke up a J.J. McCarthy pass intended for receiver Tai Felton near the goal line. For Demmings, it was the latest in a series of pass breakups, including two earlier in camp while he was defending Justin Jefferson . The Vikings seem to have their top three cornerbacks set with Byron Murphy Jr ., Isaiah Rodgers and James Pierre , and it is always dangerous to get too excited when a rookie makes splash plays. But to this point, he has demonstrated he could provide an immediate contribution this season should defensive coordinator Brian Flores need him. 

 Other observations: 

 
 Veteran Jamal Adams said he appreciates the Vikings giving him a chance to work at safety, the position the New York Jets drafted him as in 2017, and that his new number of 32 is "definitely a better feeling" than the number he opened camp with (54). But Adams agreed it was likely he will also resume his linebacker duties at times in Flores' scheme. "I think it's going to be a little bit of everything, just being versatile in a lot of ways," he said. 
 Adams continued to get first-team work at safety in some packages with fellow safeties Jay Ward and Jakobe Thomas sitting out team drills. 
 Right tackle Brian O'Neill appeared to be taking a veteran's rest day. 
 Receiver Jordan Addison (left thumb) caught passes from quarterbacks for the first time since he suffered the injury while working in some team drills. 
 The Vikings will have their annual night practice Sunday at TCO Stadium. 
 

 
 
 Friday, Aug. 7 
 NFL training camps can be tediously routine at times, but some days close observers can be surprised.

 Friday, the Vikings changed linebacker Jamal Adams ' jersey number from 54 to 32 and worked him in some of their safety specialty packages during full-team drills. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores is well known for experimenting with personnel during training camp, and it's quite possible that Adams could alternate between linebacker and safety.

 Two other safeties, Jay Ward and rookie Jakobe Thomas , did not appear to be taking part in team drills.

 According to NFL rules, linebackers can wear numbers between 1-59 (and also 90-99). But defensive backs can't wear numbers higher than 49, which necessitated Adams' number change.

 Adams was drafted as a safety by the Jets in 2017, but he moved to linebacker for the Raiders last season. The Vikings signed him on the eve of training camp.

 More observations: 

 
 Quarterback J.J. McCarthy had one of his better days of camp as the competition with Kyler Murray continued. McCarthy hit wide receiver  Dontae Fleming  on a deep out, a route McCarthy has excelled at this summer, and also threw three touchdowns in a four-play red zone sequence. 
 
 

 Wednesday, Aug.5 
 The Vikings haven't won a playoff game since 2019 and have three playoff victories in the past 25 seasons. So during his annual training camp meeting with reporters, co-owner/president Mark Wilf was asked about the patience his family has exhibited during its tenure as owners.

 "We try to be patient as an ownership, and that we know [leads to] ultimate success," he said. "But of course, patience isn't infinite. We understand that, but I feel really good about the direction of this football club and we're going to get to those benchmarks."

 Mark and Zygi Wilf hired general manager Nolan Teasley this spring to work with fifth-year coach Kevin O'Connell. Of their early interactions, Mark Wilf said: "I just think they work well together. I had an opportunity to watch them interact, and I just see how comfortable they are with each other. They have different characteristics but from my perspective, it's working well. And I think coach can focus on what he has to focus on. Nolan can focus on what he focuses on and they share and they collaborate and everyone in the building feels that."

 

 More observations: 

 
 Facing pressure during a two-minute drill, quarterback Kyler Murray made a smart decision: He lofted a jump ball for receiver Justin Jefferson . Predictably, Jefferson extended over cornerback Isaiah Rodgers and safety Theo Jackson to make the catch and scoot into the end zone. Murray also had a key scramble during the drill, keeping the drive alive. 
 Receiver Jordan Addison jammed his thumb Tuesday. O'Connell said tests revealed no serious injury. During practice, Addison was in full pads and ran routes during individual drills. But he did not have a pass thrown in his direction, and he worked out on a side field during team drills. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 As members of the 2023 draft class begin getting contract extensions, Vikings receiver Jordan Addison  said Tuesday that he is focused on "being where my feet are."

 Four receivers were drafted between picks No. 20-23 that year, and two of them -- Seattle's Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Baltimore's Zay Flowers -- have agreed to new deals. Addison and the Vikings have had to navigate two arrests and one citation during his time in the NFL, and Addison said: "I'm just putting in the work in right now, going through camp, making sure I'm becoming a better receiver, and I feel like everything is going to take care of itself."

 Addison leads the 2023 class with 22 career touchdown receptions. He ranks eighth with 175 receptions and fourth with 2,396 receiving yards.

 "He loves football," Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said. "He's a great teammate. Clearly he was a young player when he came into the NFL. I think he's learned, matured and he knows exactly what's out in front of him. He knows what's important to him. I'm proud of his growth and development in that phase as well and I think there's a lot of folks in this building that deeply, deeply care about Jordan and what's best for him on and off the field moving forward, and you can count me as one of them."﻿

 More observations: 

 
 The Vikings had a relatively light practice Tuesday in shells, one day after their first full-pads practice of summer. Quarterback J.J. McCarthy elicited murmurs from fans in the stands after overthrowing three consecutive passes in the red zone against no defense, but he came back later with two strong throws on deep outs to receivers  Myles Price  and Dontae Fleming .

title: 2026 New England Patriots training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Patriots training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The New England Patriots ' camp is taking place in Foxborough, Massachusetts, and Patriots reporter Mike Reiss has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Patriots camp. We will update this file often. Will Drake Maye  start another MVP-like campaign in Year 3? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Patriots camp 
 
 A.J. Brown on injury: 'Thumb out of place, you keep going' 
 Patriots' Brown knows Vrabel's rip comes from 'great place' 
 Kraft: Patriots' Gonzalez has offer to be 'highest-paid' CB ever 
 Too many receivers? A look at the Patriots' crowded WR room 
 
 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 A middle linebacker running a time of 4.77 seconds in the 40-yard dash isn't ideal, so when the Patriots hosted Missouri's Khalil Jacobs on a predraft visit in April, coach Mike Vrabel got right to the point.

 "I was trying to just give him a hard time about his 40, and he was like, 'Oh, that was [a] timing [error].'" Vrabel said.

 "I'm like, '32 teams timed your 40 wrong?' But to his credit, he plays a lot faster than the 40. He has a play speed about him."

 Jacobs went undrafted -- probably primarily as a result of the slower 40-yard dash -- but he said he chose to sign with the Patriots because they were the only team to bring him in for a visit.

 That decision looks to be a smart one, as the 6-foot-1, 227-pound Jacobs -- adopting a philosophy of "see ball, get ball" -- has been one of the surprise stories of training camp. He's getting reps on top special teams units, and in recent days seems to have overtaken veteran K.J. Britt for a backup role on defense behind starters Robert Spillane , Christian Elliss and No. 3 option Chad Muma .

 Vrabel said Jacobs "loves football," which shows up with how much time he spends at the team's facility.

 "I see him all the time," the coach said.

 For Jacobs, it ties to proving the Patriots correct for believing in him despite the 40 time.

 "I want whoever wants me," Jacobs said. "These guys showed me love."

 Other observations:  

 
 The Patriots have the weekend off before returning to practice Monday (closed to the public) and then welcoming the Colts to town for a practice Tuesday. 
 WR A.J. Brown summed up this plans for the weekend off succinctly. "Rest," he said. Asked what he's enjoyed about New England as a region, he said he hasn't done much exploring. "I'm a homebody," he said. 
 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 A.J. Brown shared part of what has made his first training camp with the New England Patriots unique from his prior seven NFL seasons.

 "This is my first time going against a defense on a day-to-day basis where the mentality has [picked] up. I believe we need to go against somebody else because we're right at the edge. And that's good for a team, that's really good for a team, but that mentality on both sides of going back and forth, we're toeing that line," he said Friday.

 "That's why I think we're going to be excited for the Colts coming up."

 The Patriots held their 12th practice Friday in humid, 90-degree temperatures, and it featured an intrasquad scrimmage heading into an off weekend. Brown was on the same team as cornerback Christian Gonzalez , which turned down the heat on easily the team's most intense 1-on-1 matchup in camp.

 On Thursday, the two almost needed to be separated after a drill in which Gonzalez had lockdown coverage on Brown, and Gonzalez seemed to be trash-talking in his direction.

 "Every day is a battle with him. It's nothing but respect," Brown said. "Ultimately it's not about me and him. We're competing, all of us are challenging each other, for the greater good of the team."

 For his part, Brown said he's focusing on "crafting" in practice, and if he's doing any talking on the field, it's only to himself. He believes his matchups with Gonzalez have "absolutely" set a tone for the team, which now looks ahead to welcoming the Colts for a practice next Tuesday leading into Thursday's preseason opener.

 "The defense has not been giving us any leeway, and we're not trying to give them any leeway as well," he said. "We're both pushing ourselves."

 More observations: 

 
 Fourth-year WR Pop Douglas had two TD catches in the scrimmage and also hauled in a deep pass from backup QB Tommy DeVito . He looked like the offense's most productive player. 
 DeVito was celebrating his 28th birthday, and as he was signing autographs after a practice in which he looked in command, fans sang to him at the urging of his agent, Sean Stellato. 
 QB Drake Maye had touchdown throws to WR Romeo Doubs (returning after missing two days) and RB TreVeyon Henderson . Maye led a successful two-minute drill to set up a field goal to end practice, which was notable after struggles the day prior in the same situation (2 INTs). 
 One play that got a rise out of the crowd came when rookie QB Behren Morton fired a pass along the left sideline to WR Tejhaun Palmer , and the ball somehow ended up in the hands of RB Myles Montgomery , who had been sprinting up that sideline. The play went for a gain of 40-plus yards. 
 Coach Mike Vrabel served as referee for the scrimmage. He assigned assistants Terrell Williams and Tony Dews as head coaches, Todd Downing and Ashton Grant as offensive coordinators, and Scott Booker and Justin Hamilton as defensive coordinators. 
 Coaches held a draft to split the team up, with Vrabel saying he had just two stipulations -- Maye had to be paired with C Jared Wilson , and WRs Mack Hollins and  Efton Chism III  couldn't be split up (a playful acknowledgement to how close they've become). 
 Starting LT Will Campbell , who wore a brace on his left arm/elbow Thursday, did not participate in the scrimmage, but Vrabel said he expects him back after the weekend. First-round pick Caleb Lomu got some work at LT after spending the majority of camp at RT. 
 Vrabel said it would likely be another week before starting CB Carlton Davis III returns. Davis appeared to injure his hamstring July 28. 
 

 

 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 Cornerback Christian Gonzalez and receiver A.J. Brown needed to be separated at one point of Thursday's practice, as the competitive one-on-one matchup between them that has been a highlight of Patriots training camp nearly boiled over.

 The fireworks seemed to be sparked by Gonzalez's trash talk following a red zone drill in which his tight coverage held Brown without a catch. As the Patriots transitioned to a different period of practice, Gonzalez appeared to be chirping in Brown's direction. At first, Brown was walking away, but something appeared to spark him to turn back in Gonzalez's direction.

 Receiver Kayshon Boutte also came over to that area of the sideline and said he was trying to pull Brown away from Gonzalez. Boutte said he heard someone say, "You're a grown man!"

 The battle between Gonzalez and Brown seemed to build throughout the full-pads practice, with Gonzalez gesturing in Brown's direction after covering him tightly in 11-on-11 drills as a long pass from quarterback Drake Maye in that direction was incomplete.

 In the final drill, Brown caught a comeback route on Gonzalez.

 "It's good on good. He's a No. 1 receiver in this league going up against a No. 1 corner. That's how it's going to go," Gonzalez said after practice. "It's football at the end of the day. There's never no disrespect or anything. We're just battling to make each other better.

title: 2026 New Orleans Saints training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Saints training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  New Orleans Saints ' camp is taking place in Metairie, Louisiana, and Saints reporter Katherine Terrell has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Saints camp. We will update this file often. Kellen Moore enters his second season as head coach, and expectations are higher after  Tyler Shough  impressed while starting the final nine games of the 2025 campaign. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Saints news 
 
 Drew Brees' greatness, as seen through eyes of teammates, coaches 
 Saints place WR Ja'Lynn Polk, 24, on reserve/retired list 
 Saints starting DT Bryan Bresee to have season-ending ACL surgery 
 The legacy of Taysom Hill in New Orleans: 'There's only one' 
 WR Chris Olave signing four-year extension 
 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 It was Drew Brees day at practice as the former Saints quarterback goes into the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

 The Saints painted a No. 9 on the practice field, and the staff, including coach Kellen Moore, wore No. 9 shirts. Running back  Alvin Kamara , defensive end  Cameron Jordan and long-snapper Zach Wood , along with coaches Josh Hill and Joel Thomas, were absent to watch the enshrinement in Canton, Ohio, but are expected back tomorrow.

 But the excitement of Brees being enshrined wore off early as the Saints dealt with some injuries. Offensive guard  Dillon Radunz  (knee) limped off the field after going up against Vernon Broughton in a one-on-one rep and did not return, while starting safety Julian Blackmon also left with a knee injury.

 Wide receiver Chris Olave walked to the sideline late in practice and had his wrist inspected and taped by athletic trainers before returning to take part in a "run down the clock" sequence at the end of practice, where he made a contested catch across the middle.

 Jordyn Tyson also had back-to-back catches from Tyler Shough in team drills, including one that Shough floated over the head of a defender attempting to break up a pass.

 Other observations:  

 
 Defensive tackle  John Ridgeway III  took over long-snapping duties with Wood out. 
 William Sherman played first-team right guard with Radunz out. The usual starting right guard, Cesar Ruiz , played second-team center. Moore said that was part of the plan to get Ruiz snaps there and that he will play in that position tomorrow as well. 
 Kicker Tanner Brown was 4-of-6 with misses from 39 and 54 yards. 
 Travis Etienne Jr . got all the first-team reps at running back.  
 Jordan Howden played first-team safety with Blackmon out. 
 Isaiah Stalbird intercepted Spencer Rattler in 11-on-11 drills. 
 Kendre Miller (back), Devin Neal (hamstring), Rejzohn Wright , Christen Miller (toe),  Chris Rumph II  (ankle) missed practice. 
 This was a scheduled shorter practice intended to end at 10:30 in front of the fans, but the Saints had to finish the final minutes inside because of lightning in the area.  
 New linebacker Deion Jones was at practice and wearing No. 45. 
 The Saints waived injured player Zxavian Harris . 
 

 

 
 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 Rookie wide receiver Barion Brown continues to be the rising star of camp after he concluded Thursday's practice with a 46-yard touchdown from Spencer Rattler to finish out the two-minute drill.

 "Spencer got out of it -- we'll watch the film to see if there's a sack. There's always a debate of sack/no sack, it's never ending. So we let it play out and Barion did a great job adjusting to that ball, tracking it, those are deep balls and the ball usually tails one way or another because the QB is running, so awesome job making a play," coach Kellen Moore said.

 While Brown has mostly been with the second team to start camp, he's starting to get more opportunities, including some snaps with the first team in the two-minute drill, where he caught a pass from Tyler Shough for about a 15-yard gain.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Chris Rumph (ankle), Devin Neal (hamstring) did not finish practice. Christen Miller (toe), Jeremiah Wright (shoulder) and Kendre Miller (back) are day-to-day and did not participate Thursday. 
 Alvin Kamara was not at practice, which Moore said was due to a rest day. 
 It was a rough day for kicker Charlie Smyth , who went 3-for-6 and missed three straight field goals in the indoor facility. Smyth missed from 39, 45 and 51 yards, so the team backed things up to 39 yards again. When he made that, they attempted another 51-yarder, which was good. He is now 17-of-22 for camp. 
 The first-team two-minute drill was won by the defense after a sack (pressure from Cameron Jordan ) and an interception of Shough by Quincy Riley (pressure from Carl Granderson ) as time expired. The offense was moving the ball well prior to that, with Shough completing two passes to Juwan Johnson and then passes to Travis Etienne Jr ., Chris Olave and Brown before spiking the ball to stop the clock. 
 Shough was also picked off by Kool-Aid McKinstry in the previous set of team drills in the end zone. Moore said it looked like the pass came up short in a throwaway situation. Etienne had the ball four plays in a row prior to the interception. 
 
 
 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 Wide receiver Barion Brown , a sixth-round pick in April's draft, has seemed to find his stride since the pads came on. Brown has taken advantage of the one-on-one drills vs. defensive backs and made several nice catches during that period Wednesday. He also had a 36-yard catch-and-run from Spencer Rattler over safety Jordan Howden in the two-minute drill to end practice. That play helped the Saints get into field goal range.

 Brown was the third receiver the Saints drafted this year and he came in with the potential to make the team as a kick returner. Saints coach Kellen Moore said they saw more than that when they drafted Brown, who played at Kentucky and LSU.

 "We watched a lot of evidence of him playing receiver and playing impactful plays in the SEC for a number of years, not just the LSU year, but the Kentucky years. And when you watch all that exposure and get to know Barion, you're really fired up to have this guy," Moore said.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Cesar Ruiz was back at practice following the birth of his son, which he described as the best experience of his life. 
 Running back Kendre Miller is dealing with a back issue that has kept him limited in the past two practices. Christen Miller has a toe issue and Jeremiah Wright left early with a shoulder ailment. 
 The Saints worked the two-minute drill to end practice. The scenario was that the offense was down 3 with less than two minutes and one timeout. Both the first- and second-team offenses kicked a field goal to tie. 
 Tanner Brown  made 5 of 6 field goals, with a miss from 39 yards. He also kicked the two-minute field goals. Charlie Smyth is now 15-for-16 in camp and Brown is 17-for-19. 
 Linebacker Kaden Elliss , who is sometimes used as a pass rusher, worked in one-on-one drills against the OL. That drill is usually OL vs. DL but Moore said Elliss wanted to do the drill to get more reps. 
 

 
 Monday, Aug. 3 
 The Saints' offense bounced back in the team's first day in pads. It was a run-focused day featuring some usage of 12 and 13 personnel (sets with two and three tight ends).

 Saints quarterback Tyler Shough and the offensive unit had a solid end to practice when he completed a pass to Alvin Kamara , hit Travis Etienne Jr . near the sideline and connected again with Etienne, who…

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The New York Giants camp is taking place at The Greenbrier in White Sulphur Springs, West Virginia, and Giants reporter Jordan Raanan has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Giants camp. We will update this file often. How will the Giants handle increased expectations and a new coach? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Giants camp 
 
 Cam Skattebo admits doing 'dumb things,' will save backflips for TDs 
 Nabers 'looked good' in 1st practice since knee injury 
 Giants have spoken with Skattebo after Fanatics Fest flip 
 2026 New York Giants training camp preview 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 The Giants finished their 12 days in West Virginia with another physical practice filled with goal-line and run-game work. It was a typical John Harbaugh workout. No easy days.

 Harbaugh thinks it's going to make a difference for a team that won seven games combined the past two seasons.

 "Well, I think we got a lot better. That's probably what we got out of it. We improved tremendously," Harbaugh said. "We're much further along than we were when we started. I think we can look back and say that we've come a long way."

 The trip helped with team building and camaraderie.

 "I would give it an A, A-plus for that. It's been really everything," Harbaugh said. "We've been able to focus on the task at hand. There's really no distractions out here. It's a beautiful setting. It's a beautiful resort. Everything has been excellent. And the guys have been able to lock in on the football. The fields have held up extremely well. I mean, every little thing has been good. It's not lavish by any stretch in terms of the facility, but it's everything we could want. Maybe that's even better."

 

 Other observations: 

 
 RB Cam Skattebo returned to practice after stretching out his leg the previous day. He participated in all 10 practices in West Virginia as he returns from a fractured ankle last year. 
 Defensive lineman Darius Alexander had a strong practice with multiple sacks in live drills. It concluded a nice camp for the second-year player whom the Giants are counting on to make a leap. 
 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Wide receiver Malik Nabers looked the best he has this summer during individual drills Friday. He continues to get better -- making sharper cuts, jumping and landing on the affected leg and running crisper routes as he rebounds from a knee injury .

 

 Coach John Harbaugh said he noticed this was the best version of Nabers, who is getting to the final stages of recovery. The next step is for Nabers to "work his way back into practice more and more."

 The expectation seems to be that Nabers will return to live team drills in the next couple of weeks. That would have him trending to be ready for Week 1 against the Cowboys.

 "[Return to play coordinator Allison Boudreau] is working with him, and she's been working on situations where you're off-balance, landing off-balance and unpredictable type situations that you're going to get rather than just doing normal rehab and then getting out there and all of a sudden being surprised by the awkwardness of football," Harbaugh said. "Try to create that as much as you can in a controlled setting."

 More observations: 

 
 The offense had perhaps its best day of camp. On its final drive, the unit went the length of the field with tight end Theo Johnson and running back Dante Miller each making multiple receptions. The series concluded with a 2-yard touchdown from quarterback  Jaxson Dart to wide receiver  Darius Slayton . Dart finished 16-of-19 passing on the day. 
 Malachi Fields on the offense: "It just keeps building over time. We've had almost two weeks now, just getting together, so I think we'll just keep jelling, keep clicking, and we'll just keep building that confidence as we go into the preseason." 
 Cam Skattebo left practice early after stretching out his left leg. Harbaugh described the issue as "working through the football shape part" and didn't think it was serious. C  John Michael Schmitz Jr . left after getting his "bell rung" and is being evaluated, while OLB Brian Burns continues to nurse a minor ankle injury. 
 
 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 The Giants shed the pads after three straight days of full contact. Coach John Harbaugh ran a 2½-hour walk-through to give his players' bodies some rest.

 They'll be back at it Friday and Saturday with full padded practices before leaving West Virginia.

 Harbaugh has run a hard training camp to date. The Giants ran over 100 live plays in the heat Wednesday. It has been in stark contrast to the training camps they had under Brian Daboll.

 But the Giants knew this was going to be the case. Harbaugh is known to run a tough camp. Even his practices in the spring don't waste time and have a lot of live periods.

 "Man, it's tough, gritty," cornerback Greg Newsome II said. "We're going to work, and I like that. There's no off days for us in terms of not competing. He's going to make sure we compete. We're always doing situational football and things like that. So, it's been super fun to play. He's a great coach. We're always talking all the time and I'm super excited to play for him."

 More observations:  

 
 CB Dru Phillips has a mild knee sprain and will miss some time. CB Jarrick Bernard-Converse also didn't practice again and is dealing with an "ongoing" knee problem. Harbaugh said the Giants might sign another cornerback. 
 Jaxson Dart doesn't seem too worried about the offense despite the early inconsistency. "We're taking steps each day," he said. "Obviously there are thing that you go out there and maybe it's our first time running something and you have things to talk through. A lot of times we'll have the opportunity the next day to go out there and try to fix it and run it again. So I think the really good thing I'm seeing about our offense is the communication after practices to be able to fix the adjustments the next day. That's really encouraging to see." 
 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 It was another up and down day for the Giants' offense. It really has been the story of training camp in West Virginia.

 Quarterback Jaxson Dart and Co. were pedestrian again on Wednesday, even against the second-team defense. He threw a pair of interceptions early, before tossing three touchdown passes and rushing for two more in red-zone drills.

 Coach John Harbaugh thought it was a good response after Dart let the frustration get the best of him one day earlier.

 "The football response absolutely was there. Yeah, he stepped up," Harbaugh said. "A lot of third down stuff we did. Fourth down stuff, fourth down in the red zone to win the game, things like that.

 "Yeah, he had a heck of a practice. It was impressive."

 Dart and the first-team offense have yet to fully hit their stride this summer. And there are some built-in excuses. Dart is learning a new offense. He's also without his No. 1 receiver in Malik Nabers , who still isn't taking part in team drills as he recovers from a knee injury. Still, it would be nice to see them put together a complete practice before leaving West Virginia.

 More observations: 

 
 Second day in a row Odell Beckham Jr . had a strong practice. This time he had four catches in live drills. He continues to get open and make it a tough decision for the Giants whether to find a roster spot for the veteran receiver. 
 Outside linebacker Brian Burns , wide…

title: 2026 New York Jets training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Jets training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  New York Jets  camp is taking place at the Atlantic Health Training Facility in Florham Park, New Jersey, and Jets reporter Rich Cimini has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Jets camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football, and which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Thursday.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Jets camp 
 
 Rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq to miss time after hernia setback 
 Jets' Smith rues being 'distraction' after dispute with girlfriend 
 2026 Jets training camp preview 
 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 The Jets ended the first phase of training camp with a controlled instrasquad scrimmage.

 There was a scary moment near the end, when prized rookie edge rusher David Bailey walked off gingerly, favoring his left ankle.

 Afterward, coach Aaron Glenn confirmed it was an ankle injury, adding that Bailey likely will be listed as day-to-day. He was able to jog back to the sideline after being examined in the medical tent.

 Bailey, drafted No. 2 overall, continued his strong camp, recording one sack and at least two pressures, unofficially. He probably should've had another sack, but the officials let the play continue.

 This was one of those good news-bad news days. Glenn's new-look defense looked terrific, while the offense struggled, especially in the red zone.

 There were plenty of self-inflicted mistakes. QB Geno Smith started hot, leading a 65-yard touchdown drive and completing his first five passes, but the starting offense unraveled after that. There were five penalties and two sacks.

 Penalties were a bugaboo last season. Glenn noted that most of the penalties came toward the end of the scrimmage, adding, "It's the part that we get tired. And once you get fatigued, mentally things start to get jumbled. So we have to do a better job of that."

 Smith finished 12-of-20 for 157 yards, leading only one touchdown drive in nine series, six of which began in plus territory.

 

 Other observations:

 
 The offensive highlight was rookie Cade Klubnik 's 66-yard pass to WR Isaiah Williams in a hurry-up period. Moments later, the former Clemson star threw an 11-yard TD pass to TE Jelani Woods . Klubnik finished 10-of-14 for 154 yards, two TDs and one interception. He's battling journeyman Bailey Zappe for the No. 2 job. Because of his experience, Zappe shows more command than Klubnik, but the battle is far from over. The preseason games will tell a lot. 
 Glenn wouldn't reveal his QB plans for the preseason, but it certainly sounds like Smith will see action. "My mentality is that everybody's playing," Glenn said. You can expect to see a lot of Klubnik and Zappe. 
 Williams has been one of the most productive players in camp; he's a lock for the WR4 job. Whenever his name is mentioned, Glenn lights up. He caught five balls in the scrimmage, including a 36-yard TD from Smith. 
 Some of the defensive standouts: S Dane Belton (interception), NB Jordan Clark (two pass breakups), DT Darrell Jackson Jr (sack), S Minkah Fitzpatrick (QB pressure). 
 injury update: Rookie S V.J. Payne, a seventh-round pick, will be sidelined three to four weeks with a bone bruise. 
 The Jets have no practice Sunday and Monday, then host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers for two days of joint practices before opening the preseason Friday against the Bucs. 
 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 

 Geno Smith has a big fan in offensive coordinator Frank Reich, who gushed about his starting quarterback after a sweltering practice.

 "He's a leader of the offense and, make no mistake about it, in every way, shape and form," Reich said. "To me, what has come crystal clear ... the attribute that sticks out to me is his laser focus. This man is laser focused like people don't understand. He comes to work. He comes to work, and he is locked in. And I feel like the whole offense plays off of that. That's a big deal."

 Smith is having a solid camp. He delivered another strong practice (8-for-12 in team drills), hooking up five times with WR Garrett Wilson . August optimism is nice; the bottom line is how the player performs in September and beyond.

 Reich praised Smith's upper-body throwing mechanics, calling them "pure."

 "There's only a couple guys in the league that I would say are pure. Geno's one of them," said Reich, adding that Smith, 35, from a physical standpoint, looks like a 28-year-old.

 Smith has always thrown a pretty ball. The key is eliminating negative plays. He has more interceptions (52) and more sacks (182) than any QB over the past four seasons.

 Other observations: 

 
 The front office has to feel good about the Breece Hall contract extension (three years, $43.5 million) in May. At the time, his average per year ($14.5 million) ranked fourth among running backs. The market has exploded in recent days with extensions for Bijan Robinson , Jonathan Taylor and Jahmyr Gibbs . Hall now ranks eighth in APY. "Man, am I glad we got that done," said Reich, calling Hall a "phenomenal" player. It pays to be proactive. 
 In keeping with the load-management theme to camp, LB Demario Davis , S Minkah Fitzpatrick and DT Harrison Phillips received veteran rest days on Friday. Davis still managed to get involved. During a brief break in the action, he ran out on the field, into the huddle, and gave some quick words to the defense. 
 Coaches never want to see players get hurt, but T'Vondre Sweat 's hamstring injury has opened the door for rookie DT Darrell Jackson Jr . to get reps with the starters. 
 Backup LB Kiko Mauigoa is looking forward to facing his brother, Francis Mauigoa , in the preseason. Mauigoa, a 2026 first-round pick, is slated to start at right guard for the Giants, so the two brothers could cross paths on the field. The family will have to make a decision during the regular season: Whose game will it attend? "I told them, 'We have one home stadium, so they can come every Sunday,'" Kiko said with a laugh. 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 Quarterbacks always wear a red jersey in practice. Geno Smith is taking the red thing to a new level.

 Red contact lenses.

 To reduce the glare on the field, Smith is wearing the red lenses for the first time in his career. They were quite apparent during his weekly news conference, with one reporter joking that the red-eye look was scary.

 "It's actually pretty cool," Smith said. "It blocks out the sunlight and all that, so it's actually pretty cool. It keeps the glare from the sun out of your eyes."

 Smith's former Jets teammate Santonio Holmes, a wide receiver, was known for wearing red contact lenses more than a decade ago. Smith got the idea from Holmes but didn't go red until he consulted recently with eye specialists, who signed off on the idea.

 "It's just something we're trying out, just to see what it's like," Smith said. "I like it, so we've been sticking with it."

 Even though his eyes look red, he's not seeing that way.

 "The entire room is yellow, so it's a yellow tint to everything," Smith said. "But yeah, it's pretty cool. You guys should try it."

 Smith, who threw a league-high 17 interceptions last season for the Las Vegas Raiders , is trying to reboot his career with the team that drafted him in 2013. So far, so good. Teammates and coaches have been impressed with his command of the offense and willingness to take chances downfield.

 His goal is to make opposing defenses see red.

 Other observations:

title: 2026 Philadelphia Eagles training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Eagles training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Philadelphia Eagles camp is taking place in the Jefferson Health Training Complex, and Eagles reporter Tim McManus has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and -- of course -- the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Eagles camp. We will update this file often. How will quarterback  Jalen Hurts fare in the reimagined offense? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Thursday.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Eagles news 
 
 Epenesa grateful to be Eagle after 'weird' Browns situation 
 Eagles' Nolan Smith apologizes for 'unacceptable' speeding arrest 
 Eagles, DT Carter agree to four-year, $152M extension 
 Eagles coach Nick Sirianni adjusting to offseason changes 
 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 Eagles running back Saquon Barkley made his presence felt. He got animated after a short touchdown run, chirping at Cooper DeJean before giving Quinyon Mitchell a playful shove.

 The offense switched from goal line to backed up work a short time later. Barkley used a nifty jump cut to speed to daylight on one play and followed that up by shaking defensive tackle Jordan Davis on his next carry.

 Barkley believes this new system can open up some things for him that he hasn't been able to fully showcase to this point in his career.

 "That's the plan," said offensive coordinator Sean Mannion . "Saquon, he's a tremendous player, and I think everything we do offensively ultimately is about how do we put all of our players in the best position to succeed and obviously Saquon is a focal point of our offense, that goes without saying."

 Other observations:  

 
 Linebacker Zack Baun intercepted Jalen Hurts on a throw over the middle. Hurts completed a pass to Elijah Moore on the previous play, and when he tried to go back to the well on a similar concept, Baun was there to jump the route. Baun nearly came up with another pick earlier in practice, but the ball somehow made it past him and into the hands of Moore along the sideline. 
 Hurts' connection with tight end Dallas Goedert is heating up. Hurts escaped pressure by rolling to his right and threw one to the corner of the end zone for Goedert, who pulled it in with Jihaad Campbell in coverage. 
 Center Cam Jurgens left practice early with a trainer for the second straight day. Saturday's exit was at the end of the session, and Jurgens appeared to be moving fine. 
 Receivers Makai Lemon and DeVonta Smith were sidelined for the fourth straight day with hamstring injuries. 
 

 

 
 
 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Right tackle Lane Johnson returned following a four-practice absence for personal reasons. Johnson was originally scheduled to speak after Friday's practice but will likely now talk Saturday, the team said. He was a limited participant as he reacclimates to the grind.

 
"He has a calming presence," defensive tackle Jordan Davis  said of Johnson. "One day, I'm not going to be able to say that I have him in the locker room. It's just very good to have him out here. Everybody knows he's a baller, man. He's a f---ing baller. Lane, man, he's a cornerstone."

 
Rookie Markel Bell continued to get first-team reps at right tackle during team drills. Center Cam Jurgens spent time in the medical tent before heading indoors. Jake Majors took over at center in his absence.

 Other observations:  

 
 The defensive line made life tough for the short-handed offensive front. Jalen Carter ripped past Majors with a swim move to shut down a would-be passing play for Jalen Hurts . He later rose up to deflect a throw. Davis blew up a play in the backfield earlier in the session. 
 Second-year receiver Darius Cooper is making a push for a roster spot. He has enjoyed a strong camp, and that continued Friday with a number of catches, including one from Hurts over the middle with Quinyon Mitchell in coverage. 
 Tanner McKee had perhaps his best day of the summer. He hit Cooper on consecutive attempts before tossing one into the right corner of the end zone for the 6-foot-6 Johnny Wilson , who rose to snag the pass with corner Jonathan Jones nearby. McKee and Andy Dalton continue to split second-team reps. 
 Receivers DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon missed their third straight practice with hamstring injuries. 
 New Sixer Jaylen Brown visited training camp. He chopped it up with coach Nick Sirianni, Hurts and Smith, among others, and got a nice ovation from the fans as he walked by. 
 Hurts turned 28 on Friday. The whole team sang "Happy Birthday" to him when they huddled after practice. 
 
 
 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 The Jalen Hurts - Dontayvion Wicks connection continues to shine. The highlight Wednesday came during 7-on-7s with Hurts tossing a precision pass deep down the left sideline for Wicks, who corralled it with defensive backs Jonathan Jones and Andre Sam bearing down on him. Hurts said Wicks was "trying to beat down the door" this offseason to get extra reps in with him and complimented his attack mindset.

 "When you talk about adversity, you learn a lot about the guys around you this time of camp. It's humid, it's sticky, it's hot. You see who's got that anger to them, who's got a little bit of rage in them -- for the best," Hurts said. "He's got it. That's exciting to see."

 

 Other observations:  

 
 Eagles receivers DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon both missed practice due to hamstring injuries for a second straight day. Right tackle Lane Johnson was absent for the fourth straight practice for personal reasons. 
 The linebacker corps looks to have some good depth to it behind presumed starters Zack Baun and Jihaad Campbell . Jeremiah Trotter Jr . has enjoyed a strong camp. He put himself in perfect position to extinguish a Saquon Barkley toss run. DC Vic Fangio also told reporters not to "sleep" on veteran Chance Campbell when putting together their "lists," seemingly referring to the 53-man roster projections. He has looked solid as well. 
 New offensive coordinator Sean Mannion has dialed up a healthy amount of designed runs for Hurts, generally to good results, including one Wednesday with Dallas Goedert as an escort that produced a chunk gain down the left side. Hurts said it's too early to know how those kind of plays will mesh with the new offensive scheme but the bet here is Hurts uses his legs a little more than last season based off what we've seen at camp. 
 

 
 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Eagles receivers DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon both missed practice with hamstring injuries. The team is not expressing any long-term concern with either player. Still, these are meaningful reps -- especially for a rookie. Lemon missed minicamp as well with a hamstring injury. He has served primarily as the starting slot receiver when healthy but hasn't produced many splash moments to date. It's important Jalen Hurts gets as many snaps as possible with his skill players as the offense breaks in a new system in the post A.J. Brown era.

 Other observations:  

 
 Standout right tackle Lane Johnson was absent (excused/not injury related) for the third straight practice. The team declined to provide further details given that it is a personal matter. Rookie Markel Bell received first-team reps in his absence and appeared to hold his own. 
 With a number of starters missing, it wasn't a big surprise the offense sputtered. Penalties made for a clunky, rhythmless practice with few highlights.
