title: 2026 Pittsburgh Steelers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Steelers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Pittsburgh Steelers ' camp is taking place in Latrobe, Pennsylvania, and Steelers reporter Brooke Pryor has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Steelers camp. We will update this file often. How will coach Mike McCarthy shape this roster and the offense in his first year in Pittsburgh? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Steelers camp 
 
 'Tempered': Inside Mike McCarthy's new vision for Steelers 
 Steelers' Broderick Jones cleared after eight months (neck) 
 Rodgers: 'Zero debate' 2026 will be last season 
 Jalen Ramsey, Joey Porter Jr. placed on PUP list 
 Steelers revamp wide receiver unit 
 Rodgers reunites with family ahead of final NFL season 
 
 
 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 Cornerback Jamel Dean got things started with a bang in the first play of the "Franco Moment" (Mike McCarthy's pop quiz team period formerly known as the "Mojo Moment" in Dallas) on Saturday night under the lights at Latrobe Memorial Stadium.

 Dean jumped in front of Roman Wilson and intercepted Aaron Rodgers ' first pass attempt then ran it back for a 35-yard pick-six.

 "I love being off the field," veteran defensive lineman  Cameron Heyward  said. "And when we get turnovers like that, that accomplishes that. The best defenses are on the sideline."

 In fact, the defense stayed on the sideline for much of the "Franco Moment" snaps. The group went on to win the period 3-0, as the next offense under Mason Rudolph stalled out and backup kicker Laith Marjan 's 45-yard field goal attempt went wide left.

 Like the first team, the third-team offense, led by Will Howard , was off the field after one play when Howard and running back Lew Nichols had a miscommunication on the handoff and the ball hit the turf. Rookie defensive lineman Kevin Jobity Jr. , a recent addition, quickly snatched the ball to recover the fumble.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Official attendance for the sellout crowd at the Steelers' Saturday Night Lights practice checked in at 8,499. 
 While plenty of fans clamored for Rodgers' autograph along the fence line before practice, rookie offensive lineman and new Steelers cult hero Gennings Dunker got some love too. One fan made a sign that read "Gennings Dunker 4 President!!" and wore a red mullet wig to match Dunker's signature 'do. Dunker signed the poster and posed for a selfie with the fan. "I've not met a person I didn't like or a bad person, so I mean, everyone's been awesome," Dunker said of his reception in Pittsburgh. "And it's almost like a big small town, is kind of how I would explain it. That's kind of the vibe I've been getting, and it's been awesome." 
 Quarterback Drew Allar had a solid night slinging the deep ball, connecting with Robert Tonyan and Brandon Smith on back-to-back plays in 7-on-7. "It felt really good," Allar said. "And it's been something I'm working on in terms of the trajectory of the throw. I kind of picked Aaron's brain on it maybe a week ago or so. To be able to finally get the chance to do it in, like, a live setting -- even though it's 7-on-7 but against live DBs and tight coverage -- felt really good." 
 Neither DK Metcalf nor Michael Pittman Jr.  participated in the final team periods. A trainer appeared to look at Pittman's leg, but both Pittman and Metcalf kept their helmets throughout the end of practice, which would seemingly signal they weren't being held out because of injury. 
 Offensive lineman Broderick Jones , still working to regain his strength after spinal fusion surgery on a season-ending neck injury, won both of his pass rush reps during one-on-ones, first putting Nick Herbig , rushing from the right, on the ground then holding off Jack Sawyer from the left. "Broderick was a first-round pick for a reason," Herbig said. "Guy's got all the talent in the world. He has all the intangibles. He's got the physicality for it. And it's just a matter of feeling confident again, coming back from injury like that. But I know that he can do it. I've seen it firsthand." 
 

 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Thunderstorms in the area Friday morning forced the Steelers to adjust their practice schedule. Not only did the team close practice to fans because of lightning in the area, but coach Mike McCarthy also pushed the start time to 11:30 a.m. to give the group as much time as possible to decide between holding practice outdoors or moving to the new indoor facility at St. Vincent College.

 The team managed to squeeze in an abbreviated practice outside between storm cells, practicing for an hour and 45 minutes instead of the scheduled 2 hours and 30 minutes. McCarthy cut out some of the individual work, but he still got in all of the preplanned scheme installations.

 "These two practices yesterday and today, they're the most difficult," McCarthy said Friday morning. "You got four installs already in. You can play games with the first four installs, but now you're adding a second, third down package. We put in short yardage yesterday. Today will be the second red zone package that'll go in. We'll also install goal line. We'll do that thud tempo. We'll do some two-minutes today.

 "This is a really good practice. It gives you everything."

 

 More observations: 

 
 The Steelers seemed to get good news on rookie tackle Max Iheanachor after the first-round pick left practice early Thursday. Though Iheanachor missed Friday's practice, McCarthy said he expected Iheanachor back on Monday. 
 McCarthy said he wasn't pleased with Thursday's practice, specifically saying there were too many mental lapses, including the seven pre-snap penalties he counted. Not among them, though, were the chippy moments and heated altercations between players. "I'd be more concerned if we didn't have that," McCarthy said. "So it's part of football. It's part of the game." 
 
 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
Rookie first-round pick Max Iheanachor left practice after about an hour and didn't return after appearing to suffer an upper-body injury Thursday. The team's medical staff extensively evaluated the offensive tackle's shoulder and neck area on the sideline, and he eventually walked up the hill to the locker room with an athletic trainer.
 Coach Mike McCarthy talks to the media before practice only, so he's expected to give an update on Iheanachor before Friday morning's practice.

 Iheanachor was making significant progress through the early portions of camp before the injury. In the initial preseason depth chart, he was listed as the second-team right tackle. And though McCarthy was quick to tell reporters not to put much stock in the required depth chart, Iheanachor has consistently been working with the second-team offensive line.

 "Max has had a great start," center Zach Frazier said. "Obviously for any rookie coming in, it's a lot. It's just an NFL offense, but every day he's taking steps. He doesn't really make the same mistakes twice. So he's coachable, and I'm really happy with how he's done so far."

 With Iheanachor out, Broderick Jones took the bulk of second-team reps at right tackle. He was inconsistent in the role as he continues to work his way back from season-ending neck surgery. Though he has been cleared to return to all football activities, Jones, who was the team's starting left tackle last season before his injury, is still regaining his strength and getting back his technique.

 

 More observations: 

 
 DT Cameron Heyward appeared to have a veteran day…

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Seattle Seahawks ' camp is taking place in Renton, Washington, and Seahawks reporter Brady Henderson has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Seahawks camp. We will update this file often. What is new with the defending Super Bowl champions? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp previews for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Seahawks camp 
 
 WR Tory Horton healthy after cracking tibia last season 
 Seattle Pro Bowl DL Williams confirms deal talks 
 Seattle's Nick Emmanwori has ankle surgery, expected to play W1 
 Who are the Khoslas? Meet the family set to buy the Seahawks 
 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 The Seahawks have been without rookie running back Jadarian Price the past two days as their first-round draft pick deals with a minor leg injury. His absence has given free agent addition  Emanuel Wilson a chance to join George Holani with the No. 1 offense and show what he can bring to Seattle's potentially crowded backfield.

 Which appears to be more than just a rugged, between-the-tackles runner.

 "I'm bringing something different," Wilson said. "A lot of people think I don't got speed, but I've got a lot of speed on my end, and really just bringing a lot of power."

 Case in point was one play Saturday from the Seahawks' annual practice at Lumen Field, an off-tackle run in which Wilson stuck his foot in the ground, turned upfield and showed some burst for a gain of roughly 15 yards.

 No one will confuse him for  Kenneth Walker III  -- the explosive runner and Super Bowl LX MVP who signed with the Kansas City Chiefs in free agency -- but Wilson moves well for a back of his size.

 A "heavy runner" and a "230-pound guy with great feet" was how general manager John Schneider described Wilson after Seattle signed him in March to a one-year, $1.595 million contract. Undrafted in 2023 out of Division II Fort Valley State in Georgia, Wilson spent his first three seasons as a backup with the Green Bay Packers .

 Exactly where he'll fit in Seattle's post-Walker backfield remains to be seen. Price and Holani have shared first-team reps this offseason, while Wilson has usually been with the No. 2 offense. But that's all subject to change once Zach Charbonnet returns, which might not happen until late in the season even though he had ACL surgery in February.

 Wilson is giving himself the best chance to factor into the mix, one way or another.

 "I'm going to sound really cliché right now, but he just keeps stacking days, from where he started to where he is now," coach Mike Macdonald said. "It seems like he keeps making plays, he keeps being productive in his style of ball, which is really cool. What he brings to the table is exciting. There's a physicality, a heaviness to his game, which is fun to have on offense."

 As for Price, Macdonald said he's dealing with lower-body soreness and should return soon.

 "It's a minor issue right now," he said. "We'll see. It's a matter of days."

 

 More observations: 

 
 At the team's annual Lumen Field practice last year, AJ Finley 's bid for a roster spot came to an end when he tore an ACL. So it was meaningful for the fourth-year safety to be playing at the team's home stadium for the first time since then -- even more so when he intercepted Sam Darnold during an 11-on-11 period. "It didn't hit me until I got to the sideline, and all the boys were congratulating me," Finley said. "It's a full-circle moment. Sticking to the process and taking it day-to-day, it's been a hell of a ride. I have a lot of good people in my circle: my wife, my family. Being here [rehabbing] with the team last year, it helped me a lot. It's been a great experience." 
 Rodney Thomas II , another backup safety who is fighting for a roster spot, intercepted Drew Lock in 11-on-11. 
 Second-year tight end Elijah Arroyo continued his strong camp by hauling in a touchdown catch over starting safety Julian Love in the end zone. "If he can continue this trend of having a routine, attacking the details, making those marginal gains every day, then I think this is the type of stuff that he is capable of -- and he can take it even further," Macdonald said. "So the challenge is, keep going." 
 The Seahawks have an off day Sunday. 
 

 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Wide receiver  Cooper Kupp continued his strong training camp with another touchdown Friday, catching a dart in the end zone during an 11-on-11 period.

 The 33-year-old has not looked his age this summer, moving well and appearing routinely in sync with quarterback Sam Darnold as both enter their second season with the Seahawks.

 Which is to say that Kupp still has productive football left. Whenever he does call it a career, though, coach Mike Macdonald has said he has a job on Seattle's staff if he wants it.

 Kupp is already something of a coach, as the first episode of "Hard Knocks" documented. It showed the 10-year veteran sitting in on quarterback meetings as the conduit of information for the receivers. The episode also featured a film session in which Kupp appeared to decipher an Xs and Os conundrum for Macdonald.

 

 "Being in the same room as Cooper Kupp, it helps us all elevate to his level," receiver Rashid Shaheed said Friday. "Not necessarily to his level, because he's so far beyond what you can expect as a receiver because he's like another coach, as 'Hard Knocks' kind of explained.

 "But Cooper's amazing. Just his knowledge of the game, how he breaks things down in meetings, he's so willing to help and that's what we appreciate about him. You obviously see what he does on the field. He's a triple crown winner, Super Bowl champion for a reason. It's just great to have him around."

 More observations: 

 
 The Seahawks will hold their annual practice at Lumen Field on Saturday evening. Macdonald has said the 5:15 p.m. PT start time is meant to give players -- especially the younger ones -- a sense of what it will feel like to play in primetime. Seattle has six games this season starting around that time. 
 Rookie RB  Jadarian Price  did not practice Friday for undisclosed reasons.  
 
 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 Dante Fowler Jr . is a newcomer to Seattle's defense, but he was hardly a stranger when he arrived in May on a one-year deal.

 The 12th-year veteran has known defensive tackle Leonard Williams since 2012, when the two Florida natives took part in the Under Armour All-America Game. Fowler played for Aden Durde in Atlanta and Dallas, when Seattle's defensive coordinator was a position coach for the Falcons and Cowboys. In Dallas, Fowler was a teammate of fellow outside linebacker DeMarcus Lawrence , who took him under his wing.

 Lawrence helped sell Fowler on the Super Bowl champions this past offseason. A year earlier, Fowler had discussions with Durde about potentially signing with Seattle before opting for a second stint in Dallas instead.

 "I just respect the man he is," Fowler said Thursday of Durde. "He got it out the mud. He got it out the hard way. He's from London. He's not from here, and his IQ of football is just impressive. I love his passion, his intent of the game, the way he coaches his players, that's what I like the most. He demands something out of his players. He's not just telling them the X's and O's. He's going to demand it out of you."

 As Fowler was lauding Durde, Seahawks players were heading out of the team's indoor practice facility after a walk-through. Williams, Lawrence and a few other defensive…

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 Left tackle Laremy Tunsil left practice after a one-on-one rep versus linebacker Odafe Oweh and was being evaluated for what appeared to be an upper-body injury. Oweh rushed to the inside, with his left hand at Tunsil's right shoulder.

 Corner Trey Amos also left practice early, returning to the building along with Tunsil. Amos returned to practice Friday after being activated off the physically unable to perform list. He fractured his fibula in Week 10 last season but also dealt with a soft-tissue injury in the spring.

 It's uncertain why Amos had to leave practice. He did participate in some full-team work before exiting, running downfield on a deep post to receiver Terry McLaurin on one play that resulted in pass interference. 

 Washington's players are off Sunday so coach Dan Quinn won't provide updates on the players until practice resumes Monday morning.

 Other observations:  

 
 Brandon Coleman and  Chris Paul  continue to rotate with the first group as they compete for the starting left guard position. Paul started 15 games at the position, taking over for Coleman. 
 Quinn said center Nick Allegretti (calf strain) and tight end John Bates (strained hamstring) will miss another week of practice. Both were injured on the first day of practice. Washington will practice three days next week, including a joint session with Miami on Wednesday before playing the Dolphins in the preseason opener Friday. 
 With Allegretti out, Washington signed two centers -- Trey Hill and Daniel Brunskill -- and guard Max Scharping . The Commanders were thin at center before his injury. Brunskill offers experience, having started 71 games in his seven-year career at guard, center and right tackle. The Commanders also signed tackle Nicholas Petit-Frere . 
 Undrafted rookie receiver  Jaden Bradley  made two nice catches Saturday. The first catch was on a nice throw from quarterback Marcus Mariota on an out route -- just over corner Fabian Moreau and Bradley made a leaping catch. Later, on a pass that might have been tipped at the line he had to stretch out to his left to make the grab. 
 Receiver Stefon Diggs was more active, catching several passes in full-team work. On one, the offense put the defensive backs in a bind -- the safety had to run with another target and the corner had to move up to cover someone on an out. That left Diggs in a soft spot for a long gain. 
 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 The Commanders not only introduced a new receiver in Stefon Diggs on Friday, they also welcomed back three key players.

 Corner Trey Amos and defensive end/linebacker Dorance Armstrong were activated off the physically unable to perform list while punter Tress Way was removed from the non-football illness list.

 Amos practiced in full Friday, taking reps with the first group -- he started the first 10 games last season before fracturing his right fibula. He also was dealing with a soft-tissue issue before camp, which is why general manager Adam Peters said they wanted to be "overly cautious."

 Armstrong tore his ACL in Week 7; he posted 5.5 sacks in his first six games. He will participate in individual drills and slowly work his way back into full-team work. He'll play outside linebacker in their base defense and can rush as an end in nickel situations.

 Way, Washington's longest-tenured player, suffered a pectoral injury in the offseason. He's coming off his third Pro Bowl season.

 More observations: 

 
 During a one-on-one drill, receiver Terry McLaurin showed his footwork and hands against corner Rasul Douglas . The play also highlighted Jayden Daniels ' accuracy and their chemistry. McLaurin appeared to be running a fade, but Daniels read the coverage and threw a back-shoulder -- McLaurin quickly adjusted his body and made the catch. However, there would have been strong debate about whether he got both feet in bounds. There might have been a centimeter. 
 Diggs dropped the one pass thrown his way in full-team work, a slant route. Diggs has been credited with two drops in his last 166 targets. 
 Undrafted free agent kicker Drew Stevens continues to have a consistent camp. He made all five of his field goal attempts while Jake Moody missed wide left on two of his -- both were wobbly balls. Moody missed three kicks in practice Wednesday compared to one for Stevens. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels has continued to grow more comfortable in their new offense -- and it's showing on the field. He had a strong day Tuesday and another solid one Wednesday.

 He wasn't alone, as backup Marcus Mariota also had a strong day, particularly in the red zone.

 Daniels showcased his dynamic ability in a red-zone drill. There was pressure inside, but he extended the play to his right and connected with receiver Jaylin Lane for a score. Later, in 7-on-7 work, Daniels hit wide receiver  Luke McCaffrey in the back of the end zone, despite good coverage by Mike Sainristil .

 Coaches have said Daniels' growing comfort level can be heard by how he's directing receivers at the line -- focusing on the details of their splits -- or in how he'll remind the center about the snap count as they approach the line.

 All of this is what running back Rachaad White expected when he reunited with Daniels, a teammate for two years at Arizona State.

 "Why I think he's the best quarterback I played with, it's the way he moves, the way he has poise," said White, who played with Tom Brady and Baker Mayfield in Tampa. "Not a lot of guys can do it as well. I've seen him come through in the clutch so many times for us and it was the same in his rookie year. When you've got a guy like that out there and he's so talented and the way he attacks the game, you'll be in every game."

 More observations: 

 
 Guard Sam Cosmi and tackle Laremy Tunsil both returned to practice after sitting out Tuesday. But two defensive players sat out today: linebacker K'Lavon Chaisson and corner Amik Robertson . Last season Washington gave a number of vets planned rest days in camp but they're not doing that this season. However, Quinn will give players recovery days when needed and the previous two practices had been two hours long and intense. 
 Linebacker Sonny Styles closed practice with a hard pop of running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt in a goal-line drill. The defensive players celebrated as if they had just saved a game. One day earlier, defensive lineman Javon Kinlaw said of Styles, "He's coming downhill and he's bringing thump with it. He ain't getting danced out of the hole. You love to see that; he ain't losing his ground on contact."
